retained_claims.statement:
Adopt the postulates [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] of the classical gravitational
framework, and let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and curvature
$R$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). All statements below
are deductions within the model so specified; they assert nothing about
nature.

At an event $q$, a **frame** means an ordered basis
$(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ of $T_qM$. If an orthonormal frame is intended, it means
a tetrad satisfying $g_q(E_A,E_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$;
these terms and their distinction from coordinate frames are defined in
[[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. Such a frame is pointwise basis
data, not a chart on an open set or an observer congruence, which is a smooth
future unit timelike vector field on an open set
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).

**(a) Free-fall congruences.** A **free-fall congruence** of the model is a
smooth map $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times I\to M$, with
$\varepsilon>0$ and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval with nonempty interior,
whose values we write $\gamma(r,s)$. For each
$r\in(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ the curve $\gamma_r:I\to M$ is defined by
$\gamma_r(s):=\gamma(r,s)$ and is a future timelike geodesic parametrized by
proper time, with tangent field $U_r(s):=\partial_s\gamma(r,s)$ satisfying
$$g(U_r,U_r)=-c^2,\qquad D_sU_r=0,$$
where $D_s$ is the covariant derivative along $\gamma_r$.
Here this term denotes a mathematical family of candidate free-fall histories.
Clause (ii) of [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] requires any ideal
freely falling massive test body's history to be such a geodesic on its
actual proper-time interval; it does not guarantee bodies realizing arbitrary
release data or an entire geodesic domain. If a smooth family of these body
histories is realized on a common interval $I$, it is a free-fall congruence
in the sense just defined. Conversely each individual such body history can
be included mathematically in a constant family $\gamma(r,s)=\gamma_0(s)$,
without asserting the existence of additional bodies. No injectivity or
immersion condition is imposed on the family map.

**(b) Deviation equation (model deduction).** Let $\gamma$ be a free-fall
congruence and set $J:=\partial_r\gamma$. Then, along each $\gamma_r$, the
separation field satisfies
$$D_s^2J=R(U_r,J)U_r,$$
where $D_s$ is the covariant derivative along $\gamma_r$. In particular, the
relative four-acceleration encoded by the family’s infinitesimal separation
field $J$ is exactly the curvature term: at each event,
$J\mapsto R(U_r,J)U_r$ is an $\mathbb R$-linear map on the event's tangent
space, vanishes at $J=0$, is tensorial and independent of the frame or chart
used for its components, and contains no rest mass, charge or
internal-structure parameter of the bodies. When the family is realized by
ideal test-body histories, this is their infinitesimal relative acceleration
within the adopted model.

**(c) Flat comparison and the vanishing criterion.** If the curvature
vanishes on an open subset $O\subseteq M$, then every free-fall congruence
with worldlines in $O$ has $D_s^2J=0$ there: the model predicts no tidal
relative acceleration of freely falling test bodies in that region.
Conversely, if at an event $q$ the operator $J\mapsto R(U,J)U$ vanishes for
every future timelike $U$ and every $J\in T_qM$, then $R_q=0$; hence within
the model the tidal response of all free-fall congruences detects exactly the
curvature when all mathematical candidate families of (a) are considered,
and $R$ is the model's complete tidal field at every event. Every normalized
future timelike $U$ and every separation value $J$ are realized by such a
local mathematical family. This does not assert the existence of test bodies
realizing those families; inference from only physically realized families
would additionally require that they supply all these directions and values.

**Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of the stated
postulates and the cited mathematics. No observation, apparatus, measured
input or statistical inference is used; the item contains no empirical
premises, and the word "tidal" denotes the curvature term in the model's
deviation equation, not a measured force on any particular body.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
## Conventions, units and scope

**Signs and index order.** The curvature operator, the component order and the
lowered, Ricci, scalar and Einstein contractions are fixed once in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] and used unchanged throughout
this page: $R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$ and
$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$, so that the
algebraic symmetries of [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] and the
divergence identity $\nabla^aG_{ab}=0$ of
[[thm-gr-second-bianchi-and-divergence-free-einstein]] hold in exactly the
displayed form. Sources that order the loop indices differently, or that use
the opposite overall sign, state the same mathematics in another convention;
no formula is imported from a source without converting it to this one.

**Units.** In length coordinates, in which $x^0=ct$ and all $x^a$ carry
metres and the metric components are dimensionless
([[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]), the Christoffel symbols
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have units of inverse length and the components
$R^a{}_{bcd}$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ and $S$ have units of
inverse length squared. The Einstein tensor has the same units as the Ricci
tensor, and the field-equation coupling of the framework is normalized so
that $\kappa T_{ab}$ has the same units; no numerical value of any constant
is asserted by these conventions. In other coordinates, such as charts with
an angular coordinate, individual component units change with the Jacobian
and carry no universal dimension; only invariant statements, proper times and
observer-relative quantities keep their physical reading.

**Connection artifacts versus curvature.** The Christoffel symbols are chart
functions and not tensor components; a chart can make all of them vanish at a
point ([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]) without
making the curvature vanish there:
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (c) shows
that curvature at a point is exactly the second-order metric information that
no coordinate choice can remove. Conversely a chart may have nonzero
Christoffel symbols everywhere while the curvature vanishes identically, as
for flat space in curvilinear coordinates. Curvature is also not a trace of
itself: $\operatorname{Ric}=0$ is a weaker condition than $R=0$, and the
converse implications are not asserted anywhere on this page.

**"Tidal" is a model term.** In [[pthm-gr-tidal-comparison]] the word tidal
refers to the curvature term $R(U,J)U$ in the deviation equation satisfied by
smooth free-fall congruences of the adopted model; the deduction shows that
this term is exactly the infinitesimal relative four-acceleration when ideal
test-body histories realize the mathematical family on a common interval.
Its vanishing for all timelike directions and all separation values at an
event is equivalent to the vanishing of curvature there. All these values
are attained by local mathematical candidate families, without guaranteeing
bodies realizing them. It does not assert
that any real body is freely falling, that any particular measured effect is
of this form, or that agreement of any such comparison would establish the
postulates; a comparison with data would require apparatus models, empirical
premises with uncertainties and statistical inference, none of which is part
of this page.

**Scope of the maximum and conjugacy results.** The exact maximum statement
is [[thm-gr-conjugacy-and-local-timelike-maximum]] clause (b). Its hypotheses
are a smooth future timelike geodesic $\gamma:[0,b]\to M$, $b>0$, with
$g(\gamma',\gamma')=-1$ and no conjugate instant in $(0,b]$ relative to $0$:
no nonzero smooth field $J$ along $\gamma$ satisfying
$D_s^2J=R(\gamma',J)\gamma'$ vanishes both at $0$ and at such an instant.
Fix a finite chart cover $(U_i,x_i)$ and a partition
$0=s_0<\cdots<s_m=b$ with $\gamma([s_{i-1},s_i])\subseteq U_i$.
The comparison curves $\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ are continuous piecewise-$C^1$
future timelike curves with the same endpoints. For some $\delta>0$, each
comparison curve must remain in the corresponding $U_i$ and satisfy
$\sup\|x_i\circ\alpha-x_i\circ\gamma\|<\delta$ and
$\sup\|(x_i\circ\alpha)'-(x_i\circ\gamma)'\|<\delta$ on every common
smooth partition piece, with Euclidean norms as in that clause. Only in
this comparison class is $L_g(\alpha)\le b=L_g(\gamma)$ asserted; equality
means a piecewise-$C^1$ strictly increasing reparametrization onto $[0,b]$.

The local inverse branches used in that theorem's proof steps 2.1-3.1 are
smooth maps $\psi_k:V_k\to D_k\subseteq T_pM$, $p=\gamma(0)$, inverse to
$\exp_p|_{D_k}:D_k\to V_k$, where $D_k,V_k$ are open and the restricted
exponential map is a diffeomorphism. A finite parameter subdivision puts
each radial subsegment $s\gamma'(0)$ in its corresponding $D_k$.
Compatibility means adjacent branches agree on a neighborhood of the
shared endpoint event and send that event to the same radial vector.
Branches at nonadjacent occurrences of a repeated event need not agree;
one injective exponential chart containing the whole segment is not assumed.
These are local assertions, not global maximality, existence of conjugate
instants, or a classification of where global maximality first fails.
Global causal, completeness and singularity statements are reserved for
later pages and are not prerequisites of the results here.

retained_claims.statement:
On $M=\mathbb R^4$ consider the identity chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, the
metric with components
$$g_{00}=-1,\qquad g_{11}=1+(x^0)^2,\qquad g_{22}=g_{33}=1,\qquad g_{ab}=0 \ \text{for }a\neq b,$$
and the time orientation $N:=\partial_0$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected
connection and $R$ its curvature
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Then:

1. The identity chart is point-normal at the origin: $g_{ab}(0)=\eta_{ab}$,
   $\partial_ag_{bc}(0)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(0)=0$; nevertheless the
   curvature does not vanish at the origin, since
   $R_{0101}(0)=R_{1010}(0)=-1$ and $R_{0110}(0)=1$.
2. The only nonzero Christoffel symbols of the metric-selected connection are
   $$\Gamma^1{}_{10}=\Gamma^1{}_{01}=\frac{x^0}{1+(x^0)^2},\qquad \Gamma^0{}_{11}=x^0 .$$
3. The deviation equation is verified exactly on the explicit family of
   geodesics $\Phi(s,r)=(s,r,0,0)$: with $T=\partial_s\Phi$ and
   $J=\partial_r\Phi$ one has $D_s^2J=R(T,J)T$ for every $s$, and the
   relative acceleration does not vanish at the event where all connection
   symbols of the chart vanish.

items.title: A flat metric with nowhere-zero Christoffel coefficients: flat space in cylindrical coordinates
items.statement:
On the open set $\Omega:=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:x^1>0\}$ with the identity chart
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ consider the metric
$$g:=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+(x^1)^2(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2,\qquad N:=\partial_0 ,$$
and let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection and $R$ its curvature
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Writing
$X:=x^1\cos x^2$ and $Y:=x^1\sin x^2$, the chain rule gives
$dX=\cos x^2\,dx^1-x^1\sin x^2\,dx^2$ and
$dY=\sin x^2\,dx^1+x^1\cos x^2\,dx^2$, hence
$dX^2+dY^2=(dx^1)^2+(x^1)^2(dx^2)^2$: the displayed metric is the flat metric
$-(dx^0)^2+dX^2+dY^2+(dx^3)^2$ pulled back by the map
$(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)\mapsto(x^0,X,Y,x^3)$. This map is a local diffeomorphism
on all of $\Omega$, so the metric is locally the flat Minkowski metric. It is
not globally injective because $x^2\in\mathbb R$ is an unwrapped angular
coordinate; on every restriction where $x^2$ ranges over an interval of
length less than $2\pi$, it gives genuine cylindrical coordinates. The
component verification below uses only the displayed metric.

1. The only nonzero Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart are
   $$\Gamma^1{}_{22}=-x^1,\qquad \Gamma^2{}_{12}=\Gamma^2{}_{21}=\frac{1}{x^1},$$
   so these three coefficients are nonzero at every point of $\Omega$,
   while all other Christoffel symbols vanish identically.
2. The curvature vanishes identically, $R=0$, even though the chart has
   nonvanishing Christoffel symbols everywhere.
3. Consequently $R(T,J)T=0$ for every geodesic tangent $T$ and every field
   $J$ along it: for every smooth family of affinely parametrized geodesics
   the deviation equation reads $D_s^2J=0$, with no tidal term.
items.strategy: Compute the Christoffel symbols of the flat metric in cylindrical coordinates and verify, by the coordinate formula and a finite case check, that the curvature vanishes identically although no connection coefficient does.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3: the Christoffel symbols of the plane in polar coordinates (3.22)-(3.25) with Gamma^r_{theta theta} = -r and Gamma^theta_{r theta} = 1/r, and the remark that connection coefficients vanish in Cartesian but not in curvilinear coordinates, printed pp. 60-61 (PDF pp. 67-68)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 3.4: the coordinate formula (3.39) for the Riemann tensor, printed pp. 130-131 (PDF pp. 137-138); section 3.3.2 on curvature as the obstruction to flattening coordinates

items.title: Curvature, Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors of a metric with a round two-sphere factor
items.statement:
Let $S^2:=\{(X,Y,Z)\in\mathbb R^3:X^2+Y^2+Z^2=1\}$ with the round metric
induced by the Euclidean inner product, and let $M:=\mathbb R^2\times S^2$
with the product Lorentzian metric whose first factor has line element
$-(dx^0)^2+(dx^3)^2$. Use the sphere chart
$\sigma:(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)\to S^2$ given by
$$\sigma(\theta,\varphi)=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta),$$
and put $U:=\mathbb R^2\times\sigma((0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi))\subset M$. In the
product chart with coordinate order
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(x^0,\theta,\varphi,x^3)$, the metric is
$$g:=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+\sin^2(x^1)\,(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2,\qquad N:=\partial_0 .$$
This chart contains the equatorial geodesic segment used in
[[ex-gr-conjugate-instant-on-a-round-sphere-factor]]; the underlying manifold
has an actual $S^2$ factor, not an unwrapped angular cover. The metric is
smooth and Lorentzian on $M$ with time orientation $N$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected
connection and $R$, $R_{abcd}$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ its curvature data
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Then:

1. The only nonzero Christoffel symbols in this chart are
   $$\Gamma^1{}_{22}=-\sin x^1\cos x^1,\qquad \Gamma^2{}_{12}=\Gamma^2{}_{21}=\cot x^1 .$$
2. The curvature has exactly one independent nonzero lowered component up
   to the algebraic symmetries, namely
   $$R_{1212}=\sin^2(x^1);$$ equivalently $R(\partial_1,\partial_2)\partial_2=\sin^2(x^1)\partial_1$ and $R(\partial_1,\partial_2)\partial_1=-\partial_2$, and every component containing an index $0$ or $3$ vanishes.
3. The Ricci tensor, scalar curvature and Einstein tensor are $$\operatorname{Ric}_{11}=1,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{22}=\sin^2(x^1),\qquad S=2,\qquad G=\operatorname{diag}(1,0,0,-1).$$
4. The contracted second Bianchi identity $\nabla^aG_{ab}=0$ holds. In the
   displayed chart $U$, $\nabla_eG_{ab}=0$ identically, so the divergence
   vanishes term by term there.
items.strategy: Compute the Christoffel symbols, curvature, Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors of the product of a round unit sphere with flat time and space directions, and verify the contracted second Bianchi identity on it.

references.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 3.3.2: the Christoffel symbols of the round sphere S^2 (3.19), the Riemann component R_{phi theta theta phi} = -r^2 sin^2 theta and the geodesic deviation of meridians (3.37)-(3.38), printed pp. 126-129 (PDF pp. 133-136)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3: the Ricci tensor (3.90), the Ricci scalar (3.92) and the Einstein tensor (3.95), printed pp. 81-82 (PDF pp. 88-89)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 4.6: the Ricci tensor (4.30), the Ricci scalar (4.31) and the Einstein tensor (4.32); section 4.7: the contracted Bianchi identity and the divergence-free property of the Einstein tensor, printed pp. 48-51 (PDF pp. 49-52)

items.title: Jacobi fields in flat space are affine, and no geodesic has conjugate instants
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the identity chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, the flat
Lorentzian metric $g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the time orientation
$N=\partial_0$; let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection and $R$ its
curvature ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). Then:

1. In the identity chart $\nabla$ is the coordinate connection, $\Gamma\equiv0$,
   and its geodesics are exactly the affine lines $t\mapsto p+tv$; moreover
   $\exp_p(v)=p+v$ and $d(\exp_p)_u=\operatorname{id}$ for every $u\in T_pM$.
2. $R=0$: every curvature component vanishes, although the identity chart is
   global.
3. Along the geodesic $\gamma(t)=p+tv$ the covariant derivative is the
   componentwise derivative in the identity chart, and the Jacobi fields along
   $\gamma$ are exactly the affine fields
   $$J(t)=J_0+tJ_1,\qquad J_0,J_1\in\mathbb R^4 ,$$
   with $D_tJ(0)=J_1$; the map $J\mapsto(J(0),D_tJ(0))$ from this space
   onto $T_pM\oplus T_pM$ is the initial-value isomorphism of
   [[thm-gr-jacobi-equation-and-geodesic-deviation]] clause (c), and its
   inverse sends $(J_0,J_1)$ to the field $t\mapsto J_0+tJ_1$.
4. No geodesic of this model has a conjugate instant: if
   $J(t_0)=J(t_1)=0$ for $t_0<t_1$, then $J=0$. Consistently
   $d(\exp_p)_u=\operatorname{id}$ is invertible for every $u\in T_pM$,
   because $\exp_p(v)=p+v$ is a translation.
5. For the flat congruence $F(t,r):=p+tv+rw$ with $p,v,w\in\mathbb R^4$,
   $v\neq0$, the variation field is the constant field $J=w$ and
   $D_t^2J=0=R(T,J)T$: the deviation equation holds with no curvature term,
   and the relative acceleration of the congruence vanishes identically.
items.strategy: Show that in flat space the covariant derivative is the componentwise derivative, that Jacobi fields along geodesics are exactly the affine fields J_0 + tJ_1, and that no geodesic has a conjugate instant.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3: the geodesic deviation equation (3.113) and its flat-space reading, printed pp. 86-88 (PDF pp. 93-95)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 4.5: the geodesic deviation equation (4.22)-(4.24) and the flatness criterion, printed pp. 46-48 (PDF pp. 47-49)

items.title: An equator geodesic of the round-sphere factor: conjugate instant at distance pi with multiplicity one
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^2\times S^2$ carry the product metric of
[[ex-gr-curvature-of-a-product-with-a-round-sphere]]. Use its local chart
$U$ with $0<\theta:=x^1<\pi$, $0<\varphi:=x^2<2\pi$ and coordinate order
$(x^0,\theta,\varphi,x^3)$; this chart contains the full geodesic segment
below. The metric has time orientation $N=\partial_0$, and its Christoffel
symbols and curvature are computed in
[[ex-gr-curvature-of-a-product-with-a-round-sphere]]. Let $\nabla$ be the
metric-selected connection. Define $\gamma:[0,\pi]\to M$ and fix
$$p:=(0,\tfrac{\pi}{2},\tfrac{\pi}{2},0),\qquad \gamma(s):=(0,\tfrac{\pi}{2},\tfrac{\pi}{2}+s,0),\qquad T:=\gamma'=\partial_2 .$$
Then:

1. $\gamma$ is a geodesic with affine parameter $s$ and unit spacelike
   tangent, $g(T,T)=\sin^2(\pi/2)=1$, and every Christoffel symbol of the
   chart vanishes along $\gamma$; hence the coordinate frame
   $\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3$ is parallel along $\gamma$.
2. The smooth field $J(s):=\sin(s)\,\partial_1|_{\gamma(s)}$ along $\gamma$ is
   a nonzero Jacobi field with $J(0)=J(\pi)=0$. Therefore $\pi$ is a
   conjugate instant of $\gamma$ relative to $0$
   ([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (d)), and the events
   $p=\gamma(0)$ and $\gamma(\pi)=(0,\tfrac{\pi}{2},\tfrac{3\pi}{2},0)$ are
   distinct conjugate points of $M$.
3. No $s_1\in(0,\pi)$ is a conjugate instant of $\gamma$ relative to $0$:
   the first conjugate instant is exactly $\pi$.
4. The conjugate instant $\pi$ has multiplicity $1$, and consistently
   $\ker d(\exp_p)_{\pi T(p)}$ is the one-dimensional subspace
   $\pi\,\mathbb R\,\partial_1|_p$ of $T_pM$
   ([[lem-gr-conjugacy-via-the-exponential-map]] clause (b)).
items.strategy: Verify that the equator geodesic of the round-sphere factor has the Jacobi field sin(s) partial_1, a first conjugate instant at s = pi of multiplicity one, and a one-dimensional kernel of d(exp_p) at pi v.

references.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 3.3.2: the equator geodesic of S^2, the Riemann component (3.38) and the geodesic deviation of neighbouring meridians, printed pp. 128-129 (PDF pp. 135-136)

E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), section 6.1: conjugate points, the matrix of Jacobi fields with A(0)=0, nabla A(0)=Id and the characterization by the exponential map (Proposition 6.3 and following), printed pp. 159-161 (PDF pp. 159-161)
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3: geodesic deviation and the failure of coordinates at conjugate points, printed pp. 86-88 (PDF pp. 93-95)

items.title: The exchange symmetries of a curvature-like tensor do not imply the first Bianchi identity
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold with a global chart and
let $T$ be a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor field on $M$ whose components satisfy, at
every point,
$$T_{abcd}=-T_{bacd},\qquad T_{abcd}=-T_{abdc},\qquad T_{abcd}=T_{cdab}$$
for all $a,b,c,d$ — the skew-symmetries and the exchange of the two index
pairs of [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(b). Then $T$
also satisfies the first Bianchi identity $T_{abcd}+T_{acdb}+T_{adbc}=0$ of
clause (c)."
items.strategy: Refute the implication from the skew and pair-exchange symmetries to the first Bianchi identity with the constant tensor T_abcd = omega_ab omega_cd, whose Bianchi sum at (0,1,2,3) equals 1.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3: the Riemann symmetries (3.78)-(3.83) and the counting of independent components, printed pp. 79-81 (PDF pp. 86-88)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 3.4: the symmetries and the first Bianchi identity R_{sigma[rho mu nu]} = 0, printed pp. 130-131 (PDF pp. 137-138)

items.title: A nonzero algebraic curvature tensor whose tidal operator vanishes for one timelike direction
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "Let $R_p$ be an algebraic curvature tensor at a point $p$
of a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, with the four identities
of [[lem-gr-algebraic-curvature-vanishing-criterion]], and suppose there is
**one** timelike vector $T\in T_pM$ such that the tidal operator
$J\mapsto R(T,J)T$ vanishes for every $J\in T_pM$. Then $R_p=0$."
items.strategy: Refute the one-observer vanishing criterion with the algebraic curvature tensor R_abcd = h_ac h_bd - h_ad h_bc built from the degenerate form h, whose tidal operator vanishes for partial_0 but not for the tilted timelike direction partial_0 + (1/2) partial_1.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3: the Riemann tensor symmetries (3.78)-(3.83) and the tidal reading of geodesic deviation (3.113), printed pp. 79-81 and 86-88 (PDF pp. 86-88 and 93-95)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 4.5: the geodesic deviation equation (4.22)-(4.24) and the flatness criterion that curvature is detected by all congruences, printed pp. 46-48 (PDF pp. 47-49)

items.title: The metric volume form, current flux through 3-faces and finite-chain charges
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $M$ carry an orientation in the
sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]] (so that its
charts that are oriented in that orientation have orientation-preserving
transition maps), and let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection. This item
fixes the metric volume form, the flux of a current through oriented $3$-faces
and finite-chain charges. The orientation of $M$ is an independent datum: it is
not determined by the metric and not by the time orientation.

**(a) Metric volume density and volume form.** Let $(U,x)$ be an oriented
chart, with metric components $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (a)). Define the **metric volume
density**

$$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}>0\qquad\text{on }U,$$

a strictly positive smooth function because $g_{ab}$ is smooth and
$g_p$ is nondegenerate. In the chart define the local $4$-form

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,U}:=w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3,$$

with the exterior product of [[def-wedge-product-of-differential-forms]] and the
coordinate covector fields of
[[prop-local-coordinate-expression-for-a-differential-form]]. That these local
forms agree on chart overlaps and therefore define one smooth nowhere-vanishing
$4$-form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ on $M$ — the **metric volume form** — is proved in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (a), together
with the reading statement of clause (b) there: in every oriented chart
$\mathrm{vol}_g=w\,dx^0\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^3$, and on every positively
oriented $g_p$-orthonormal basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $T_pM$ one has
$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=1$.

**(b) Current flux through oriented $3$-faces and chains.** Let $J$ be a
smooth vector field on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **current
$3$-form** of $J$ is the contraction

$$\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

the interior product of the $4$-form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ with $J$
([[def-interior-product-of-a-form-by-a-vector-field]]).

By a **smooth singular $k$-simplex** of $M$ — the convention of the library
definition `def-smooth-singular-simplex` (differential-geometry track),
restated here so this page is self-contained — we mean a map
$\sigma:\Delta^k\to M$ whose domain is the standard $k$-simplex
$$\Delta^k=\Bigl\{t\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:t_i\ge0,\ \textstyle\sum_it_i=1\Bigr\},$$
for which there exist an open set $O\subseteq A^k=\{t\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:\sum_it_i=1\}$
containing $\Delta^k$ and a smooth map $\bar\sigma:O\to M$ with
$\bar\sigma|_{\Delta^k}=\sigma$; the extension is not part of the simplex
data, and degenerate parametrizations are allowed. With the integration of
forms over such simplices
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]]), a **$3$-face** is
a smooth singular $3$-simplex $\sigma$, and the **flux of $J$ through
$\sigma$** is the real number

$$\Phi_J(\sigma):=\int_\sigma\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

A **finite smooth singular $k$-chain** — the convention of the library
definition `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes`, restated here —
is a finite formal real linear combination $\Sigma=\sum_i c_i\sigma_i$ of
smooth singular $k$-simplices. For such a $3$-chain the **flux of $J$ through
$\Sigma$** is defined additively,

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma):=\sum_i c_i\,\Phi_J(\sigma_i),$$

a definition independent of the written expression for $\Sigma$, because a
finite formal sum is evaluated by adding the finitely many coefficients and
inserting a zero coefficient changes nothing. $\Phi_J(\Sigma)$ is the **charge**
of the current $J$ assigned to $\Sigma$ when the model reads $J$ as a conserved
current; that reading belongs to the physical postulates and is not part of
this definition.

**(c) Non-null faces and their unit normals.** A $3$-dimensional linear subspace
$H\subseteq T_pM$ is **nondegenerate** for $g_p$ when the restriction of $g_p$
to $H$ is nondegenerate, equivalently when $H\cap H^\perp=\{0\}$ in the
orthogonality of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. A
smooth singular $3$-simplex $\sigma$ is **non-null at** a parameter point $t$
when the span of the three velocity vectors
$\sigma_*\partial_1|_t,\sigma_*\partial_2|_t,\sigma_*\partial_3|_t$ has
dimension $3$ and is nondegenerate at $\sigma(t)$, and **non-null** when this holds at every
parameter point. For a non-null face the **unit normal** $\nu$ at that point is
the unique vector of $T_{\sigma(t)}M$ with $\nu\in H^\perp$,
$g(\nu,\nu)\in\{-1,+1\}$ and $(\nu,\sigma_*\partial_1,\sigma_*\partial_2,
\sigma_*\partial_3)$ a positively oriented basis of $T_{\sigma(t)}M$; its
existence, uniqueness and its sign $\varepsilon:=g(\nu,\nu)$ are proved in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c), together
with the density identity of clause (c) used to read $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g$ on
such a face. Rank-deficient faces and rank-three faces with degenerate induced
metric are not assigned a unit normal; their flux is defined
by the $3$-form $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g$ itself, as in clause (b).

items.title: Chart independence of the metric volume form, its value on orthonormal frames, and the unit normal and density of a non-null hyperplane
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) whose underlying manifold carries an
orientation ([[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), and let
$w$ and the local forms $\mathrm{vol}_{g,U}$ be as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (a).

**(a) Chart independence.** Let $(U,x)$ and $(V,y)$ be oriented charts with
$x=\varphi\circ y$ on the overlap of their domains, where $\varphi$ is the
smooth transition map; write $g_{ab}$ and $g'_{ab}$ for the metric components
in the two charts and $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$,
$w'=\sqrt{|\det(g'_{ab})|}$. Then

$$\det(g'_{ab})=\bigl(\det D\varphi\bigr)^{2}\det\bigl(g_{ab}\circ\varphi\bigr),\qquad w'=\bigl(\det D\varphi\bigr)\,(w\circ\varphi),$$

and the local forms agree on the overlap,

$$\varphi^{*}\bigl(w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\bigr)=w'\,dy^0\wedge dy^1\wedge dy^2\wedge dy^3 .$$

Consequently there is a unique smooth nowhere-vanishing $4$-form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ on $M$ — the **metric volume form** — whose restriction to the
domain of every oriented chart $(U,x)$ is $w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge
dx^3$; it is a smooth section with nowhere-zero values and positive on the
given orientation.

**(b) Value on orthonormal frames.** For every $p\in M$ and every positively
oriented ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $T_pM$ with
$g_p(e_A,e_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$,

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=1 .$$

**(c) Non-null hyperplanes: normal and density.** Let $p\in M$, let
$H\subseteq T_pM$ be a $3$-dimensional subspace that is nondegenerate for
$g_p$, and let $v_1,v_2,v_3$ be an ordered basis of $H$. Then $H^{\perp}$ is
one-dimensional and nondegenerate and $H=(H^{\perp})^{\perp}$. Let
$u\in H^{\perp}\setminus\{0\}$ and write $\nu:=u/\sqrt{|g_p(u,u)|}$, so that
$\varepsilon:=g_p(\nu,\nu)\in\{-1,1\}$. If $\delta\in\{-1,1\}$ is the sign for
which $(\delta\nu,v_1,v_2,v_3)$ is a positively oriented basis of $T_pM$, then
$\nu^{*}:=\delta\nu$ is the **unit normal to $H$ adapted to the ordered basis**
$(v_1,v_2,v_3)$; it satisfies $g_p(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})=\varepsilon$,
$g_p(\nu^{*},h)=0$ for every $h\in H$, and it is the unique vector with these
two properties for which $(\nu^{*},v_1,v_2,v_3)$ is positively oriented.
Moreover

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(\nu^{*},v_1,v_2,v_3)=\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_p(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|}.$$

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 2 'the metric again': transformation of the metric components under a coordinate change, printed pp. 49-51 (PDF pp. 56-58); Ch. 2 'tensor densities' (2.44): the volume element as an n-form and the transformation of sqrt|det g|, printed pp. 52-54 (PDF pp. 59-61)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), sections 8.6-8.7: the volume element sqrt(-g) d^4x in a chart and its use with Stokes' theorem, printed pp. 108-110 (PDF pp. 109-111)

items.title: The derivative of the metric density and the chart formula for the divergence of a vector field
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, and define the local **metric density** by
$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$, using the matrix of metric components
in this chart. This definition requires no orientation or volume form. Write
$g^{ab}$ for the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}$ for the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in the chart.

**(a) Derivative of the density.** At every point of $U$,

$$\partial_a w=\tfrac12\,w\,g^{bc}\,\partial_a g_{bc}.$$

**(b) Trace of the Christoffel symbols.** At every point of $U$,

$$\Gamma^{b}{}_{ba}=w^{-1}\partial_a w .$$

**(c) Divergence formula.** For every smooth vector field $J$ on $M$, at every
point of $U$,

$$\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_aJ^a+\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}J^b=w^{-1}\partial_a\bigl(w\,J^a\bigr),$$

where $\nabla_aJ^a=g^{ab}\nabla_bJ_a$ is the divergence of $J$ contracted with
the metric and $J^a$ are the components of $J$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).

The identity of (c) is a chart formula for a chart-independent scalar: the
right-hand side is independent of the chart, as the left-hand side is.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 4: the variation of sqrt(-g), (4.62)-(4.65), printed pp. 116-117 (PDF pp. 123-124)
D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.1: the variation of sqrt(-g) from the determinant identity, printed pp. 140-142 (PDF pp. 147-149)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), sections 9.1-9.2 (variations of the volume factor), printed pp. 111-115 (PDF pp. 112-116), and section 8.6 (integration with sqrt(-g)), printed pp. 108-109 (PDF pp. 109-110)

items.title: Divergence, Stokes flux balance and the non-null face formula for a Lorentzian current
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with an
orientation, metric-selected connection $\nabla$, metric volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ and current flux $\Phi_J$ as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]], and let $J$ be a smooth vector
field on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Write
$\nabla_aJ^a$ for the divergence of $J$.

**(a) Exterior derivative of the current form.** As smooth $4$-forms on $M$,

$$d\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)=\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

**(b) Flux balance (Stokes).** For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$
of $M$ — a finite formal real sum of smooth singular $4$-simplices, the
library convention `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes` restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — and the flux
$\Phi_J$ of the induced boundary $3$-chain
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]],
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]]),

$$\Phi_J(\partial C)=\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently, if $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for smooth singular $3$-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)+\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

In particular, if $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $C$ then
$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)$, and if moreover
$\Phi_J(B)=0$ then $\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)=\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)$: equal charges need a
vanishing side flux, not merely a divergence-free current.

**(c) Non-null face formula.** Let $\sigma$ be a smooth singular $3$-simplex —
a map $\sigma:\Delta^3\to M$ admitting a smooth extension to a neighbourhood
of the standard $3$-simplex inside its affine plane, the convention restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — that is
non-null at a parameter point $t$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (c)), with
$v_i:=\sigma_*\partial_i|_t$ spanning the hyperplane $H$ and with the unit
normal $\nu^{*}$ adapted to the ordered basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ as in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c); write
$\varepsilon:=g_{\sigma(t)}(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})\in\{-1,1\}$. Then

$$\sigma^{*}\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)\big|_{t} =\varepsilon\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(J,\nu^{*}\bigr)\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_{\sigma(t)}(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|} .$$

Equivalently, the tangent vector $J$ is decomposed as
$J=\varepsilon g(J,\nu^{*})\nu^{*}+w'$ with $w'\in H$, and only the normal
component contributes to the flux through the face.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 8.7 'Submanifolds and Stokes' theorem': Stokes' theorem on an oriented manifold, printed pp. 109-110 (PDF pp. 110-111), with the divergence-theorem application in section 9.2, printed p. 115 (PDF p. 116)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.5 with figures 40-41: charge conservation in curved spacetime, the flux through B and Q(Sigma_2)=Q(Sigma_1) when no current flows out of the region, printed pp. 187-189 (PDF pp. 194-196)

items.title: Lorentzian metrics are stable under small compactly supported symmetric perturbations
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), so that at every $p\in M$ the form
$g_p$ has inertia $(3,1,0)$, and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) whose
support is compact.

**(a) Pointwise openness.** Let $V$ be a real vector space of dimension $4$
and let $G$ be a symmetric bilinear form on $V$ of inertia $(3,1,0)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]). If in some basis of $V$ the matrix of $G$
has the form $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)+E$, then $G$ has inertia $(3,1,0)$
whenever $|E_{ij}|<1/8$ for all $i,j$. Consequently, for every basis the set
of matrices of symmetric forms of inertia $(3,1,0)$ is open in the space
$M_4^{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)$ with respect to the maximum-entry norm, and
equivalently $g_p$ has a neighborhood in the space of symmetric forms at $p$
consisting entirely of forms of inertia $(3,1,0)$.

**(b) Global stability.** There is $\lambda_0>0$ such that for every real
$\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<\lambda_0$ the smooth symmetric field $g+\lambda h$
is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $M$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with
time orientation inherited from $N$ (the field $N$ remains timelike for
$g+\lambda h$ for $|\lambda|$ small).

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 2: the classification of quadratic forms and the canonical form of the metric at a point, printed pp. 48-51 (PDF pp. 55-58)
H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 2.1: the signature of a Lorentzian metric and the local normal form, printed pp. 25-28 (PDF pp. 26-29)

items.title: A continuous symmetric coefficient orthogonal to every compactly supported variation vanishes
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold, let $g$ be a smooth symmetric nondegenerate
covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), and let $(U,x)$ be any smooth
chart, with indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$. Write $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$,
let $(g^{ab})$ be the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$, and define the strictly
positive chart weight $w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$. These are local
matrix constructions; no signature, time orientation or orientation is assumed.
A continuous covariant tensor field means a family of bilinear forms whose
chart components are continuous; smooth means that they are $C^\infty$.
For a covector or vector field the same regularity convention applies to its
components in the coordinate dual basis or coordinate basis, respectively.
Let $F$ be a
continuous symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$. Suppose that for every
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $q$ on $M$ whose support is a
compact subset of $U$,

$$\int_U F_{ab}(x)\,q^{ab}(x)\,w(x)\,d^4x=0,$$

where $q^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}q_{cd}$ are the components of $q$ raised with the
inverse metric and the integral is the ordinary Riemann integral of the
continuous compactly supported function
$F_{ab}q^{ab}w$ in the chart coordinates
([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]). Then
$F=0$ on $U$. Moreover, if $W$ is a continuous covector field on $U$ with
$\int_UW_a(x)\,q^a(x)\,w(x)\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth vector field $q$ on $M$
whose support is a compact subset of $U$, then $W=0$ on $U$.

references.title: S. M. Chong and W. Kendall, 'the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations' argument: a continuous function orthogonal to every compactly supported smooth test function vanishes; see also the bump construction used by S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), the variation of the Einstein-Hilbert action (4.66)-(4.68): arbitrary variations force the coefficient to vanish, printed p. 117 (PDF p. 124)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), sections 9.2-9.3 (9.23)-(9.29): a compactly supported metric variation localized about any point and the resulting field equation, printed pp. 113-116 (PDF pp. 114-117)

items.title: The Hilbert stress-energy tensor of a metric-dependent action
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, let $\mathcal X$ be a set, and let

$$S:\mathcal D\longrightarrow\mathbb R$$

be a real-valued functional defined on a subset $\mathcal D$ of the set of
pairs $(\tilde g,\varphi)$ with $\tilde g$ a smooth Lorentzian metric on $M$ of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and $\varphi\in\mathcal X$. Fix $(\tilde g,\varphi)\in
\mathcal D$; below we always take $\tilde g=g$. The elements $\varphi$ are the
model's matter configurations; nothing about their nature is assumed here.
Assume that $\mathcal D$ admits every compactly supported metric direction at
$(g,\varphi)$: for each smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $h$ with
compact support, there is $\varepsilon_h>0$ such that
$(g+s h,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon_h$. Since
$\mathcal D$ contains only pairs whose metric is Lorentzian, these admitted
linear families are Lorentzian throughout that interval. This condition makes every compactly
supported inverse-metric variation available as well, since
$h\mapsto -g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$ is a bijection on compactly supported smooth
symmetric tensor fields.

**(a) Metric families.** A **smooth metric family at $g$ with compactly
supported variation** is a map $s\mapsto g_s$, $|s|<\varepsilon$ for some
$\varepsilon>0$, such that $(g_s,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for all $s$, such that
$g_s$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ for every $s$,
such that in every chart $(U,x)$ the component functions
$(s,x(p))\mapsto (g_s)_{ab}(p)$ are jointly $C^\infty$ on
$(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times x(U)$,
such that $g_0=g$, and such that there is a compact subset $K\subseteq M$ with
$g_s=g$ outside $K$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon$. For such a family define

$$q^{ab}:=\frac{d}{ds}g_s^{ab}\Big|_{s=0},$$

the derivative at $s=0$ of the components of the inverse metric of $g_s$ in any
smooth chart; the family of functions $q^{ab}$ is a smooth symmetric
contravariant $2$-tensor field of compact support, well defined because the
components $g_s^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $s$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Hilbert tensor.** A smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on
$M$ is a **Hilbert stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to
$c$** when, for **every** smooth metric family $s\mapsto g_s$ at $g$ with
compactly supported variation,

$$\frac{d}{ds}S(g_s,\varphi)\Big|_{s=0}=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{ab}\,q^{ab}\, \mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $\mathrm{vol}_g$ is the metric volume form of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] and $\int_M\omega$ is the
integral of the compactly supported smooth top form $\omega:=T_{ab}q^{ab}
\mathrm{vol}_g$ over the oriented manifold $M$
([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]).
The right-hand side is defined because $q^{ab}$ has compact support, so
$\omega$ is compactly supported. If such a $T$ exists it is unique, by
[[lem-gr-hilbert-tensor-uniqueness]]; one then calls it **the** Hilbert
stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$.

**(c) Conventions and scope.** The sign and the factor $1/(2c)$ are fixed
conventions of this library: they are the ones that turn the framework's
adopted Einstein-Hilbert normalization into the field equation displayed in the
framework's physical postulate. The condition is a property of the functional
$S$ at the point $(g,\varphi)$; it is not automatic, and this definition does
not assert that any functional has a Hilbert tensor. The definition uses the
orientation of $M$; a general functional $S$ has no orientation-reversal law,
so no transformation of $S$ or $T$ is asserted. When $S$ is given by
integrating $L(g,\varphi)\mathrm{vol}_g$ with an orientation-independent
scalar coefficient $L$ and the integral exists (or compact action differences
are used), define the reversed-orientation action by the same construction.
Reversing orientation replaces $\mathrm{vol}_g$ by $-\mathrm{vol}_g$ and
reverses the sign of integration of a fixed top form. These two signs cancel,
so both the action variation and the integral in the defining identity are
unchanged, as is its tensor $T$.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 4: the definition T_{mu nu} = -(1/sqrt(-g)) delta S_M/delta g^{mu nu}, (4.70), printed p. 116 (PDF p. 123), and the variation (4.69) of the total action

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 9.3: the definition T^{ab} = (2/sqrt(-g)) delta S_matter/delta g_{ab}, (9.28)-(9.29), printed p. 116 (PDF p. 117)
D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.2: T_{mu nu} = -(2/sqrt(-g)) delta S_M/delta g^{mu nu}, (4.46), printed p. 183 (PDF p. 190)

items.title: Uniqueness of the Hilbert stress-energy tensor
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold,
let $c>0$, let $S:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ and $\varphi$ be as in
[[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]; in particular, $\mathcal D$ admits
every compactly supported metric direction at $(g,\varphi)$. Suppose that $T$
and $T'$ are both Hilbert stress-energy tensors of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with
respect to $c$ relative to the metric volume form of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]. Then $T=T'$ on $M$; hence the
definite article in "the Hilbert stress-energy tensor" is justified.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 4: the energy-momentum tensor defined by the metric variation (4.70) and the statement that arbitrary variations determine the coefficient, printed pp. 116-118 (PDF pp. 123-125)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), sections 9.2-9.3: the variational derivative of the action determining the field equations and T^{ab} uniquely, (9.23)-(9.29), printed pp. 113-116 (PDF pp. 114-117)

items.title: First variation of the Einstein-Hilbert density under compactly supported metric variations, and of the timelike length functional
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$, curvature tensors
$R^{a}{}_{bcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, scalar curvature $S$ and Einstein
tensor $G_{ab}$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, let $K\subseteq U$ be compact, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an
open interval with $0\in I$, and let $s\mapsto g(s)$, $s\in I$, be a family of
smooth Lorentzian metrics of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ such that

- $g(0)=g$ and $g(s)=g$ on $M\setminus K$ for every $s\in I$; and
- the components $g(s)_{ab}$ in the chart are smooth functions of $(s,x)$ on
  $I\times x(U)$ ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

Write $h_{ab}:=\partial_sg(s)_{ab}|_{s=0}$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field with support in $K$, and
$q^{ab}:=\partial_sg(s)^{ab}|_{s=0}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Variation of the inverse metric; realizability.** $q^{ab}
=-g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$; conversely, for every smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h_0$ with compact support in $U$ there is $\lambda_0>0$ such
that for every $|\lambda|<\lambda_0$ the family $s\mapsto g+s\lambda h_0$
satisfies the hypotheses above on the parameter interval $(-1,1)$ (with
$K=\operatorname{supp}h_0$). In particular any prescribed smooth compactly
supported inverse-metric direction $q$ is realized by $g+s h$ on a
sufficiently small interval, with $h_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$.

**(b) Variation of the Christoffel symbols.** The field
$\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_s\Gamma(s)^{a}{}_{bc}|_{s=0}$ is a smooth
tensor field on $U$ and

$$\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}=\tfrac12g^{ad}\bigl(\nabla_bh_{cd}+\nabla_ch_{bd}-\nabla_dh_{bc}\bigr).$$

**(c) Variation of the Ricci tensor (Palatini identity).**
$\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\partial_s\operatorname{Ric}(s)_{bd}|_{s=0}$
satisfies

$$\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\nabla_a\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-\nabla_d\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}.$$

**(d) Variation of the curvature density.** With
$V^{a}:=g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^{d}{}_{db}$ and
$w(s):=\sqrt{|\det(g(s)_{ab})|}$ the metric density of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]],

$$\partial_s\bigl(w(s)S(s)\bigr)\big|_{s=0}=w\,G_{ab}q^{ab}+\partial_a\bigl(wV^{a}\bigr).$$

**(e) Variation of the chart action integral.** For every constant
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, the function
$F(s):=\int_U\bigl[(S(s)-2\Lambda)w(s)-(S(0)-2\Lambda)w(0)\bigr]\,d^4x$ is the compactly supported chart action difference, differentiable at $0$, and

$$F'(0)=\int_U\bigl(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}\bigr)q^{ab}\,w\,d^4x,$$

where the integrand is compactly supported in $K$ and the integral is an
ordinary Riemann integral in the chart coordinates
([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]).

**(f) Variation of the timelike length and particle action.** Let
$\gamma:[a,b]\to U$ and $H$ be as in
[[lem-gr-first-variation-of-proper-time]], so that $\gamma$ is $C^2$, future
timelike, parametrized with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-c^2$, the variation is $C^2$
with fixed endpoints and future timelike fibres, and $L(s)$ is the length
functional of that lemma. Then the first-variation formulas (1)-(3) of that
lemma hold verbatim. Consequently for every $m>0$ the particle action
$S_p(\gamma):=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))}\,dt$ satisfies
$\partial_sS_p(H(s,\cdot))|_{s=0}=-mc\,L'(0)$, so within this class of curves
and variations $\gamma$ is stationary for $S_p$ if and only if
$D_t\gamma'=0$, i.e. if and only if $\gamma$ is a geodesic in its proper-time
parameter ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

items.title: Killing fields of a Lorentzian metric
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field
on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **Lie
derivative of the metric along $\xi$**, written $\mathcal L_\xi g$, is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field obtained by the flow definition of
[[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]] applied to $g$: for the local flow
$\Phi_t$ of $\xi$,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g:=\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g .$$

The field $\xi$ is a **Killing field** of $(M,g)$ (an **isometry generator**,
or a **Killing vector**) when

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0 .$$

The equivalent local characterization

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0,$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and
$\xi_b:=g_{bc}\xi^c$ is the lowered field, is proved in
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a); the definition
itself asserts neither direction. Whether a given metric has Killing fields is
a property of that metric: neither existence nor uniqueness of a Killing field
is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field
$\xi=0$.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 5 'More Geometry': isometries and Killing vectors, L_X g_{mu nu}=0 and the equivalent form nabla_mu X_nu + nabla_nu X_mu = 0, (5.39)-(5.42), printed pp. 140-142 (PDF pp. 147-149)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 5.3 'Lie derivative': Killing vectors defined by L_X g_{ab}=0 and the conservation of X_a V^a along geodesics, printed pp. 53-56 (PDF pp. 54-57)

items.title: Killing fields and conserved currents, and on-shell conservation of the Hilbert stress-energy tensor
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]).

**(a) Characterization of Killing fields.** For every smooth vector field
$\xi$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), with
$\xi_b=g_{bc}\xi^c$ the lowered field,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0 .$$

**(b) Contraction along geodesics.** If $\xi$ is a Killing field and
$\gamma:I\to M$ is a geodesic with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its affine parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]), then $t\mapsto
g_{\gamma(t)}(\xi_{\gamma(t)},\gamma'(t))$ is constant on $I$.

**(c) Conserved current.** Let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $T$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $\xi$ be a Killing field on $U$. Then
$J^{a}:=T^{ab}\xi_b$ is a smooth vector field on $U$ with
$\nabla_aJ^a=0$; consequently the flux balance of
[[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] clause (b) applies to $J$
on every smooth singular $4$-chain contained in $U$.

**(d) On-shell conservation of the Hilbert tensor.** Let $c>0$, let
$S:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be a model action with Hilbert stress-energy tensor
$T$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]). For the flow diffeomorphisms $F$
below, suppose the configuration set $\mathcal X$ carries specified maps
$P_F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$ with $P_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$; write
$F^*\varphi:=P_F(\varphi)$. For geometric matter fields these are the
model's pullbacks; no pullback operation on an arbitrary set is implicit.
For **every** smooth compactly supported vector field $\xi$, its flow
$\Phi_v$ is global
([[def-complete-vector-field]], [[def-local-and-global-flow]]); this holds for
every compactly supported smooth field, using the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] through
[[thm-compactly-supported-vector-fields-are-complete]]. Write
$G(u,v):=S(\Phi_v^*g,\Phi_u^*\varphi)$ for the simultaneous pullback by the
flow (this presupposes that the pairs lie in $\mathcal D$, which is part of the
hypotheses below). Suppose (H1)–(H4) hold for **every** such $\xi$ (with
its own $G$ and parameter neighborhood):

- **(H1)** the map $G$ is defined on a neighborhood of $(0,0)$ in
  $\mathbb R^2$ and is differentiable at $(0,0)$;
- **(H2)** $\partial_uG(0,0)=0$ (the matter configuration $\varphi$ satisfies
  its model equations in this direction);
- **(H3)** $\partial_vG(0,0)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_MT_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$,
  where $q^{ab}:=\partial_v(\Phi_v^*g)^{ab}|_{v=0}$ (the metric variation is
  represented by the Hilbert tensor);
- **(H4)** $G(s,s)=S(g,\varphi)$ whenever $(s,s)$ lies in that neighborhood
  (invariance of the action under simultaneous pullback by the flow).

Then $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $M$.

H. S.
