H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision): the Ricci identity and the Bianchi identities, sections 4.2-4.6 printed pp. 41-49 (PDF pp. 42-50)

E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: the Riccati equation (6.4) for the Weingarten map of a hypersurface-orthogonal congruence, derived from the curvature commutator, section 6.2 printed pp. 161-163

items.title: The Raychaudhuri equation for a geodesic congruence and finite-time focusing
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$U\subseteq M$ be open and let $n$ be a smooth future unit timelike geodesic
congruence on $U$ with kinematic quantities $B$, $\theta$, $\sigma$, $\omega$
and rest-space metric $h$
([[def-gr-geodesic-congruence-and-kinematics]]). Let $q\in U$ and let
$\gamma_q:I_q\to U$ be the observer curve through $q$ with affine parameter
$s$, $s\in I_q$ ([[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]]).

**(a) Raychaudhuri equation.** For every $s\in I_q$,
$$\frac{d}{ds}\theta(\gamma_q(s)) =-\tfrac13\theta(\gamma_q(s))^2-\sigma_{ab}\sigma^{ab}(\gamma_q(s)) +\omega_{ab}\omega^{ab}(\gamma_q(s))-\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(\gamma_q(s))\,n^a(\gamma_q(s))\,n^b(\gamma_q(s)),$$
where all contractions use $g$ and $\operatorname{Ric}$ is the Ricci tensor
of the metric-selected connection
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]).

**(b) Focusing.** Suppose $\omega=0$ and
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}n^an^b\ge0$ on $U$, and suppose there is
$s_0\in I_q$ with $\theta_0:=\theta(\gamma_q(s_0))<0$. Then
$\theta(\gamma_q(s))<0$ for every $s\in I_q$ with $s>s_0$, and
$$\frac{1}{-\theta(\gamma_q(s))}\le\frac{1}{-\theta_0}-\frac{s-s_0}{3}.$$
Consequently $s<s_0+3/(-\theta_0)$ for every such $s$, so
$\sup I_q\le s_0+3/(-\theta_0)$ for the maximal integral curve in $U$.
Any continuation beyond this bound that remains a smooth geodesic congruence
and continues to satisfy $\omega=0$ and $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}n^an^b\ge0$
along the continued flow line is impossible. A continuation outside $U$ that
does not preserve these hypotheses is not ruled out by this result.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: the Weingarten map, its Riccati equation (6.4), the Raychaudhuri equation (6.5) with the shear evolution (6.6) and the focusing arguments, section 6.2 printed pp. 161-164
H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision): the geodesic deviation equation, section 4.5 printed pp. 46-48 (PDF pp. 47-49)
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997): the energy-momentum tensor and the weak energy condition (4.72), printed p. 117 (PDF p. 124)

items.title: Convergent causal ends are extendible, maximal geodesics have no limit, and Cauchy sets are acausal
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous endpoint argument in this clause. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Definition 2.16 and Lemma 2.17 relating inextendibility to unbounded h-arclength domains, printed pp. 33-34; limit curve theorems, section 2.11 printed pp. 45-49
H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision): the geodesic initial value problem and normal coordinates, sections 3.3-3.4 printed pp. 37-40 (PDF pp. 38-41)

items.title: A chart with constant metric components has vanishing metric-selected Christoffel symbols and curvature
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$(U,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ in which every metric component
$g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$ is a constant function on $U$. Then:

**(a)** Every Christoffel symbol of $\nabla$ in the chart vanishes
identically on $U$,
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=0$ ([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b)** The curvature tensor of $\nabla$ vanishes identically on $U$,
$R=0$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]).

**(c)** Every coordinate curve of the chart is a geodesic of $\nabla$; that
is, for fixed constants $c^1,c^2,c^3$ the curve $s\mapsto
x^{-1}(s,c^1,c^2,c^3)$ is a geodesic in the affine parameter $s$
([[prop-coordinate-geodesic-equation]]).

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997): the Christoffel formula (3.21)-(3.23) in terms of the metric and its first derivatives, printed pp. 60-61 (PDF pp. 67-68), under which constant metric components give vanishing Christoffel symbols

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision): the Christoffel formula (3.31)-(3.33) and the Riemann tensor in terms of the connection, section 4.3 printed pp. 36-37 and 43-45 (PDF pp. 37-38 and 44-46)

E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007): local existence of normal coordinates around any point, with the metric equal to diag(-1,1,1,1) and vanishing connection coefficients at the point, section 2.2.2 printed pp. 31-33

items.title: The flat model: Minkowski space R^4, its standard Lorentz form, inertial charts and cone sets
items.statement:
**(a) The underlying manifold.** Let $M:=\mathbb R^4$ be Euclidean four-space
as a set and real vector space ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), equipped
with its standard smooth structure, in which the identity map
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3):M\to\mathbb R^4$ is a global smooth chart
([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[prop-open-subsets-of-euclidean-space-have-the-standard-smooth-structure]]).
The coordinate vector fields $\partial_a:=\partial/\partial x^a$,
$a=0,1,2,3$, are smooth vector fields on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), and at every
$p\in M$ the tuple
$(\partial_0|_p,\partial_1|_p,\partial_2|_p,\partial_3|_p)$ is a basis of
$T_pM$ ([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(b) The metric.** The **flat metric** $\eta$ is the smooth covariant
$2$-tensor field on $M$ whose components in the chart $x$ are the constant
functions $\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), that is
$$\eta=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2 .$$
It is symmetric, and at every $p$ its matrix in the basis of (a) is
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$: diagonal, with one negative and three positive
entries and no zero entry. Hence $\eta_p$ is nondegenerate with inertia
$(3,1,0)$, that is, a Lorentz form on $T_pM$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), and $(M,\eta)$ is a smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The restriction of $\eta_p$ to
$\operatorname{span}(\partial_1|_p,\partial_2|_p,\partial_3|_p)$ is positive
definite.

**(c) Time orientation.** The field $N:=\partial_0$ satisfies
$\eta(N,N)=-1<0$ pointwise, so $N$ is a time orientation of $(M,\eta)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c)). The triple $(M,\eta,N)$ is
the **flat model**. At every $p$ the pointwise vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]] applies, and a nonzero causal
$v\in T_pM$ is future-directed exactly when $\eta_p(v,N_p)<0$
([[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]).

**(d) Events, displacements and straight paths.** The points of $M$ are the
**events** of the model. Since $M=\mathbb R^4$ is a vector space, for events
$p,q\in M$ the **displacement** from $p$ to $q$ is the vector $q-p\in M$, and
the **straight path** from $p$ to $q$ is the curve $s\mapsto p+s(q-p)$ on
$[0,1]$, whose chart representative has the constant velocity $q-p$. For
$v\in\mathbb R^4$ the **translation** is the map $\tau_v(p):=p+v$ of $M$.

**(e) Inertial charts and frames.** A chart of $M$ with domain $M$ is called a
**global chart**. A global chart $y=(y^0,y^1,y^2,y^3):M\to\mathbb R^4$ is
**inertial** when its components of $\eta$ are the constant functions
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ on $M$ and its first coordinate vector field
$\partial/\partial y^0$ is future-directed at every point. The chart $x$ of (a)
is inertial: its components of $\eta$ are $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ by
(b), and its first coordinate vector field is $N$, future-directed by (c). If
$y$ is inertial and $o\in M$, the tuple
$(o;\partial/\partial y^0|_o,\partial/\partial y^1|_o,
\partial/\partial y^2|_o,\partial/\partial y^3|_o)$ is an **inertial frame**
at $o$; its vectors satisfy
$\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ and $e_0$ is
future-directed.

**(f) Cone sets.** Let a vector $v\in T_pM$ have coordinates
$(v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3)$ in an inertial chart, write $v_s:=(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ and
$|v_s|:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Write
$$C^+:=\{v\in\mathbb R^4:v^0>|v_s|\}$$
and $\overline{C^+}:=\{v\in\mathbb R^4:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$ for the coordinate cone
sets. In every inertial chart and at every event $p$,
the future cone $C_p^+$ of (c) consists of exactly those $v$ with
$v^0>|v_s|$, its closure of exactly those with $v^0\ge|v_s|$, and the
future-directed causal vectors of $T_pM$ are exactly the nonzero vectors with
$v^0\ge|v_s|$; moreover the future cone is closed under sums. All of this is
proved in [[lem-gr-flat-inertial-cone-criterion-and-sums]], where the
independence of the inertial chart is also established.

**(g) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition; it asserts nothing about
nature. The physical reading of the flat model is recorded with the framework
postulates of this library and is not part of this definition, and the flat
examples and counterexamples of this page are conditional statements inside
the model.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Minkowski spacetime as the basic model (section 1.1 printed pp. 3-6) and its chronological and causal relations in coordinates (section 1.11 printed pp. 15-16)
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997): light cones and the timelike/null/spacelike classification, printed p. 7 (PDF p. 14)
H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision): the Minkowski metric eta_{mu nu} on R^4, section 2.1 printed p. 25 (PDF p. 26)

items.title: The causal cones of the flat model in inertial coordinates, and closure of the future cone under sums
items.statement:
Let $(M,\eta,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], let $y$ be an inertial
chart, let $p\in M$, and let $v\in T_pM$ have coordinates
$v=v^0\partial_0+\dots+v^3\partial_3$ in the chart
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]). Write
$v_s:=(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ and $|v_s|:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then:

**(a)** For every nonzero $v\in T_pM$: $v$ is future timelike iff
$v^0>|v_s|$, and past timelike iff $v^0<-|v_s|$; $v$ is future null iff
$0<v^0=|v_s|$, and past null iff $0<-v^0=|v_s|$; $v$ is future causal iff
$v^0\ge|v_s|$, past causal iff $v^0\le-|v_s|$, and causal iff
$|v^0|\ge|v_s|$; and every nonzero future causal $v$ satisfies $v^0>0$.

**(b)** $C_p^+=\{v\in T_pM:v^0>|v_s|\}$ and
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)=\{v\in T_pM:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$; the future-directed
causal vectors are exactly $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}
=\{v\neq0:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$.

**(c)** If $v,w\in T_pM$ are future causal, then $v+w$ is future causal; if
one of $v,w$ is future timelike and the other is future causal, then $v+w$ is
future timelike. Equivalently
$C_p^++\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\subseteq C_p^+$ and
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)+\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)
\subseteq\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)$.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: the chronological and causal relations of Minkowski spacetime in coordinates, section 1.11 printed pp. 15-16
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997): light cones and the timelike/null/spacelike classification, printed p. 7 (PDF p. 14)

items.title: Monotonicity of inertial time and the Lipschitz graph property for causal curves in the flat model
items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,\eta,N)$ be the
flat model of [[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], with its
global inertial chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, written $x=(x^0,z)$ with
$z\in\mathbb R^3$ (clauses (a), (b) and (e) of that definition), and let
$\gamma:I\to M$ be a future causal curve in the class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** $x^0\circ\gamma:I\to\mathbb R$ is strictly increasing.

**(b)** For all $a<b$ in $I$,
$$\bigl|z(\gamma(b))-z(\gamma(a))\bigr|\le x^0(\gamma(b))-x^0(\gamma(a)),$$
and consequently $\gamma$ is injective and its image is a $1$-Lipschitz graph
over the interval $(x^0\circ\gamma)(I)$.

**(c)** If $\gamma$ is future-inextendible then
$\sup\,(x^0\circ\gamma)(I)=+\infty$; if $\gamma$ is past-inextendible then
$\inf\,(x^0\circ\gamma)(I)=-\infty$. Hence if $\gamma$ is inextendible then
$x^0\circ\gamma$ is a strictly increasing surjection onto $\mathbb R$, and
for every $c\in\mathbb R$ the parameter set
$\{t\in I:x^0(\gamma(t))=c\}$ is a singleton.

**(d)** The coordinate function $u:=x^0$ is a temporal function of the flat
model in the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]]
clause (e): its gradient is the vector field $\nabla u=-\partial_0$ on all of
$M$, with $\eta(\nabla u,\nabla u)=-1<0$ and $du(\partial_0)=1>0$
everywhere.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Minkowski spacetime as the basic model (section 1.1 printed pp. 3-6); non-decreasing functions along the causal relation (section 1.12 printed pp. 17-18) and the locally Lipschitz parametrization of continuous causal curves (section 2.5 printed pp. 32-33)
E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007): the Lorentzian metric framework and time orientation, section 2.2 printed pp. 15-19
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997): light cones and the timelike/null/spacelike classification, printed p. 7 (PDF p. 14)

items.title: The flat model is globally hyperbolic and its inertial level sets are Cauchy hypersurfaces
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous causal-curve
conclusions used here.

Let $(M,\eta,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], with its global inertial
chart $x=(x^0,z)$, its cone sets $C^+,\overline{C^+}$ of clause (f) and its
translation action of clause (d), and with the causal relations of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** For every $p\in M$, $J^+(p)=p+\overline{C^+}$ and
$I^+(p)=p+C^+$, where the sum is the translation of clause (d), the cone sets
are those of clause (f), and the displacement is read in the vector space
$M=\mathbb R^4$; in the chart,
$$q\in J^+(p)\Longleftrightarrow x^0(q)-x^0(p)\ge|z(q)-z(p)|_{\mathrm e}.$$

**(b)** For every $c\in\mathbb R$ the level set
$\Sigma_c:=x^{-1}(\{c\}\times\mathbb R^3)$ is a spacelike embedded hypersurface of $M$, and
every inextendible causal curve of $M$ meets $\Sigma_c$ in exactly one
parameter value; equivalently, $\Sigma_c$ is a Cauchy hypersurface in the
sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c).

**(c)** For all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond $J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is
compact.

**(d)** The model is strongly causal in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (b); hence it is
globally hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Definition 4.117 and Theorem 4.119 (global hyperbolicity, Cauchy hypersurfaces and the R x S splitting) printed pp. 146-147; Minkowski spacetime as the basic model, section 1.1 printed pp. 3-6
E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007): globally hyperbolic spacetimes and Cauchy surfaces, section 3.2.1 printed pp. 39-40

items.title: Quotients of Lorentzian manifolds by free proper isometric discrete actions
items.statement:
Let $(\hat M,\hat g)$ be a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), let $\Gamma$ be a discrete
group equipped with its discrete smooth structure (a zero-dimensional Lie
group, so that a **smooth action** is one for which every map
$p\mapsto\gamma\cdot p$, $\gamma\in\Gamma$, is smooth), and let $\Gamma$ act
on $\hat M$ smoothly, freely and properly in the sense of
[[def-free-and-proper-lie-group-actions]]; write $\gamma\cdot p$ for the
action and $d\gamma_p$ for the differential of $p\mapsto\gamma\cdot p$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]). Suppose that every $\gamma\in\Gamma$
**preserves $\hat g$**, that is
$$\hat g_{\gamma\cdot p}\bigl(d\gamma_p V,d\gamma_p W\bigr)=\hat g_p(V,W)$$
for all $p\in\hat M$, $V,W\in T_p\hat M$ and $\gamma\in\Gamma$. Let
$q:\hat M\to M:=\hat M/\Gamma$ be the orbit map. Then:

**(a)** $M$ is a Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold, $q$ is a
smooth surjective submersion, and $q$ is a local diffeomorphism at every
point of $\hat M$.

**(b)** There is a unique smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ with $q^*g=\hat g$; equivalently
$g_{q(p)}(dq_pV,dq_pW)=\hat g_p(V,W)$ for all $p,V,W$.

**(c)** If $\hat N$ is a smooth vector field on $\hat M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) which is
$\Gamma$-invariant, $\hat N_{\gamma\cdot p}=d\gamma_p(\hat N_p)$, and
satisfies $\hat g(\hat N,\hat N)<0$, then the prescription
$N_{q(p)}:=dq_p(\hat N_p)$ defines a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$ with
$g(N,N)<0$ for all points. In particular, a $\Gamma$-invariant time
orientation of $(\hat M,\hat g)$ descends to one of $(M,g)$.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.: quotients by free proper actions, Proposition 21.4 and Theorem 21.10, printed pp. 543-547

E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: closed timelike curves, vicious spacetimes and the causal ladder, Proposition 4.18 and Definition 4.19 printed p. 113; sections 4.2 printed pp. 111-118

items.title: The flat cylinder model: closed timelike curves, total viciousness and no Cauchy set
items.statement:
Let $A:=\mathbb R^4$ carry the flat structure $(\eta,N)$ of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], with global inertial
chart $x=(x^0,z)$ and translations $\tau_\lambda(p)=p+\lambda$ of clause (d),
and write $e_0:=(1,0,0,0)\in A$. Fix $L>0$, let
$\Lambda:=\{nLe_0:n\in\mathbb Z\}\subseteq A$ act on $A$ by the translations
$\tau_\lambda(p)=p+\lambda$ and fix $o\in A$
(the action of the discrete group $\mathbb Z$, equipped with its discrete
smooth structure, is a special case of the actions of
[[def-free-and-proper-lie-group-actions]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be the quotient
time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold produced by
[[lem-gr-quotient-by-isometric-free-proper-action]], with orbit map
$q:A\to M$. Then:

**(a)** $q$ is a local isometry: $g_{q(p)}(dq_pV,dq_pW)=\eta_p(V,W)$ for all
$p\in A$ and $V,W\in T_pA$; and $(M,g)$ is flat, in the sense that every
point has a chart in which the metric components are the constants
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the curvature tensor of the
metric-selected connection vanishes identically.

**(b)** The curve $\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$, $\gamma(s):=q(o+se_0)$, is a
nonconstant smooth future timelike curve with $\gamma(s+L)=\gamma(s)$ for
all $s$; hence $(M,g,N)$ is neither chronological nor causal, and it
possesses a closed future timelike curve.

**(c)** Every two points $p,q\in M$ (equal or distinct) satisfy $p\ll q$:
the model is totally vicious. Consequently no subset of $M$ with two
distinct points is achronal or acausal.

**(d)** $M$ admits no Cauchy set and hence no Cauchy hypersurface in the
sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]].

items.title: The open flat slab: an incomplete timelike geodesic, a Cauchy slice and global hyperbolicity
items.statement:
For the general causal-curve conclusions (c) and (d), assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) as required by the absolutely continuous flat-curve calculus. The geometric restriction and explicit incomplete geodesic in (a)-(b) use no choice premise.

Let $A:=\mathbb R^4$ carry the flat structure $(\eta,N)$ of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], with global inertial
chart $x=(x^0,z)=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, and write $e_0:=(1,0,0,0)\in A$. Put
$$M:=x^{-1}\bigl((0,1)\times\mathbb R^3\bigr)=\{p\in A:0<x^0(p)<1\},$$
an open subset of $A$, and let $g:=\eta|_M$ and $N:=\partial_0|_M$ be the
restrictions of the metric and of the time-orientation field; write $x$ also for
the restricted chart $x|_M:M\to(0,1)\times\mathbb R^3$. Then:

**(a) The slab model.** $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) whose restricted chart
$x$ has the constant components
$g_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$; the Christoffel symbols of the
metric-selected connection vanish on $M$, the curvature of that connection
vanishes on $M$, and every coordinate curve of the chart is a geodesic
([[lem-gr-constant-component-chart-flatness]]). Every curve in $M$ is locally
absolutely continuous, future causal or future timelike for $(M,g)$ exactly
when it is so for $(A,\eta)$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]).

**(b) An incomplete timelike geodesic.** Fix $z_0\in\mathbb R^3$ and let
$$\gamma:(0,1)\to M,\qquad \gamma(s):=x^{-1}(s,z_0),$$
be the vertical line through $z_0$. Then $\gamma$ is a smooth future timelike
curve and a geodesic with affine parameter $s$ and unit tangent
$\gamma'(s)=\partial_0|_{\gamma(s)}$; its velocity satisfies
$\nabla_{\gamma'}\gamma'=0$. There is no geodesic
$\tilde\gamma:(a,b)\to M$ with $b>1$ (or $a<0$) whose restriction to $(0,1)$
equals $\gamma$: the parameter interval $(0,1)$ is the maximal domain of a
geodesic with these data. Moreover $\gamma$ does not converge to any point of
$M$ as $s\to1$ (it converges in $A$ to the boundary point $x^{-1}(1,z_0)$,
which does not lie in $M$); hence $\gamma$ is future-inextendible in the
sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d) and its affine
parameter is bounded above. The model is therefore timelike geodesically
**incomplete**: it carries an inextendible future-directed timelike geodesic
whose affine parameter domain is bounded.

**(c) A Cauchy slice.** The set
$\Sigma_{1/2}:=x^{-1}(\{1/2\}\times\mathbb R^3)$ is a spacelike embedded
hypersurface of $(M,g)$ and a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clauses (a) and (c)):
every inextendible causal curve of $(M,g)$ meets it in exactly one parameter
value. Hence $\Sigma_{1/2}$ is a Cauchy hypersurface.

**(d) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal and its causal
diamonds $J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$, $p,q\in M$, are compact; hence it is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c).

E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007): Cauchy surfaces and global hyperbolicity, section 3.2.1 printed p. 39

items.title: Scope and status of the causal and initial-value material: model conditions, predictions and deferred theorems
items.statement:
This note fixes the scope of the page's causal and initial-value content and
the status of its claims; it proves nothing by itself.

- **Model conditions versus physical readings.** Chronology, causality, strong
  causality, global hyperbolicity, achronality, acausality, the Cauchy-set
  property and the existence of time or temporal functions are mathematical
  conditions on a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
  ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]],
  [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]],
  [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]). The reading of the
  causal future and past as the model's signalling structure, and of the
  absence of closed causal curves or of a Cauchy set as a failure of
  predictability for the classical model, is adopted in the framework
  postulates ([[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]]); it is not proved
  and not observationally established by the mathematics of this page. A
  model with a closed timelike curve is not "mathematically inconsistent": it
  is a model whose causal structure differs from that of the flat models of
  the examples page.

- **What is proved here.** Conditional deductions inside the stated classes
  of curves and models: the curve calculus of
  [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]], the implication from temporal functions
  to time functions and the exclusion of closed causal curves by a time
  function ([[lem-gr-temporal-functions-and-time-functions]]), the
  extendibility of convergent causal ends and the acausality of Cauchy sets
  ([[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]]), the Minkowski model's global
  hyperbolicity and its inertial Cauchy hypersurfaces
  ([[thm-gr-minkowski-cauchy-and-global-hyperbolicity]]), the flat cylinder's
  failure of chronology, causality and the Cauchy property
  ([[thm-gr-flat-cylinder-closed-timelike-and-no-cauchy-set]]), the open
  slab's incompleteness together with its Cauchy slice and global
  hyperbolicity ([[thm-gr-flat-slab-incomplete-geodesic-and-cauchy-slice]]),
  and the local focusing bound along a geodesic congruence
  ([[thm-gr-timelike-raychaudhuri-and-local-focusing]]). Each is a statement
  about the explicitly displayed model and its curve class.

- **Initial value material.** [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]
  defines initial data $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ and the constraint equations as
  the normal and normal-tangential projections of the field equation;
  [[lem-gr-constraint-projections]] proves that data induced by a solution of
  the field equation ([[post-gr-einstein-field-law]]) satisfy the
  constraints, and the normal, induced metric and second fundamental form are
  constructed in
  [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]. The
  page does not assert the converse in any form: the existence of a
  development of given data, its uniqueness, the maximal globally hyperbolic
  development, and the equivalence of global hyperbolicity with the existence
  of a Cauchy hypersurface or of a smooth temporal function with Cauchy
  levels are not proved here. Those statements require the local
  Einstein-matter well-posedness theory, the Gauss-Codazzi relations and
  global causal gluing arguments, and are deferred to the later pages of this
  track (the convex-normal-neighborhood and full symmetric-hyperbolic
  pages). The equivalent component form of the constraints in terms of the
  induced scalar curvature and the divergence of $K$ is deferred with them.

- **Focusing versus singularities.** The Raychaudhuri theorem of this page is
  a local differential inequality along one flow line of a smooth geodesic
  congruence: it bounds the affine parameter range on which the congruence
  remains smooth under the stated hypotheses. It does not assert that the
  spacetime ends, that a singularity theorem holds, or that an
  infinite-curvature point forms. A genuine singularity theorem requires its
  own energy, causality and global compactness hypotheses and a complete
  proof, none of which is claimed here; cosmic censorship and chronology
  protection are not theorems and are not used.

- **Empirical status.** The page contains no experiment, no apparatus, no
  measured input, no sampling model and no statistical inference, and it
  draws no conclusion about nature. A prediction computed from a fully
  specified model may later be compared with reported observations; such a
  comparison tests the combined model and its auxiliary assumptions, and
  agreement is evidence, not a proof of the model or of its postulates.

- **Deferred obligations.** The causal hierarchy's equivalences, the
  equivalence of the global-hyperbolicity formulation used here with the
  Cauchy-hypersurface and smooth-splitting formulations, the existence and
  uniqueness theory for the Einstein-matter initial value problem, the
  maximal development, and singularity and censorship statements are
  obligations of the later pages of the general-relativity track, not of this
  page.
items.physical_scope: Scope and status note for the causal, initial-value and focusing material of the classical gravitational framework in its smooth branch: which items are mathematical definitions and conditional deductions, which physical readings belong to the framework postulates, and which existence, uniqueness, splitting and singularity claims are deferred to the later pages of the track. The note asserts no law, no solution family, no measurement and no empirical fact.

retained_claims.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the pointwise causal
classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a continuous map,
where $I$ has its relative topology. A **chart representative** on a parameter
neighborhood $J\subseteq I$ is $x\circ\gamma|_J$, where $(U,x)$ is a smooth
chart and $\gamma(J)\subseteq U$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for each $t\in I$ there are
$\delta>0$ and a chart $(U,x)$ such that
$\gamma(I\cap(t-\delta,t+\delta))\subseteq U$ and every coordinate of
$x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely continuous on every compact subinterval of
$I\cap(t-\delta,t+\delta)$ in the sense of
[[def-absolutely-continuous-function]]. This includes one-sided neighborhoods
at included endpoints. Equivalently, for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the coordinates of $x\circ\gamma$ are
absolutely continuous on $[a,b]$. The equivalence and independence of the
chart and smooth atlas are proved in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]]
clause (a); continuity is part of both formulations.

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point: a
constant chart representative has derivative zero everywhere in its interior,
contradicting the full-measure nonzero-velocity requirement.

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

The **causal future** and **chronological future** of a subset $S\subseteq M$
are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ q\in J^+(p)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the causal-curve class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Chart independence.** Local absolute continuity in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (a) is independent of the
chosen chart and of the smooth atlas. Every compact parameter interval
admits a finite subdivision on each of whose pieces a chart representative
is absolutely continuous. For a continuous curve, the relative neighborhood
formulation and the compact chart-interval formulation of that definition
are equivalent.

**(b) Velocity and smooth composition.** At every interior parameter value
$t$ at which one chart representative is differentiable, every chart
representative is differentiable, the velocity $\gamma'(t)$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (b) is well defined and
independent of the chart, and the set of parameter values at which some
chart representative is differentiable has full measure in the domain. For
every smooth map $F$ of an open subset of $M$ into a finite-dimensional
smooth manifold $P$ (in particular $P=\mathbb R$) whose domain contains
the image of $\gamma$, the composite $F\circ\gamma$ is locally absolutely
continuous in charts of $P$ using the same relative neighborhood definition,
and $(F\circ\gamma)'(t)=dF_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t))$ at almost
every parameter value $t$.

**(c) Piecewise $C^1$ curves.** Every piecewise $C^1$ curve (with the finite
admissible partition and one-sided endpoint convention of clause (a) of
[[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]) is locally absolutely
continuous; a piecewise $C^1$ curve all of whose tangents are future causal
is a future causal curve, and if in addition its tangents are future
timelike, it is a future timelike curve.

**(d) Concatenation.** If $\gamma_1:[a,b]\to M$ and $\gamma_2:[b,c]\to M$ are
future causal curves (respectively future timelike curves) with
$\gamma_1(b)=\gamma_2(b)$, then the concatenation $\gamma:[a,c]\to M$,
$\gamma(t):=\gamma_1(t)$ for $t\le b$ and $\gamma(t):=\gamma_2(t)$ for
$t\ge b$, is a future causal (respectively future timelike) curve; the same
holds for any finite chain of such curves.

**(e) Reparametrization.** If $\varphi:J\to I$ is a strictly increasing
$C^1$ diffeomorphism of intervals with $\varphi'>0$ and $\gamma:I\to M$ is
locally absolutely continuous, then $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is locally
absolutely continuous and $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is future causal (respectively
future timelike) exactly when $\gamma$ is. Moreover $\gamma$ is
future-inextendible if and only if $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is
future-inextendible, and this equivalence holds for every strictly increasing
continuous surjection $\varphi$ of intervals, not only the $C^1$ ones.

**(f) Relations.** The relation $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] is reflexive and transitive, and
$p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$ for all $p,q$; the relations $J^{\pm}$ and
$I^{\pm}$ of that definition are therefore nested, $I^{\pm}(S)\subseteq
J^{\pm}(S)$ for every $S\subseteq M$.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves and the relations $\le$, $\ll$, $I^{\pm}$, $J^{\pm}$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. All curves below are curves in
that sense.

**(a) Chronology and causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **chronological** when there is
no $p\in M$ with $p\ll p$, equivalently when there is no nonconstant future
timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$. It is **causal**
when there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with
$\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$; a nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
is called a **closed causal curve**, and a closed future timelike curve is
called a **closed timelike curve**.

**(b) Strong causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **strongly causal** when for every
$p\in M$ and every open set $U\subseteq M$ with $p\in U$ there is an open set
$V$ with $p\in V\subseteq U$ such that for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ and all $a\le s<t\le b$ with $\gamma(s)\in V$ and
$\gamma(t)\in V$ one has $\gamma([s,t])\subseteq V$. Thus no causal curve can
leave $V$ and later re-enter it; a set $V$ with this property for all causal
curves is called **causally convex for causal curves that meet it twice**.

**(c) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is **globally hyperbolic** when it is
strongly causal and for all $p,q\in M$ the **causal diamond**
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact in the subspace topology
([[def-compact-space]]).

**(d) Time functions.** A **time function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a function
$u:M\to\mathbb R$ which is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and satisfies
$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))$ for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ that is not constant on $[a,b]$.

**(e) Temporal functions.** A **temporal function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth
function $u:M\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]])
whose gradient is past-directed timelike: writing $du$ for its differential
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]) and $\nabla u$ for the vector field
with $g(\nabla u,X)=du(X)$ for every smooth vector field $X$, constructed from
the inverse metric of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], one
has
$$g(\nabla u,\nabla u)<0\qquad\text{and}\qquad du(N)=g(\nabla u,N)>0 .$$
The first inequality says that the gradient is nowhere zero and timelike; the
second fixes it as past-directed for the chosen time orientation. No level set
of a temporal function is asserted here to be a hypersurface or to be
spacelike, and no relation between temporal functions and compactness is
asserted; those claims are proved separately where they are used.

**(f) Scope and conventions.** These are mathematical conditions on the
Lorentzian model. Different sources define global hyperbolicity by equivalent
but differently phrased conditions; this page fixes the formulation of (c)
and proves the implications it uses. In particular no equivalence between
global hyperbolicity and the existence of a Cauchy hypersurface is asserted
by this definition, and the physical reading of strong causality or global
hyperbolicity as predictability of a classical model is adopted only in the
framework postulates.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $u$ be a temporal function
on it in the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]]
clause (e), and write $\nabla u$ for its gradient. Then:

**(a)** $du(v)=g(\nabla u,v)>0$ for every nonzero future causal vector $v$.

**(b)** For every future causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ in the class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], the composite $u\circ\gamma$ is
locally absolutely continuous, its derivative satisfies
$(u\circ\gamma)'(t)>0$ at almost every $t\in I$, and consequently
$$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))\qquad\text{whenever }a<b\text{ and }\gamma \text{ is not constant on }[a,b].$$

**(c)** $u$ is a time function on $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (d); every level
set $u^{-1}(c)$, $c\in\mathbb R$, is achronal; and $(M,g,N)$ is causal and
chronological: it admits no nonconstant future causal curve with equal
endpoints.

retained_claims.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and let
$S\subseteq M$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike
embedded hypersurface** when it is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
of $M$ ([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) such that the
restriction of $g_p$ to $T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for
every $p\in\Sigma$; equivalently, every nonzero vector tangent to $\Sigma$ is
spacelike ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). A spacelike
embedded hypersurface is automatically a nondegenerate hypersurface, so its
$g$-orthogonal complement in $T_pM$ is one-dimensional and nondegenerate, and
it carries a unique future-directed unit timelike normal; that normal is
constructed where it is used, not here.

**(b) Achronality and acausality.** $S$ is **achronal** when no two distinct
points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\ll q$ or $q\ll p$; $S$ is **acausal** when no two
distinct points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\le q$ or $q\le p$. Every acausal set is
achronal, since $p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$.

**(c) Cauchy sets.** $S$ is a **Cauchy set** when for every inextendible
causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ the parameter set
$$\gamma^{-1}[S]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$$
has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection
of intervals induces a bijection of parameter sets, this condition is
invariant under reparametrization
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (e)); it is stated in terms of
parameters rather than of the point set $\gamma(I)\cap S$, so that a closed
causal curve counts two visits to the same point as two parameter values. A
**Cauchy hypersurface** is a Cauchy set that is also a spacelike embedded
hypersurface in the sense of clause (a).

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define
$$D^+(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve through }p \text{ meets }S\},$$
and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve
through }p\text{ meets }S\}$, where "meets $S$" means that some parameter
value is mapped into $S$, and $D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$ is the **domain of
dependence** of $S$.

**(e) Cauchy horizon.** For a closed set $S\subseteq M$ the **future Cauchy
horizon** is
$$H^+(S):=D^+(S)\setminus I^-(D^+(S)),$$
the set of points of $D^+(S)$ that are not chronologically preceded by any
point of $D^+(S)$; dually $H^-(S):=D^-(S)\setminus I^+(D^-(S))$, and the
**Cauchy horizon** is $H(S):=H^+(S)\cup H^-(S)$.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of
Cauchy sets nor any relation between the objects defined here is asserted.

retained_claims.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and Einstein tensor $G$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]],
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a)), and fix real
constants $\kappa$ and $\Lambda$ (the framework coupling constants, purely
parameters for this definition).

**(a) The geometric data.**
For $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is
one-dimensional and nondegenerate
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]],
[[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]]); there is therefore a unique
$n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with $g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$ and it
depends smoothly on $p$, the **future unit normal field** of $\Sigma$; this
and the properties of $h$ and $K$ below are proved, not assumed, in
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]. Define
on $\Sigma$ the **induced metric** $h$ and the **second fundamental form**
$K$ by
$$h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W),\qquad K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma),$$
where $\nabla_Vn$ is the covariant derivative at $p$ of the ambient field $n$
in the tangential direction $V$; $h$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on
$\Sigma$ and $K$ a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]).

**(b) Matter data and constraints.** Let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $M$ (the stress-energy field of a matter branch). Its
**matter data on $\Sigma$** are the smooth fields
$$\rho:=T(n,n),\qquad j(V):=-T(n,V)\quad(V\in T\Sigma).$$
The tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ **satisfies the constraint equations** for
$(\kappa,\Lambda)$ when
$$G(n,n)-\Lambda=\kappa\,\rho,\qquad G(n,V)=\kappa\,T(n,V)\quad\text{for every }V\in T_p\Sigma,\ p\in\Sigma .$$
The first is the normal projection of the equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$
evaluated on $(n,n)$, namely $G(n,n)+\Lambda g(n,n)=\kappa T(n,n)$, with
$g(n,n)=-1$; the second is the normal-tangential projection, the term in
$\Lambda$ dropping because $g(n,V)=0$. That a solution of the field equation
satisfies these two projections is proved in
[[lem-gr-constraint-projections]]. The purely tangential projection
$G(V,W)+\Lambda h(V,W)=\kappa T(V,W)$ is not part of the constraints and is
not required here.

**(c) Developments.** A **development** of the data
$(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
$(M',g',N')$ together with a smooth embedding $\varphi:\Sigma\to M'$ whose
image is a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric $\varphi^*g'=h$
and second fundamental form $K$ with respect to its future unit normal $n'$.
Write $T'$ for the smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field included as
the development's stress-energy field. Require the tensor equation
$$G'+\Lambda g'=\kappa T'$$
at every point of $M'$, where $G'$ is the Einstein tensor of $g'$ with its
metric-selected connection, defined as above. The constants $\kappa$ and
$\Lambda$ are the fixed parameters of the initial data. The matter-data matching condition is
the pair of normal projections
$$\rho(p)=T'_{\varphi(p)}(n'_{\varphi(p)},n'_{\varphi(p)}),\qquad j_p(V)=-T'_{\varphi(p)}(n'_{\varphi(p)},d\varphi_p(V))\quad(p\in\Sigma,\ V\in T_p\Sigma).$$
Equivalently, the scalar field $T'(n',n')$ along $\varphi(\Sigma)$ pulls
back to $\rho$, and the covector field $-T'(n',\cdot)$ restricted to
$T\varphi(\Sigma)$ pulls back to $j$. This tuple prescribes only these
stress-energy projections; any additional matter-field data are not included
in $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$. The development is a **globally hyperbolic
development** when
$\varphi(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy hypersurface of $(M',g',N')$. The implication
from this Cauchy property to global hyperbolicity of $(M',g',N')$ is a
separate theorem, deferred to the later causal theory; it is not established
by this definition
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]],
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)).

**(d) Maximality.** A globally hyperbolic development $(M_*,g_*,N_*;
\varphi_*)$ is **maximal** for the data when for every globally hyperbolic
development $(M',g',N';\varphi')$ there is a smooth isometric embedding
$\psi:M'\to M_*$ with $\psi\circ\varphi'=\varphi_*$, $\psi$ preserving the
time orientations and carrying the selected stress-energy tensor $T'$ to
$T_*$, that is, $\psi^*T_*=T'$. This is a universal embedding property: every globally hyperbolic
development embeds into the selected maximal one with its data and
stress-energy tensor preserved. It does not assert that arbitrary globally
hyperbolic developments are mutually isometric.

**(e) Scope.** The definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of
developments, and it does not assert that $T'$ is generated by matter fields
solving any equation: those claims require the local and global existence theory of
the Einstein-matter system and are not made on this page. The constraint
equations are displayed only as equations satisfied or not by given data.
The equivalent formulation of the constraints in terms of the induced scalar
curvature of $h$ and the divergence of $K$, and the existence theory for
solutions of the constraints, rest on the Gauss-Codazzi relations and on PDE
theory and are deferred to the later pages of this track; no such
equivalence is asserted here.

retained_claims.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a
spacelike embedded hypersurface in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a), so that
$\Sigma$ is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) and the restriction of $g_p$
to $T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for every $p\in\Sigma$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). In the notation of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (a), whose claims
this lemma establishes:

**(a) The future unit normal.** For every $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal
complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is one-dimensional, nondegenerate for $g_p$,
and negative definite: every nonzero $u\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is timelike,
$g_p(u,u)<0$. Hence there is exactly one $n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with
$g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$.

**(b) Smoothness along the hypersurface.** The assignment $p\mapsto n_p$ is
smooth along $\Sigma$: for every $p\in\Sigma$ there are an open neighborhood
$O$ of $p$ in $M$ and a smooth vector field $\tilde n$ on $O$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) with
$\tilde n|_{\Sigma\cap O}=n|_{\Sigma\cap O}$, and for any two such local
extensions the covariant derivative at a point of $\Sigma$ in a direction
tangent to $\Sigma$ agrees. Thus for $V\in T_p\Sigma$ the vector
$\nabla_Vn\in T_pM$ is well defined as $\nabla_{\tilde X}\tilde n|_p$ for any
smooth extensions $\tilde n$ of $n$ and $\tilde X$ of a tangent field with
$\tilde X_p=V$ ([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

**(c) The induced metric and second fundamental form.** The **induced
metric** $h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W)$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and
$$K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma)$$
(the **second fundamental form**) defines a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K$ on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$$K_p(V,W)=-g_p(\nabla_VW,n_p),$$
where $\nabla_VW$ is the ambient covariant derivative at $p$ of any smooth
extension of a tangent field with value $W$ at $p$, in the direction of any
extension with value $V$ at $p$.

**(d) The shape operator.** The endomorphism $S_p:T_p\Sigma\to T_p\Sigma$
defined by $h_p(S_pV,W)=K_p(V,W)$ for all $W\in T_p\Sigma$ is well defined,
linear and self-adjoint for the positive definite form $h_p$, and the
Weingarten relation $\nabla_Vn=S_pV$ holds for every $V\in T_p\Sigma$.

retained_claims.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $T$ be a
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), let $\kappa,\Lambda\in\mathbb R$
and let $G$ be the Einstein tensor of the metric-selected connection
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Suppose that the field
equation
$$G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$$
holds at every point of $M$. Let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded
hypersurface with future unit normal field $n$, induced metric $h$ and second
fundamental form $K$, and let $\rho:=T(n,n)$ and $j(V):=-T(n,V)$ for
$V\in T_p\Sigma$, $p\in\Sigma$, be the matter data of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (b). Then:

**(a)** The tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ satisfies the constraint equations
for $(\kappa,\Lambda)$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (b),
$$G(n,n)-\Lambda=\kappa\,\rho,\qquad G(n,V)=\kappa\,T(n,V) \quad\text{for every }V\in T_p\Sigma,\ p\in\Sigma;$$
equivalently $G(n,V)=-\kappa\,j(V)$ on $\Sigma$.

**(b)** The fields $\rho$ and $j$ are smooth on $\Sigma$: in every slice chart
their expressions in the slice coordinates are $C^\infty$.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset.

**(a) Geodesic congruence.** A **smooth future unit timelike geodesic
congruence** on $U$ is an observer congruence $n$ on $U$
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]],
[[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]), so that
$g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,N)<0$ on $U$, which in addition is geodesic:
$$\nabla_nn=0\qquad\text{on }U .$$
Thus each observer curve of the congruence is an affinely parametrized
geodesic ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) and its flow parameter is
affine; by [[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]] the tangent is
future unit timelike at every parameter value.

**(b) Observer curves.** By [[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]]
each $q\in U$ lies on a unique maximal integral curve
$\gamma_q:I_q\to U$ of $n$ with $\gamma_q(0)=q$; these are the **observer
curves** or **flow lines** of the congruence, and their parameter $s$ is the
**affine parameter** of the geodesic. The mathematical proper-time function
$\tau$ of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]], normalized by
$\tau(0)=0$, satisfies
$$\tau(s_2)-\tau(s_1)=\frac{1}{c}\int_{s_1}^{s_2}\sqrt{-g(n,n)}\,ds=\frac{s_2-s_1}{c}\qquad(s_1<s_2,\ s_1,s_2\in I_q).$$
Thus $\tau(s)=s/c$ with this normalization. This is the metric-defined
mathematical proper-time parameter, not a clock reading; the ideal-clock
interpretation is a separate physical assumption.

**(c) Kinematic quantities.** On $U$ define the smooth covariant $2$-tensor
field
$$B_{ab}:=\nabla_bn_a,\qquad n_a:=g_{ab}n^b ,$$
the **rest-space metric field**
$$h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+n_an_b,$$
with index-raised field $h^{ab}:=g^{ab}+n^an^b$ built from the inverse metric
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]), and:
$$\theta:=g^{ab}B_{ab},\qquad \sigma_{ab}:=B_{(ab)}-\tfrac13\theta\,h_{ab},\qquad \omega_{ab}:=B_{[ab]},$$
the **expansion**, **shear** and **vorticity** of the congruence, where
$B_{(ab)}=\tfrac12(B_{ab}+B_{ba})$ and $B_{[ab]}=\tfrac12(B_{ab}-B_{ba})$.
The three fields $\theta$, $\sigma$, $\omega$ and the tensor $B$ are smooth
in every chart ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), because
components of $\nabla n$, $g$ and $g^{-1}$ are smooth.

**(d) Scope.** The definition asserts no dynamical equation, no sign of
$\theta$ and no physical interpretation. In particular the identities making
$\sigma$ and $\omega$ rest-space tensors, their tracelessness and
antisymmetry, and the decomposition $B=\tfrac13\theta h+\sigma+\omega$ are
proved in [[lem-gr-kinematic-decomposition-identities]], not assumed here.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
Let $n$ be a geodesic congruence with kinematic quantities $B$, $\theta$,
$\sigma$, $\omega$ and $h$ on $U$ as in
[[def-gr-geodesic-congruence-and-kinematics]], and write
$h^{ab}:=g^{ab}+n^an^b$. Then, everywhere on $U$:

**(a)** $n^aB_{ab}=0$ and $B_{ab}n^b=0$; hence $B$ takes values in the
rest-space bundle $n^{\perp}$ in both slots
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]).

**(b)** $h_{ab}n^b=0$, the restriction of $h$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
definite, $h^{ab}h_{bc}=\delta^a_c+n^an_c$, and $h_{ab}h^{ba}=3$.

**(c)** $\sigma_{ab}$ is symmetric and $h^{ab}\sigma_{ab}=0$;
$\omega_{ab}$ is antisymmetric; and
$B_{ab}=\tfrac13\theta\,h_{ab}+\sigma_{ab}+\omega_{ab}$.

**(d)** $B_{ab}B^{ba}=\tfrac13\theta^2+\sigma_{ab}\sigma^{ab}-\omega_{ab}\omega^{ab}$,
where all indices are raised with $g$; moreover
$\sigma_{ab}\sigma^{ab}\ge0$ and $\omega_{ab}\omega^{ab}\ge0$, the first
vanishing exactly when $\sigma=0$ and the second exactly when $\omega=0$.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and curvature $R$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). For a smooth vector field
$Z$ let $A$ be the smooth $(1,1)$-tensor field $A^a{}_b:=\nabla_bZ^a$ and
let $B:=\nabla A$ be its covariant derivative, $B^a{}_{bc}:=\nabla_bA^a{}_c$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]] for the
extension of $\nabla$ to tensor fields).

**(a)** For all smooth vector fields $Z$ and all indices,
$$B^a{}_{bc}-B^a{}_{cb}=R^a{}_{dbc}Z^d .$$

**(b)** Contracting the first index with the second lower index,
$$B^a{}_{ab}-B^a{}_{ba}=\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}Z^d .$$

**(c)** For all smooth vector fields $V,Z$,
$$V^c\nabla_c(\nabla_aZ^a)=\nabla_a\bigl(V^c\nabla_cZ^a\bigr) -(\nabla_aV^c)(\nabla_cZ^a)-\operatorname{Ric}_{cd}V^cZ^d ,$$
where $\nabla_aW^a$ denotes the divergence of a vector field and
$\nabla_a(V^c\nabla_cZ^a)$ is the divergence of the vector field
$W^a:=V^c\nabla_cZ^a$.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$U\subseteq M$ be open and let $n$ be a smooth future unit timelike geodesic
congruence on $U$ with kinematic quantities $B$, $\theta$, $\sigma$, $\omega$
and rest-space metric $h$
([[def-gr-geodesic-congruence-and-kinematics]]). Let $q\in U$ and let
$\gamma_q:I_q\to U$ be the observer curve through $q$ with affine parameter
$s$, $s\in I_q$ ([[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]]).

**(a) Raychaudhuri equation.** For every $s\in I_q$,
$$\frac{d}{ds}\theta(\gamma_q(s)) =-\tfrac13\theta(\gamma_q(s))^2-\sigma_{ab}\sigma^{ab}(\gamma_q(s)) +\omega_{ab}\omega^{ab}(\gamma_q(s))-\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(\gamma_q(s))\,n^a(\gamma_q(s))\,n^b(\gamma_q(s)),$$
where all contractions use $g$ and $\operatorname{Ric}$ is the Ricci tensor
of the metric-selected connection
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]).

**(b) Focusing.** Suppose $\omega=0$ and
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}n^an^b\ge0$ on $U$, and suppose there is
$s_0\in I_q$ with $\theta_0:=\theta(\gamma_q(s_0))<0$. Then
$\theta(\gamma_q(s))<0$ for every $s\in I_q$ with $s>s_0$, and
$$\frac{1}{-\theta(\gamma_q(s))}\le\frac{1}{-\theta_0}-\frac{s-s_0}{3}.$$
Consequently $s<s_0+3/(-\theta_0)$ for every such $s$, so
$\sup I_q\le s_0+3/(-\theta_0)$ for the maximal integral curve in $U$.
Any continuation beyond this bound that remains a smooth geodesic congruence
and continues to satisfy $\omega=0$ and $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}n^an^b\ge0$
along the continued flow line is impossible. A continuation outside $U$ that
does not preserve these hypotheses is not ruled out by this result.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous endpoint argument in this clause. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$(U,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ in which every metric component
$g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$ is a constant function on $U$. Then:

**(a)** Every Christoffel symbol of $\nabla$ in the chart vanishes
identically on $U$,
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=0$ ([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b)** The curvature tensor of $\nabla$ vanishes identically on $U$,
$R=0$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]).

**(c)** Every coordinate curve of the chart is a geodesic of $\nabla$; that
is, for fixed constants $c^1,c^2,c^3$ the curve $s\mapsto
x^{-1}(s,c^1,c^2,c^3)$ is a geodesic in the affine parameter $s$
([[prop-coordinate-geodesic-equation]]).
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
**(a) The underlying manifold.** Let $M:=\mathbb R^4$ be Euclidean four-space
as a set and real vector space ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), equipped
with its standard smooth structure, in which the identity map
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3):M\to\mathbb R^4$ is a global smooth chart
([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[prop-open-subsets-of-euclidean-space-have-the-standard-smooth-structure]]).
The coordinate vector fields $\partial_a:=\partial/\partial x^a$,
$a=0,1,2,3$, are smooth vector fields on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), and at every
$p\in M$ the tuple
$(\partial_0|_p,\partial_1|_p,\partial_2|_p,\partial_3|_p)$ is a basis of
$T_pM$ ([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(b) The metric.** The **flat metric** $\eta$ is the smooth covariant
$2$-tensor field on $M$ whose components in the chart $x$ are the constant
functions $\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), that is
$$\eta=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2 .$$
It is symmetric, and at every $p$ its matrix in the basis of (a) is
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$: diagonal, with one negative and three positive
entries and no zero entry. Hence $\eta_p$ is nondegenerate with inertia
$(3,1,0)$, that is, a Lorentz form on $T_pM$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), and $(M,\eta)$ is a smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The restriction of $\eta_p$ to
$\operatorname{span}(\partial_1|_p,\partial_2|_p,\partial_3|_p)$ is positive
definite.

**(c) Time orientation.** The field $N:=\partial_0$ satisfies
$\eta(N,N)=-1<0$ pointwise, so $N$ is a time orientation of $(M,\eta)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c)). The triple $(M,\eta,N)$ is
the **flat model**. At every $p$ the pointwise vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]] applies, and a nonzero causal
$v\in T_pM$ is future-directed exactly when $\eta_p(v,N_p)<0$
([[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]).

**(d) Events, displacements and straight paths.** The points of $M$ are the
**events** of the model. Since $M=\mathbb R^4$ is a vector space, for events
$p,q\in M$ the **displacement** from $p$ to $q$ is the vector $q-p\in M$, and
the **straight path** from $p$ to $q$ is the curve $s\mapsto p+s(q-p)$ on
$[0,1]$, whose chart representative has the constant velocity $q-p$. For
$v\in\mathbb R^4$ the **translation** is the map $\tau_v(p):=p+v$ of $M$.

**(e) Inertial charts and frames.** A chart of $M$ with domain $M$ is called a
**global chart**. A global chart $y=(y^0,y^1,y^2,y^3):M\to\mathbb R^4$ is
**inertial** when its components of $\eta$ are the constant functions
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ on $M$ and its first coordinate vector field
$\partial/\partial y^0$ is future-directed at every point. The chart $x$ of (a)
is inertial: its components of $\eta$ are $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ by
(b), and its first coordinate vector field is $N$, future-directed by (c). If
$y$ is inertial and $o\in M$, the tuple
$(o;\partial/\partial y^0|_o,\partial/\partial y^1|_o,
\partial/\partial y^2|_o,\partial/\partial y^3|_o)$ is an **inertial frame**
at $o$; its vectors satisfy
$\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ and $e_0$ is
future-directed.

**(f) Cone sets.** Let a vector $v\in T_pM$ have coordinates
$(v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3)$ in an inertial chart, write $v_s:=(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ and
$|v_s|:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Write
$$C^+:=\{v\in\mathbb R^4:v^0>|v_s|\}$$
and $\overline{C^+}:=\{v\in\mathbb R^4:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$ for the coordinate cone
sets. In every inertial chart and at every event $p$,
the future cone $C_p^+$ of (c) consists of exactly those $v$ with
$v^0>|v_s|$, its closure of exactly those with $v^0\ge|v_s|$, and the
future-directed causal vectors of $T_pM$ are exactly the nonzero vectors with
$v^0\ge|v_s|$; moreover the future cone is closed under sums. All of this is
proved in [[lem-gr-flat-inertial-cone-criterion-and-sums]], where the
independence of the inertial chart is also established.

**(g) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition; it asserts nothing about
nature. The physical reading of the flat model is recorded with the framework
postulates of this library and is not part of this definition, and the flat
examples and counterexamples of this page are conditional statements inside
the model.

retained_claims.statement:
Let $(M,\eta,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], let $y$ be an inertial
chart, let $p\in M$, and let $v\in T_pM$ have coordinates
$v=v^0\partial_0+\dots+v^3\partial_3$ in the chart
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]). Write
$v_s:=(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ and $|v_s|:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then:

**(a)** For every nonzero $v\in T_pM$: $v$ is future timelike iff
$v^0>|v_s|$, and past timelike iff $v^0<-|v_s|$; $v$ is future null iff
$0<v^0=|v_s|$, and past null iff $0<-v^0=|v_s|$; $v$ is future causal iff
$v^0\ge|v_s|$, past causal iff $v^0\le-|v_s|$, and causal iff
$|v^0|\ge|v_s|$; and every nonzero future causal $v$ satisfies $v^0>0$.

**(b)** $C_p^+=\{v\in T_pM:v^0>|v_s|\}$ and
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)=\{v\in T_pM:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$; the future-directed
causal vectors are exactly $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}
=\{v\neq0:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$.

**(c)** If $v,w\in T_pM$ are future causal, then $v+w$ is future causal; if
one of $v,w$ is future timelike and the other is future causal, then $v+w$ is
future timelike. Equivalently
$C_p^++\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\subseteq C_p^+$ and
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)+\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)
\subseteq\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)$.

retained_claims.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,\eta,N)$ be the
flat model of [[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], with its
global inertial chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, written $x=(x^0,z)$ with
$z\in\mathbb R^3$ (clauses (a), (b) and (e) of that definition), and let
$\gamma:I\to M$ be a future causal curve in the class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** $x^0\circ\gamma:I\to\mathbb R$ is strictly increasing.

**(b)** For all $a<b$ in $I$,
$$\bigl|z(\gamma(b))-z(\gamma(a))\bigr|\le x^0(\gamma(b))-x^0(\gamma(a)),$$
and consequently $\gamma$ is injective and its image is a $1$-Lipschitz graph
over the interval $(x^0\circ\gamma)(I)$.

**(c)** If $\gamma$ is future-inextendible then
$\sup\,(x^0\circ\gamma)(I)=+\infty$; if $\gamma$ is past-inextendible then
$\inf\,(x^0\circ\gamma)(I)=-\infty$. Hence if $\gamma$ is inextendible then
$x^0\circ\gamma$ is a strictly increasing surjection onto $\mathbb R$, and
for every $c\in\mathbb R$ the parameter set
$\{t\in I:x^0(\gamma(t))=c\}$ is a singleton.

**(d)** The coordinate function $u:=x^0$ is a temporal function of the flat
model in the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]]
clause (e): its gradient is the vector field $\nabla u=-\partial_0$ on all of
$M$, with $\eta(\nabla u,\nabla u)=-1<0$ and $du(\partial_0)=1>0$
everywhere.
