retained_claims.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous causal-curve
conclusions used here.

Let $(M,\eta,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], with its global inertial
chart $x=(x^0,z)$, its cone sets $C^+,\overline{C^+}$ of clause (f) and its
translation action of clause (d), and with the causal relations of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** For every $p\in M$, $J^+(p)=p+\overline{C^+}$ and
$I^+(p)=p+C^+$, where the sum is the translation of clause (d), the cone sets
are those of clause (f), and the displacement is read in the vector space
$M=\mathbb R^4$; in the chart,
$$q\in J^+(p)\Longleftrightarrow x^0(q)-x^0(p)\ge|z(q)-z(p)|_{\mathrm e}.$$

**(b)** For every $c\in\mathbb R$ the level set
$\Sigma_c:=x^{-1}(\{c\}\times\mathbb R^3)$ is a spacelike embedded hypersurface of $M$, and
every inextendible causal curve of $M$ meets $\Sigma_c$ in exactly one
parameter value; equivalently, $\Sigma_c$ is a Cauchy hypersurface in the
sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c).

**(c)** For all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond $J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is
compact.

**(d)** The model is strongly causal in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (b); hence it is
globally hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
Let $(\hat M,\hat g)$ be a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), let $\Gamma$ be a discrete
group equipped with its discrete smooth structure (a zero-dimensional Lie
group, so that a **smooth action** is one for which every map
$p\mapsto\gamma\cdot p$, $\gamma\in\Gamma$, is smooth), and let $\Gamma$ act
on $\hat M$ smoothly, freely and properly in the sense of
[[def-free-and-proper-lie-group-actions]]; write $\gamma\cdot p$ for the
action and $d\gamma_p$ for the differential of $p\mapsto\gamma\cdot p$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]). Suppose that every $\gamma\in\Gamma$
**preserves $\hat g$**, that is
$$\hat g_{\gamma\cdot p}\bigl(d\gamma_p V,d\gamma_p W\bigr)=\hat g_p(V,W)$$
for all $p\in\hat M$, $V,W\in T_p\hat M$ and $\gamma\in\Gamma$. Let
$q:\hat M\to M:=\hat M/\Gamma$ be the orbit map. Then:

**(a)** $M$ is a Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold, $q$ is a
smooth surjective submersion, and $q$ is a local diffeomorphism at every
point of $\hat M$.

**(b)** There is a unique smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ with $q^*g=\hat g$; equivalently
$g_{q(p)}(dq_pV,dq_pW)=\hat g_p(V,W)$ for all $p,V,W$.

**(c)** If $\hat N$ is a smooth vector field on $\hat M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) which is
$\Gamma$-invariant, $\hat N_{\gamma\cdot p}=d\gamma_p(\hat N_p)$, and
satisfies $\hat g(\hat N,\hat N)<0$, then the prescription
$N_{q(p)}:=dq_p(\hat N_p)$ defines a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$ with
$g(N,N)<0$ for all points. In particular, a $\Gamma$-invariant time
orientation of $(\hat M,\hat g)$ descends to one of $(M,g)$.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
Let $A:=\mathbb R^4$ carry the flat structure $(\eta,N)$ of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], with global inertial
chart $x=(x^0,z)$ and translations $\tau_\lambda(p)=p+\lambda$ of clause (d),
and write $e_0:=(1,0,0,0)\in A$. Fix $L>0$, let
$\Lambda:=\{nLe_0:n\in\mathbb Z\}\subseteq A$ act on $A$ by the translations
$\tau_\lambda(p)=p+\lambda$ and fix $o\in A$
(the action of the discrete group $\mathbb Z$, equipped with its discrete
smooth structure, is a special case of the actions of
[[def-free-and-proper-lie-group-actions]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be the quotient
time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold produced by
[[lem-gr-quotient-by-isometric-free-proper-action]], with orbit map
$q:A\to M$. Then:

**(a)** $q$ is a local isometry: $g_{q(p)}(dq_pV,dq_pW)=\eta_p(V,W)$ for all
$p\in A$ and $V,W\in T_pA$; and $(M,g)$ is flat, in the sense that every
point has a chart in which the metric components are the constants
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the curvature tensor of the
metric-selected connection vanishes identically.

**(b)** The curve $\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$, $\gamma(s):=q(o+se_0)$, is a
nonconstant smooth future timelike curve with $\gamma(s+L)=\gamma(s)$ for
all $s$; hence $(M,g,N)$ is neither chronological nor causal, and it
possesses a closed future timelike curve.

**(c)** Every two points $p,q\in M$ (equal or distinct) satisfy $p\ll q$:
the model is totally vicious. Consequently no subset of $M$ with two
distinct points is achronal or acausal.

**(d)** $M$ admits no Cauchy set and hence no Cauchy hypersurface in the
sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]].
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
For the general causal-curve conclusions (c) and (d), assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) as required by the absolutely continuous flat-curve calculus. The geometric restriction and explicit incomplete geodesic in (a)-(b) use no choice premise.

Let $A:=\mathbb R^4$ carry the flat structure $(\eta,N)$ of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], with global inertial
chart $x=(x^0,z)=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, and write $e_0:=(1,0,0,0)\in A$. Put
$$M:=x^{-1}\bigl((0,1)\times\mathbb R^3\bigr)=\{p\in A:0<x^0(p)<1\},$$
an open subset of $A$, and let $g:=\eta|_M$ and $N:=\partial_0|_M$ be the
restrictions of the metric and of the time-orientation field; write $x$ also for
the restricted chart $x|_M:M\to(0,1)\times\mathbb R^3$. Then:

**(a) The slab model.** $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) whose restricted chart
$x$ has the constant components
$g_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$; the Christoffel symbols of the
metric-selected connection vanish on $M$, the curvature of that connection
vanishes on $M$, and every coordinate curve of the chart is a geodesic
([[lem-gr-constant-component-chart-flatness]]). Every curve in $M$ is locally
absolutely continuous, future causal or future timelike for $(M,g)$ exactly
when it is so for $(A,\eta)$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]).

**(b) An incomplete timelike geodesic.** Fix $z_0\in\mathbb R^3$ and let
$$\gamma:(0,1)\to M,\qquad \gamma(s):=x^{-1}(s,z_0),$$
be the vertical line through $z_0$. Then $\gamma$ is a smooth future timelike
curve and a geodesic with affine parameter $s$ and unit tangent
$\gamma'(s)=\partial_0|_{\gamma(s)}$; its velocity satisfies
$\nabla_{\gamma'}\gamma'=0$. There is no geodesic
$\tilde\gamma:(a,b)\to M$ with $b>1$ (or $a<0$) whose restriction to $(0,1)$
equals $\gamma$: the parameter interval $(0,1)$ is the maximal domain of a
geodesic with these data. Moreover $\gamma$ does not converge to any point of
$M$ as $s\to1$ (it converges in $A$ to the boundary point $x^{-1}(1,z_0)$,
which does not lie in $M$); hence $\gamma$ is future-inextendible in the
sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d) and its affine
parameter is bounded above. The model is therefore timelike geodesically
**incomplete**: it carries an inextendible future-directed timelike geodesic
whose affine parameter domain is bounded.

**(c) A Cauchy slice.** The set
$\Sigma_{1/2}:=x^{-1}(\{1/2\}\times\mathbb R^3)$ is a spacelike embedded
hypersurface of $(M,g)$ and a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clauses (a) and (c)):
every inextendible causal curve of $(M,g)$ meets it in exactly one parameter
value. Hence $\Sigma_{1/2}$ is a Cauchy hypersurface.

**(d) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal and its causal
diamonds $J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$, $p,q\in M$, are compact; hence it is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c).

retained_claims.statement:
This note fixes the scope of the page's causal and initial-value content and
the status of its claims; it proves nothing by itself.

- **Model conditions versus physical readings.** Chronology, causality, strong
  causality, global hyperbolicity, achronality, acausality, the Cauchy-set
  property and the existence of time or temporal functions are mathematical
  conditions on a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
  ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]],
  [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]],
  [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]). The reading of the
  causal future and past as the model's signalling structure, and of the
  absence of closed causal curves or of a Cauchy set as a failure of
  predictability for the classical model, is adopted in the framework
  postulates ([[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]]); it is not proved
  and not observationally established by the mathematics of this page. A
  model with a closed timelike curve is not "mathematically inconsistent": it
  is a model whose causal structure differs from that of the flat models of
  the examples page.

- **What is proved here.** Conditional deductions inside the stated classes
  of curves and models: the curve calculus of
  [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]], the implication from temporal functions
  to time functions and the exclusion of closed causal curves by a time
  function ([[lem-gr-temporal-functions-and-time-functions]]), the
  extendibility of convergent causal ends and the acausality of Cauchy sets
  ([[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]]), the Minkowski model's global
  hyperbolicity and its inertial Cauchy hypersurfaces
  ([[thm-gr-minkowski-cauchy-and-global-hyperbolicity]]), the flat cylinder's
  failure of chronology, causality and the Cauchy property
  ([[thm-gr-flat-cylinder-closed-timelike-and-no-cauchy-set]]), the open
  slab's incompleteness together with its Cauchy slice and global
  hyperbolicity ([[thm-gr-flat-slab-incomplete-geodesic-and-cauchy-slice]]),
  and the local focusing bound along a geodesic congruence
  ([[thm-gr-timelike-raychaudhuri-and-local-focusing]]). Each is a statement
  about the explicitly displayed model and its curve class.

- **Initial value material.** [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]
  defines initial data $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ and the constraint equations as
  the normal and normal-tangential projections of the field equation;
  [[lem-gr-constraint-projections]] proves that data induced by a solution of
  the field equation ([[post-gr-einstein-field-law]]) satisfy the
  constraints, and the normal, induced metric and second fundamental form are
  constructed in
  [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]. The
  page does not assert the converse in any form: the existence of a
  development of given data, its uniqueness, the maximal globally hyperbolic
  development, and the equivalence of global hyperbolicity with the existence
  of a Cauchy hypersurface or of a smooth temporal function with Cauchy
  levels are not proved here. Those statements require the local
  Einstein-matter well-posedness theory, the Gauss-Codazzi relations and
  global causal gluing arguments, and are deferred to the later pages of this
  track (the convex-normal-neighborhood and full symmetric-hyperbolic
  pages). The equivalent component form of the constraints in terms of the
  induced scalar curvature and the divergence of $K$ is deferred with them.

- **Focusing versus singularities.** The Raychaudhuri theorem of this page is
  a local differential inequality along one flow line of a smooth geodesic
  congruence: it bounds the affine parameter range on which the congruence
  remains smooth under the stated hypotheses. It does not assert that the
  spacetime ends, that a singularity theorem holds, or that an
  infinite-curvature point forms. A genuine singularity theorem requires its
  own energy, causality and global compactness hypotheses and a complete
  proof, none of which is claimed here; cosmic censorship and chronology
  protection are not theorems and are not used.

- **Empirical status.** The page contains no experiment, no apparatus, no
  measured input, no sampling model and no statistical inference, and it
  draws no conclusion about nature. A prediction computed from a fully
  specified model may later be compared with reported observations; such a
  comparison tests the combined model and its auxiliary assumptions, and
  agreement is evidence, not a proof of the model or of its postulates.

- **Deferred obligations.** The causal hierarchy's equivalences, the
  equivalence of the global-hyperbolicity formulation used here with the
  Cauchy-hypersurface and smooth-splitting formulations, the existence and
  uniqueness theory for the Einstein-matter initial value problem, the
  maximal development, and singularity and censorship statements are
  obligations of the later pages of the general-relativity track, not of this
  page.

canonical_row.title: Causal And Initial Value Boundaries — Examples

items.title: Worked Minkowski slice: Cauchy level sets, causal double cones and the compact diamond
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous causal-curve
conclusions used here.

Let $(A,\eta,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], written $A=\mathbb R^4$,
with its global inertial chart $x=(x^0,z)=(t,z)$, and write
$e_0:=(1,0,0,0)\in A$. This example works through the explicit computations
behind [[thm-gr-minkowski-cauchy-and-global-hyperbolicity]].

**(i)** For every $c\in\mathbb R$ the level set
$\Sigma_c:=x^{-1}(\{c\}\times\mathbb R^3)$ is a spacelike embedded
hypersurface with induced metric $\delta=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1)$ in the
coordinates $(z^1,z^2,z^3)$ and future unit normal $\partial_0$
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a)).

**(ii)** The coordinate $t=x^0$ is a temporal function: its gradient in the
chart is $\nabla t=-\partial_0$, with
$\eta(\nabla t,\nabla t)=-1<0$ and $dt(\partial_0)=1>0$
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (e),
[[lem-gr-flat-time-monotonicity-and-lipschitz-graphs]] clause (d)).

**(iii)** For $\varepsilon>0$ and $p\in A$ the double cone
$$V_\varepsilon(p):=I^+\bigl(p-\varepsilon e_0\bigr)\cap I^-\bigl(p+\varepsilon e_0\bigr)$$
is open, contains $p$, and is causally convex for causal curves that meet it
twice: if a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to A$ has
$\gamma(a),\gamma(b)\in V_\varepsilon(p)$, then $\gamma(s)\in
V_\varepsilon(p)$ for every $s\in(a,b)$. In coordinates,
$$V_\varepsilon(p)=\Bigl\{q:\ |z(q)-z(p)|_{\mathrm e}<\varepsilon-\bigl|x^0(q)-x^0(p)\bigr|\Bigr\}.$$

**(iv)** For $o:=0\in A$ and $q:=Te_0$, $T>0$, the causal diamond is
$$J^+(o)\cap J^-(Te_0)=\bigl\{r:\ |z(r)|_{\mathrm e}\le x^0(r)\le T-|z(r)|_{\mathrm e}\bigr\},$$
a closed bounded subset of $\mathbb R^4$, hence compact; its $t$-sections are
closed balls of radius $\min(t,T-t)$ for $0\le t\le T$, and are empty otherwise.

**(v)** The domain of dependence of each $\Sigma_c$ is all of $A$:
$D^+(\Sigma_c)\supseteq\{t\ge c\}$, $D^-(\Sigma_c)\supseteq\{t\le c\}$ and
$D(\Sigma_c)=A$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(d)).

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Minkowski spacetime as the basic model (section 1.1 printed pp. 3-6) and global hyperbolicity (Definition 4.117 and Theorem 4.119 printed pp. 146-147)

E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007): spacelike hypersurfaces and the orthogonal projector, section 2.4 printed pp. 28-34; foliations by spacelike slices, section 3.2.2 printed pp. 40-41

items.title: Worked vertical geodesics of the open flat slab: affine parameter, limit point and proper time
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous causal-curve
conclusions used here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the open flat slab $M=x^{-1}((0,1)\times\mathbb R^3)$ of
[[thm-gr-flat-slab-incomplete-geodesic-and-cauchy-slice]] with restricted
inertial chart $x=(x^0,z)$. Fix $z_0\in\mathbb R^3$ and let
$\gamma:(0,1)\to M$, $\gamma(s):=x^{-1}(s,z_0)$. This example records the
explicit numbers behind the incompleteness claim of that theorem:

**(i)** $\gamma$ is a smooth future timelike geodesic with affine parameter
$s$ and unit tangent $\gamma'(s)=\partial_0$; in the chart the geodesic
equation is $\ddot y=0$.

**(ii)** The affine separation and the Lorentzian length of the segment from
$s_1$ to $s_2$, $0<s_1<s_2<1$, are
$$\Delta s=s_2-s_1,\qquad L(\gamma|_{[s_1,s_2]})=\int_{s_1}^{s_2}\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}\,ds=s_2-s_1;$$
under the framework's SI length-coordinate convention
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]] clause (b), the coordinates
$x^0=s$ and the affine parameter values $s_1,s_2$ are lengths in metres,
while $c$ has units $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$; thus
$(s_2-s_1)/c$ is a duration in seconds. If $\gamma$ is also interpreted as
an ideal clock's worldline, the ideal-clock assumption of
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] clause (i) identifies that
metric-defined proper-time increment with the clock-reading difference.
This physical reading is conditional; the mathematical example alone asserts
no clock reading.

**(iii)** The maximal domain of a geodesic with the data of $\gamma$ is
exactly $(0,1)$; the image converges in the ambient affine space to the event
$x^{-1}(1,z_0)$, which does not belong to $M$. Hence $\gamma$ is
future-inextendible in $M$ with bounded affine parameter, and the slab is
timelike geodesically incomplete.

**(iv)** The slice $\Sigma_{1/2}=\{x^0=1/2\}$ is a Cauchy hypersurface and
the slab is globally hyperbolic, so the example exhibits incompleteness in a
globally hyperbolic model.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: causal curves (sections 1.11 and 2.5 printed pp. 15-16 and 32-33) and global hyperbolicity (section 4.5.4 printed pp. 146-148)

E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007): foliations by spacelike slices, the lapse function and the normal evolution vector, sections 3.2.2 and 3.3.1-3.3.2 printed pp. 40-42

items.title: Sharp radial focusing in flat Minkowski space: equality in the Raychaudhuri bound without a singularity
items.statement:
Let $(A,\eta,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], written $A=\mathbb R^4$,
with its global inertial chart $x=(t,z)$. Fix $T>0$ and let $e:=x^{-1}(T,0)$
be the event at coordinate time $T$ on the worldline of the origin. Let
$$O:=\bigl\{q\in A:\ T-t(q)>|z(q)|_{\mathrm e}\bigr\}$$
be the interior of the past light cone of $e$, and define
$$\rho:O\to(0,\infty),\qquad \rho(q):=\sqrt{\bigl(T-t(q)\bigr)^2-|z(q)|_{\mathrm e}^2},$$
and the vector field $W$ on $O$ whose chart components are
$$W^a(q):=\frac{e^a-q^a}{\rho(q)}\qquad(a=0,1,2,3).$$
Then:

**(i)** $W$ is a smooth future unit timelike vector field on the open set
$O$; it is a smooth future unit timelike geodesic congruence in the sense of
[[def-gr-geodesic-congruence-and-kinematics]] clause (a).

**(ii)** The maximal forward flow line of $W$ through $p\in O$ is
$$\gamma_p(s)=e-\Bigl(1-\frac{s}{\rho(p)}\Bigr)\bigl(e-p\bigr),\qquad s\in[0,\rho(p)),$$
with $\rho(\gamma_p(s))=\rho(p)-s$ and $\gamma_p(0)=p$; it reaches $e$ at
$s=\rho(p)$. The parameter $s=0$ is included as a one-sided endpoint, and
$e\notin O$ so it is excluded from the flow domain. Each affine geodesic
$s\mapsto\gamma_p(s)$ extends beyond $s=\rho(p)$ as a straight line of $A$
defined for all real $s$.

**(iii)** With $h_{ab}=g_{ab}+W_aW_b$ the rest-space metric of the congruence
and $B_{ab}=\nabla_bW_a$, one has
$$B_{ab}=-\frac{1}{\rho}\,h_{ab},\qquad \theta=-\frac{3}{\rho},\qquad \sigma_{ab}=0,\qquad \omega_{ab}=0 .$$

**(iv)** Along the flow line through a point $p$ with
$\theta_0:=\theta(p)=-3/\rho(p)<0$ one has, for $0\le s<\rho(p)$,
$$\theta\bigl(\gamma_p(s)\bigr)=-\frac{3}{\rho(p)-s},\qquad \frac{1}{-\theta(\gamma_p(s))}=\frac{1}{-\theta_0}-\frac{s}{3}:$$
the Raychaudhuri focusing bound of
[[thm-gr-timelike-raychaudhuri-and-local-focusing]] clause (b) holds with
equality, and the congruence cannot be continued as a smooth geodesic
congruence to affine parameter $3/(-\theta_0)=\rho(p)$ or beyond.

**(v)** The spacetime is flat, the Ricci tensor vanishes identically,
every maximal geodesic of the model has domain all of $\mathbb R$, and at
$s=\rho(p)$ the flow lines merely meet at the event $e$, where the field $W$
is not defined. Thus the finite-time breakdown in (iv) is the focal crossing
of the congruence and not a singularity of the spacetime or of any individual
geodesic.

retained_claims.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous causal-curve
conclusions used here.

Let $(A,\eta,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], written $A=\mathbb R^4$,
with its global inertial chart $x=(x^0,z)=(t,z)$, and write
$e_0:=(1,0,0,0)\in A$. This example works through the explicit computations
behind [[thm-gr-minkowski-cauchy-and-global-hyperbolicity]].

**(i)** For every $c\in\mathbb R$ the level set
$\Sigma_c:=x^{-1}(\{c\}\times\mathbb R^3)$ is a spacelike embedded
hypersurface with induced metric $\delta=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1)$ in the
coordinates $(z^1,z^2,z^3)$ and future unit normal $\partial_0$
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a)).

**(ii)** The coordinate $t=x^0$ is a temporal function: its gradient in the
chart is $\nabla t=-\partial_0$, with
$\eta(\nabla t,\nabla t)=-1<0$ and $dt(\partial_0)=1>0$
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (e),
[[lem-gr-flat-time-monotonicity-and-lipschitz-graphs]] clause (d)).

**(iii)** For $\varepsilon>0$ and $p\in A$ the double cone
$$V_\varepsilon(p):=I^+\bigl(p-\varepsilon e_0\bigr)\cap I^-\bigl(p+\varepsilon e_0\bigr)$$
is open, contains $p$, and is causally convex for causal curves that meet it
twice: if a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to A$ has
$\gamma(a),\gamma(b)\in V_\varepsilon(p)$, then $\gamma(s)\in
V_\varepsilon(p)$ for every $s\in(a,b)$. In coordinates,
$$V_\varepsilon(p)=\Bigl\{q:\ |z(q)-z(p)|_{\mathrm e}<\varepsilon-\bigl|x^0(q)-x^0(p)\bigr|\Bigr\}.$$

**(iv)** For $o:=0\in A$ and $q:=Te_0$, $T>0$, the causal diamond is
$$J^+(o)\cap J^-(Te_0)=\bigl\{r:\ |z(r)|_{\mathrm e}\le x^0(r)\le T-|z(r)|_{\mathrm e}\bigr\},$$
a closed bounded subset of $\mathbb R^4$, hence compact; its $t$-sections are
closed balls of radius $\min(t,T-t)$ for $0\le t\le T$, and are empty otherwise.

**(v)** The domain of dependence of each $\Sigma_c$ is all of $A$:
$D^+(\Sigma_c)\supseteq\{t\ge c\}$, $D^-(\Sigma_c)\supseteq\{t\le c\}$ and
$D(\Sigma_c)=A$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(d)).

retained_claims.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous causal-curve
conclusions used here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the open flat slab $M=x^{-1}((0,1)\times\mathbb R^3)$ of
[[thm-gr-flat-slab-incomplete-geodesic-and-cauchy-slice]] with restricted
inertial chart $x=(x^0,z)$. Fix $z_0\in\mathbb R^3$ and let
$\gamma:(0,1)\to M$, $\gamma(s):=x^{-1}(s,z_0)$. This example records the
explicit numbers behind the incompleteness claim of that theorem:

**(i)** $\gamma$ is a smooth future timelike geodesic with affine parameter
$s$ and unit tangent $\gamma'(s)=\partial_0$; in the chart the geodesic
equation is $\ddot y=0$.

**(ii)** The affine separation and the Lorentzian length of the segment from
$s_1$ to $s_2$, $0<s_1<s_2<1$, are
$$\Delta s=s_2-s_1,\qquad L(\gamma|_{[s_1,s_2]})=\int_{s_1}^{s_2}\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}\,ds=s_2-s_1;$$
under the framework's SI length-coordinate convention
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]] clause (b), the coordinates
$x^0=s$ and the affine parameter values $s_1,s_2$ are lengths in metres,
while $c$ has units $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$; thus
$(s_2-s_1)/c$ is a duration in seconds. If $\gamma$ is also interpreted as
an ideal clock's worldline, the ideal-clock assumption of
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] clause (i) identifies that
metric-defined proper-time increment with the clock-reading difference.
This physical reading is conditional; the mathematical example alone asserts
no clock reading.

**(iii)** The maximal domain of a geodesic with the data of $\gamma$ is
exactly $(0,1)$; the image converges in the ambient affine space to the event
$x^{-1}(1,z_0)$, which does not belong to $M$. Hence $\gamma$ is
future-inextendible in $M$ with bounded affine parameter, and the slab is
timelike geodesically incomplete.

**(iv)** The slice $\Sigma_{1/2}=\{x^0=1/2\}$ is a Cauchy hypersurface and
the slab is globally hyperbolic, so the example exhibits incompleteness in a
globally hyperbolic model.

retained_claims.statement:
Let $(A,\eta,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], written $A=\mathbb R^4$,
with its global inertial chart $x=(t,z)$. Fix $T>0$ and let $e:=x^{-1}(T,0)$
be the event at coordinate time $T$ on the worldline of the origin. Let
$$O:=\bigl\{q\in A:\ T-t(q)>|z(q)|_{\mathrm e}\bigr\}$$
be the interior of the past light cone of $e$, and define
$$\rho:O\to(0,\infty),\qquad \rho(q):=\sqrt{\bigl(T-t(q)\bigr)^2-|z(q)|_{\mathrm e}^2},$$
and the vector field $W$ on $O$ whose chart components are
$$W^a(q):=\frac{e^a-q^a}{\rho(q)}\qquad(a=0,1,2,3).$$
Then:

**(i)** $W$ is a smooth future unit timelike vector field on the open set
$O$; it is a smooth future unit timelike geodesic congruence in the sense of
[[def-gr-geodesic-congruence-and-kinematics]] clause (a).

**(ii)** The maximal forward flow line of $W$ through $p\in O$ is
$$\gamma_p(s)=e-\Bigl(1-\frac{s}{\rho(p)}\Bigr)\bigl(e-p\bigr),\qquad s\in[0,\rho(p)),$$
with $\rho(\gamma_p(s))=\rho(p)-s$ and $\gamma_p(0)=p$; it reaches $e$ at
$s=\rho(p)$. The parameter $s=0$ is included as a one-sided endpoint, and
$e\notin O$ so it is excluded from the flow domain. Each affine geodesic
$s\mapsto\gamma_p(s)$ extends beyond $s=\rho(p)$ as a straight line of $A$
defined for all real $s$.

**(iii)** With $h_{ab}=g_{ab}+W_aW_b$ the rest-space metric of the congruence
and $B_{ab}=\nabla_bW_a$, one has
$$B_{ab}=-\frac{1}{\rho}\,h_{ab},\qquad \theta=-\frac{3}{\rho},\qquad \sigma_{ab}=0,\qquad \omega_{ab}=0 .$$

**(iv)** Along the flow line through a point $p$ with
$\theta_0:=\theta(p)=-3/\rho(p)<0$ one has, for $0\le s<\rho(p)$,
$$\theta\bigl(\gamma_p(s)\bigr)=-\frac{3}{\rho(p)-s},\qquad \frac{1}{-\theta(\gamma_p(s))}=\frac{1}{-\theta_0}-\frac{s}{3}:$$
the Raychaudhuri focusing bound of
[[thm-gr-timelike-raychaudhuri-and-local-focusing]] clause (b) holds with
equality, and the congruence cannot be continued as a smooth geodesic
congruence to affine parameter $3/(-\theta_0)=\rho(p)$ or beyond.

**(v)** The spacetime is flat, the Ricci tensor vanishes identically,
every maximal geodesic of the model has domain all of $\mathbb R$, and at
$s=\rho(p)$ the flow lines merely meet at the event $e$, where the field $W$
is not defined. Thus the finite-time breakdown in (iv) is the focal crossing
of the congruence and not a singularity of the spacetime or of any individual
geodesic.

items.title: Model configurations, interface readouts, operational models, data records and the analysis vocabulary of the experiment interface
items.statement:
Adopt the unit conventions of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]], the
spacetime postulate of [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and the
clock, free-fall and light-ray postulates of
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]. This definition fixes the vocabulary in
which the framework's empirical layer is stated: it names model
configurations, the readouts assigned to them, operational models, data
records, calibration declarations and declared uncertainty bounds. It selects
no experiment, records no value and asserts no comparison.

**(a) Model configurations.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth
Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). A **model
configuration** is a finite tuple $D=(d_1,\dots,d_r)$ whose entries are objects
of the following kinds, each carrying the domain, parametrization and
regularity required by the cited item:

- a *worldline entry*: a $C^1$ future timelike worldline $h:I\to M$ on an
  interval $I$ with nonempty interior, parametrized by proper time, so that its
  four-velocity $U:=h'$ satisfies $g(U,U)=-c^2$
  ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]],
  [[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]), or the
  restriction of such a worldline to a subinterval;
- an *observer entry*: an observer at a point, that is a future unit timelike
  vector $n$ with $g(n,n)=-1$, or a smooth observer congruence
  ([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]],
  [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]);
- a *ray entry*: a smooth curve $\eta:J\to M$, where $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ is
  an interval with nonempty interior, that is a future-directed null geodesic
  of $\nabla$; thus it is affinely parametrized and satisfies
  $\nabla_{\eta'}\eta'=0$, $g(\eta',\eta')=0$ and $\eta'$ is future-directed,
  with the one-sided convention at included endpoints
  ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
  [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
  [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] clause (iii));
- a *chart entry*: a smooth chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]);
- an *azimuth entry*: a continuous real function $\varphi:K\to\mathbb R$
  on a compact parameter interval $K=[t_1,t_2]$ of a worldline entry, with
  values in radians, together with the local azimuth chart designations and
  compatibility conditions specified in (b)4; this is supplied data, not an
  assertion that such a function exists;
- a *detector entry*: the data of the ideal two-body detector of the
  linearized-wave regime, namely a TT linearized-wave datum, a reference point
  $x_0$, a separation vector $\delta\ne0$ with $\delta^0=0$, the arm direction
  $e_\delta$, and a parameter value $s$, as in
  [[def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling]] clauses (a)-(c);
- a *parameter entry*: a finite tuple of real numbers in a declared subset of
  $\mathbb R^m$, each component with declared units;
- an *annotation entry*: a finite string recording declared conditions of the
  configuration and, where a datum is taken from a report, the bibliographic
  identification of that report.

A model configuration is a description of a hypothetical model situation. The
tuple asserts nothing about any apparatus and nothing about nature, and no
clause of this definition asserts that a configuration with prescribed entries
exists: existence claims belong to the items that construct the entries.

**(b) Readouts.** Let $D$ be a model configuration. The following **readouts**
are defined whenever $D$ contains the entries named in the clause together with
the stated incidence conditions; each is a real number or a finite tuple of
real numbers determined by the entries of $D$.

1. *Frequency ratio and redshift.* Suppose $D$ contains a ray entry
   $\eta:J\to M$ with tangent $W:=\eta'$, worldline entries $h_E:I_E\to M$ and
   $h_R:I_R\to M$ with four-velocities $U_E,U_R$, and parameter values
   $s_E<s_R$ in $J$, $t_E\in I_E$, $t_R\in I_R$ with $\eta(s_E)=h_E(t_E)$ and
   $\eta(s_R)=h_R(t_R)$. The **observer energies** of the ray at the two events
   relative to the unit observers $U_E/c$ and $U_R/c$ are

   $$E_E:=-c\,g_{\eta(s_E)}\bigl(W(s_E),U_E(t_E)/c\bigr),\qquad E_R:=-c\,g_{\eta(s_R)}\bigl(W(s_R),U_R(t_R)/c\bigr),$$

   the values of clause (a) of
   [[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]] for those observers; both
   are strictly positive by claim 1 of
   [[lem-gr-observer-pairing-with-future-causal-vectors]], because $W$ is
   nonzero future null and $U_E/c$, $U_R/c$ are future unit timelike. The
   **frequency-ratio readout** and the **redshift readout** are

   $$\mathcal F:=\frac{E_R}{E_E}=\frac{g_{\eta(s_R)}\bigl(W(s_R),U_R(t_R)\bigr)}{g_{\eta(s_E)}\bigl(W(s_E),U_E(t_E)\bigr)},\qquad z:=\frac{E_E}{E_R}-1=\frac1{\mathcal F}-1 .$$

2. *Radar round-trip proper time.* Suppose $D$ contains worldline entries
   $h_R:I_R\to M$ (the receiver) and $h_C:I_C\to M$ (the reflector), parameter
   values $t_1<t_2$ in $I_R$ and $s_C\in I_C$, and ray entries $\eta_1,\eta_2$
   whose parameter intervals contain values exhibiting
   $\eta_1(s_1)=h_R(t_1)$, $\eta_1(s_1')=h_C(s_C)$ with $s_1<s_1'$, and
   $\eta_2(s_2)=h_C(s_C)$, $\eta_2(s_2')=h_R(t_2)$ with $s_2<s_2'$. The
   **radar readout** is the receiver proper-time increment
   $\Delta\tau:=t_2-t_1$ between emission and reception. It is independent of
   the affine parametrizations of $\eta_1,\eta_2$, which enter only through the
   incidence statements ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]] clause
   (d), [[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]).

3. *Deflection angle.* Suppose $D$ contains a ray entry $\eta:J\to M$ with
   tangent $W$, parameter values $s_1<s_2$ in $J$, observer entries $n_1,n_2$ at
   $p_1:=\eta(s_1)$ and $p_2:=\eta(s_2)$, and an isometric identification
   $\Phi:T_{p_1}M\to T_{p_2}M$, by which is meant a linear isomorphism with
   $g_{p_2}(\Phi v,\Phi w)=g_{p_1}(v,w)$ for all $v,w\in T_{p_1}M$ and
   $\Phi(n_1)=n_2$. Put $q_i:=h_{n_i}(W(s_i))$, the spatial projection of
   clause (b) of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]], and suppose $q_1,q_2\ne0$.
   Then $|q_i|_{n_i}:=\sqrt{g_{p_i}(q_i,q_i)}>0$, because $g_{p_i}$ is positive
   definite on the rest space ([[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]),
   and $\Phi(q_1)$ lies in $n_2^{\perp}$ with
   $g_{p_2}(\Phi q_1,\Phi q_1)=g_{p_1}(q_1,q_1)$. The **deflection cosine**
   and **deflection readout** are

   $$\kappa:=\frac{g_{p_2}\bigl(\Phi(q_1),q_2\bigr)}{|q_1|_{n_1}\,|q_2|_{n_2}}\in[-1,1],\qquad \Theta:=\arccos\kappa,$$

   where the bound is the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality in the real inner product
   space $(n_2^{\perp},g_{p_2})$
   ([[def-inner-product-space]],
   [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]]) and
   $\arccos$ is the principal inverse cosine of
   [[def-principal-inverse-sine-and-cosine]].

4. *Azimuthal increment and perihelion advance.* Suppose $D$ contains a
   worldline entry $h:I\to M$, a chart entry $(U,x)$ with
   $h([t_1,t_2])\subseteq U$ for $t_1<t_2$ in $I$, and an azimuth entry
   $\varphi:[t_1,t_2]\to\mathbb R$. Put $r(t):=x^1(h(t))$ on $h^{-1}(U)\subseteq I$. Require $t_1,t_2$
   to be strict local minima of $r$ (relative to its domain in $I$), with no
   strict local minimum between them; these are the designated successive
   perihelion passages. For every $t\in[t_1,t_2]$ require a smooth chart
   $(V,y)$ containing $h(t)$, whose dimensionless coordinate $y^2$ is
   designated as a local azimuth, and a relative parameter neighborhood $J_t$
   of $t$ on which $h(J_t)\subseteq V$ and
   $\varphi(u)-y^2(h(u))\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ for every $u\in J_t$.
   Here $2\pi\mathbb Z:=\{2\pi k:k\in\mathbb Z\}$, and the designations
   specify a common angular orientation and period $2\pi$. The supplied
   continuous $\varphi$ is the **unwrapped azimuth** along this traversal;
   local azimuth representatives alone are not sufficient input. The
   **azimuthal-increment readout** and the **perihelion-advance readout** are

   $$\Delta\varphi:=\varphi(t_2)-\varphi(t_1),\qquad A:=\Delta\varphi-2\pi .$$

   This convention subtracts one positive circuit; for a negatively oriented
   traversal it still uses the displayed signed formula. The radial and
   angular designations are part of the declared configuration, not a
   dynamical prediction or a chart-invariance assertion. Adding a constant
   $2\pi k$ to the supplied lift leaves the increment unchanged. A traversal
   with $\varphi(t_2)=\varphi(t_1)+2\pi$ has $A=0$ even when its endpoint
   local azimuth representatives coincide. No lift-existence theorem is
   assumed: the readout is defined only when the required lift is supplied.

5. *Arrival times.* Suppose $D$ contains worldline entries $h_E,h_R$, a finite
   family of ray entries $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_N$ and parameter values such that
   $\eta_k$ joins an event of $h_E$ to $h_R(t_k)$, with $t_1<\cdots<t_N$ in
   $I_R$. The **arrival-time readout** is the tuple $(t_1,\dots,t_N)$ of
   receiver proper-time values.

6. *Strain.* Suppose $D$ contains a detector entry of (a) and a parameter
   value at which the quantity under the square root of clause (c) of
   [[def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling]] is positive. The
   **strain readout** is the value $S_\delta(s)$ of the strain function of that
   clause.

**(c) Operational models.** An **operational model** is a tuple
$M=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ in which $S$ is a nonempty set, the *preparation
index set*; $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is a nonempty *parameter set* whose
coordinates carry declared units; $\theta:S\to\Theta$ is a surjection, the
*parameter map*; $D$ assigns to each $s\in S$ a model configuration $D(s)$ of
(a); and for some integer $d\ge1$ a map $F:\Theta\to\mathbb R^d$ is a
**prediction map** for $D$, subject to the declared interpretation $(*)$: for
every $s\in S$, each component of $F(\theta(s))$ is a value that the
framework's definitions, postulates and proved consequences assign to a
readout of (b) of the configuration $D(s)$, with every intermediate quantity,
event, frame, sign and unit declared. In particular, a component asserted to be
a frequency ratio, redshift, radar, deflection, azimuthal, advance,
arrival-time or strain value must be the corresponding readout of (b) for
entries that the configuration contains, and a component read from a cited
prediction theorem must be a value that theorem assigns to entries of $D(s)$
satisfying its hypotheses. Condition $(*)$ is a declared interpretation that
reviewers check when the model is used; it is not a consequence of the tuple
structure, and no clause of this definition asserts that any apparatus realizes
$M$ or that any component of $F$ is measured.

**(d) Data records.** A **data record** is a tuple $R=(N,z,\varepsilon,a)$ with
an integer $N\ge1$; $z=(z_1,\dots,z_N)$ with $z_k\in\mathbb R^d$;
$\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_N)$ with
$\varepsilon_k\in[0,\infty)^d$; and $a=(a_1,\dots,a_N)$ a finite tuple of
*condition annotations* as in (a). The record declares: for each $k$, the value
of the readout under the condition annotated by $a_k$ lies in the closed box
$\prod_{j=1}^d[z_{k,j}-\varepsilon_{k,j},\,z_{k,j}+\varepsilon_{k,j}]$, in the
declared units. A data record contains no probability space, random variable,
distribution, sampling law, independence assumption, likelihood or coverage
statement; it declares nothing about how the values $z_k$ were produced and
nothing about the correctness of any calibration.

**(e) Calibration declarations.** Let $Z$ be a nonempty set of declared
*instrument-output values*. A **calibration declaration** is a tuple
$C=(Z,c,\delta,h)$ with $c:Z\to\mathbb R^d$, $\delta:Z\to[0,\infty)^d$ and $h$
a condition annotation as in (a); it declares that for every $z\in Z$ obtained
under the condition annotated by $h$, the value of the declared readout lies in
the closed box
$\prod_{j=1}^d[c_j(z)-\delta_j(z),\,c_j(z)+\delta_j(z)]$ in the declared units.
A **calibration record** is a data record of (d) whose declared readout is the
value of the calibration map's output. The declaration asserts no accuracy
beyond the bound $\delta$ and no statistical property of $c$ or $\delta$.

**(f) Uncertainty vocabulary.** For a data record of (d), the **declared
uncertainty** of the $k$-th datum is the vector $\varepsilon_k$; a **source
label** is an element of the finite declared set
$\{\text{calibration},\ \text{systematic},\ \text{sampling-variability},\
\text{rounding},\ \text{other}\}$ attached to a bound; and a **total declared
bound** for a value computed from finitely many recorded values by a declared
finite arithmetic expression is any $B\in[0,\infty)$ for which the declaration
states: whenever each recorded value lies in its declared closed box, the
computed value lies in $[\hat y-B,\hat y+B]$ for the declared number $\hat y$
(for instance, for a sum of recorded scalars the sum of the recorded bounds is
such a bound). Every uncertainty entry is a declared constraint of the form in
(d) and (e); no probability law, coverage probability, confidence level,
p-value or posterior is defined by this vocabulary.

**(g) Comparison claims are separate.** A claim that a data record $R$ and an
operational model $M$ are consistent, or that $R$ supports, refutes or fails to
distinguish $M$, is not part of (a)-(f): it requires its own statement, an
explicitly declared comparison rule, and adequate primary-report and analysis
prerequisites. A declared rule of the form "$t\in\Theta$ is consistent with the
one-point hard-bound record $R$ exactly when $F(t)$ lies in the record's closed
box", together with the resulting consistency set
$C(R,M):=\{t\in\Theta:F(t)\in\prod_{j}[z_{1,j}-\varepsilon_{1,j},\,z_{1,j}+\varepsilon_{1,j}]\}$,
is a comparison rule in this sense; it is conditional on the record's declared
bounds and on the interpretation $(*)$, and it establishes neither the truth of
a postulate nor the correctness of any apparatus. The source design's research
prerequisite labelled M20, the primary-report and analysis layer, is not
supplied by the items of this page: no reported measurement and no experiment
item occurs here. The framework's model-side prediction content for the
readouts of (b) currently consists of the restricted redshift theorems
`pthm-gr-schwarzschild-stationary-redshift` (static observers in the
Schwarzschild exterior model) and `pthm-gr-flrw-cosmological-redshift`
(comoving observers in a homogeneous cosmological model) for readout 1, and of
the ideal-detector definition `def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling`
with the response theorem `pthm-gr-plane-wave-tidal-detector-response` for
readout 6; the propagation-delay, deflection, perihelion-advance and
arrival-time readouts of 2-5 have no in-framework prediction theorem yet and
are recorded as report destinations in
`rem-gr-primary-report-research-queue`. These item names are nonlogical
status pointers; they add no premise to this definition.

**(h) Well-definedness and scope.** All components of (a)-(g) are finite tuples
of sets, maps, curves and real numbers with declared domains and units. The
constructions use no choice principle beyond those already assumed by the cited
suppliers: [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] uses countable choice
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the canonical smooth structures of tangent
bundles, and nothing here uses any further choice. No measurability,
integrability, completeness, differentiability or convergence beyond the cited
items is used; the continuous unwrapped azimuth in (b)4 is supplied explicitly. Clause (c) evaluates a prediction only at parameter values for
which the cited items supply its ingredients, and each readout of (b) is
defined only for configurations carrying the stated entries and incidence
conditions, so this definition asserts no existence of worldlines, rays,
charts, detectors or configurations. The vocabulary asserts no measurement, no
apparatus behaviour, no empirical support or refutation, no value of the
constant $c$ or of any other physical parameter, and no statistical inference.

items.title: The reciprocal ratio map $a\mapsto a_*/a$: strict decrease, inverse, and the exact preimages of points and closed intervals
items.statement:
Let $a_*>0$ be a real number and define

$$F:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty),\qquad F(a):=\frac{a_*}{a}=a_*\,a^{-1}.$$

1. **Strict decrease.** For reals $0<a_1<a_2$ one has $F(a_1)>F(a_2)$; so $F$ is
   strictly decreasing.
2. **Inverse.** $F$ is a bijection of $(0,\infty)$ onto $(0,\infty)$ with
   inverse $F^{-1}(u)=a_*/u$: that is, $F(F^{-1}(u))=u$ and
   $F^{-1}(F(a))=a$ for all $a,u>0$.
3. **Point preimages.** For every $u>0$, $F^{-1}(\{u\})=\{a_*/u\}$, and
   $F(a)=u$ holds if and only if $a=a_*/u$.
4. **Interval windows.** For reals $0<u_1\le u_2$ the preimage of the closed
   interval is

   $$F^{-1}\bigl([u_1,u_2]\bigr)=\left[\frac{a_*}{u_2},\ \frac{a_*}{u_1}\right],$$

   a nonempty closed interval contained in $(0,\infty)$, of length

   $$\frac{a_*}{u_1}-\frac{a_*}{u_2}=\frac{a_*(u_2-u_1)}{u_1u_2};$$

   the length is $0$ exactly when $u_1=u_2$ and strictly positive exactly when
   $u_1<u_2$.

items.title: Primary-report research queue for the gravitational framework: redshift, propagation delay, light deflection, perihelion advance, binary timing and interferometric strain
items.statement:
Scope-and-queue record for the empirical layer of the classical gravitational
framework, stated in the vocabulary of
[[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]].

(i) **Status of the empirical layer.** The source design of the experimental
interface reserves a definition of the observation and analysis architecture
(delivered by [[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]]) and this
primary-report research queue. No experiment item is authored in this batch and
no measured value is recorded anywhere in it. The research label M20 of the
source design, the primary-report and analysis layer, remains unsupplied:
before any experiment item can be authored on a destination, the actual primary
report must be retrieved and read in full, and the record must carry the
apparatus and preparation, the operational definitions of the measured
quantities, the calibration model, the sampling and error model, the treatment
of systematic effects, the measured values with their reported uncertainties,
and the source's own limitations. Secondary surveys and lecture notes describe
these report families and their analysis structure; they are not substitutes
for the primary reports and no number attributed to any of them is asserted
here.

(ii) **Report families.** The source design names six *primary-report search
destinations*, that is, families of published reports to retrieve and read in
full; no destination is evidence for any postulate. For each family the
in-framework model-side content that a comparison would consume is named by its
item, and the missing predictions are recorded as future obligations rather
than assumed.

1. *Redshift and clock comparisons.* Comparisons of identical frequency
   standards or clocks at rest at different locations in a gravitational field,
   including transported-clock comparisons (Will section 2.1.3; Carroll
   (7.61)-(7.62); Tong section 1.2.5). Model-side content available: the
   frequency-ratio and redshift readouts of
   [[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]] clause (b), realized for
   static observers by `pthm-gr-schwarzschild-stationary-redshift` and for
   comoving observers by `pthm-gr-flrw-cosmological-redshift`. What is still
   missing for a comparison: the apparatus, calibration, line-shape and
   statistical analysis of an actual report, as in (i).

2. *Light-propagation delay.* Measurements of the variation of round-trip
   travel times of signals passing near a massive body, analysed differentially
   against an ephemeris (Will section 4.1.2; Carroll printed p. 181). The
   interface readout is the radar readout of clause (b)2 of
   [[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]]. Model-side content: no
   in-framework prediction theorem for the round-trip delay exists in the
   library; a restricted prediction for a specified ray family and reflector
   worldline would have to be authored before any comparison.

3. *Light deflection.* Measurements of the change in angular separation of
   sources whose lines of sight pass near a massive body, by optical astrometry
   or radio interferometry, with a fitted deflection coefficient (Will section
   4.1.1; Carroll printed p. 181). The interface readout is the deflection
   readout of clause (b)3. Model-side content: no in-framework prediction
   theorem for the deflection angle of a specified ray exists; it is a future
   obligation.

4. *Perihelion advance.* Measurements of the residual precession of an
   almost-elliptical planetary orbit after the perturbations of the other
   bodies and the precession of the equinoxes have been modelled and removed,
   analysed over long astrometric baselines (Will section 4.2; Carroll
   (7.56)-(7.57)). The interface readout is the perihelion-advance readout of
   clause (b)4. Model-side content: the restricted Schwarzschild page supplies
   circular-orbit and photon-sphere predictions only
   (`pthm-gr-schwarzschild-circular-orbit-predictions`); a prediction of the
   advance of an eccentric orbit is a future obligation.

5. *Binary-system timing.* Analyses of pulse arrival-time series of
   relativistic binary pulsars, in which orbital and relativistic parameters
   are fitted to a timing model (Will section 6.1). The interface readout is
   the arrival-time readout of clause (b)5. Model-side content: the framework
   contains no binary dynamics, no gravitational-wave source model and no
   timing-model theorem; these are future obligations in a different module.

6. *Interferometric strain.* Measurements of strain by laser-interferometric
   observatories and proposals for pulsar timing arrays (Will section 7.1;
   Carroll Ch. 6; Tong sections 5.2-5.3). The interface readout is the strain
   readout of clause (b)6. Model-side content: the ideal two-body detector of
   `def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling` clause (c) and the
   response theorem `pthm-gr-plane-wave-tidal-detector-response`. What is still
   missing: a source model producing the waveform, the propagation of light in
   the instrument, readout and noise models, calibration, and a statistical
   analysis; without them no comparison is instantiable.

(iii) **Analysis obligations for every future comparison.** Each comparison
will require a declared comparison rule of clause (g) of
[[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]], an operational model whose
prediction map satisfies condition $(*)$, a data record with declared closed
bounds or separately defined source-reported estimates and scales, a declared
treatment of calibration and of the dominant systematic effects, and, for
reported data, the primary report's own sampling and error model. Agreement of
a prediction with a record tests the combined model, apparatus and analysis
assumptions; it is evidence, not a deductive proof of the model or of any
postulate.

(iv) **Qualifications any future comparison must carry.** The following are
part of the interface contract and must appear in any consuming item: (a) model
predictions are conditional on the adopted postulates and on the explicit
hypotheses of the prediction theorem; (b) observations are reported under the
source's conditions and limitations; (c) finite-sample agreement does not
establish a postulate or a model, and a finite hard-bound record does not by
itself determine a unique parameter; (d) a p-value would not be the probability
that a theory is false and a confidence level would not be a posterior
probability; (e) reported standard uncertainties are not hard bounds and carry
no coverage guarantee; (f) every conclusion inherits the calibration
dependence, systematic limitations and selection assumptions of the source.

(v) **Pointer.** The primary observations, when they are eventually recorded,
belong in experiment items with their own empirical contracts; the comparison
arithmetic belongs in a separate proved item. This remark is a queue and status
pointer only: it supplies no independent empirical conclusion and no certainty.

retained_claims.statement:
Adopt the unit conventions of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]], the
spacetime postulate of [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and the
clock, free-fall and light-ray postulates of
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]. This definition fixes the vocabulary in
which the framework's empirical layer is stated: it names model
configurations, the readouts assigned to them, operational models, data
records, calibration declarations and declared uncertainty bounds. It selects
no experiment, records no value and asserts no comparison.

**(a) Model configurations.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth
Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). A **model
configuration** is a finite tuple $D=(d_1,\dots,d_r)$ whose entries are objects
of the following kinds, each carrying the domain, parametrization and
regularity required by the cited item:

- a *worldline entry*: a $C^1$ future timelike worldline $h:I\to M$ on an
  interval $I$ with nonempty interior, parametrized by proper time, so that its
  four-velocity $U:=h'$ satisfies $g(U,U)=-c^2$
  ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]],
  [[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]), or the
  restriction of such a worldline to a subinterval;
- an *observer entry*: an observer at a point, that is a future unit timelike
  vector $n$ with $g(n,n)=-1$, or a smooth observer congruence
  ([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]],
  [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]);
- a *ray entry*: a smooth curve $\eta:J\to M$, where $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ is
  an interval with nonempty interior, that is a future-directed null geodesic
  of $\nabla$; thus it is affinely parametrized and satisfies
  $\nabla_{\eta'}\eta'=0$, $g(\eta',\eta')=0$ and $\eta'$ is future-directed,
  with the one-sided convention at included endpoints
  ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
  [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
  [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] clause (iii));
- a *chart entry*: a smooth chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]);
- an *azimuth entry*: a continuous real function $\varphi:K\to\mathbb R$
  on a compact parameter interval $K=[t_1,t_2]$ of a worldline entry, with
  values in radians, together with the local azimuth chart designations and
  compatibility conditions specified in (b)4; this is supplied data, not an
  assertion that such a function exists;
- a *detector entry*: the data of the ideal two-body detector of the
  linearized-wave regime, namely a TT linearized-wave datum, a reference point
  $x_0$, a separation vector $\delta\ne0$ with $\delta^0=0$, the arm direction
  $e_\delta$, and a parameter value $s$, as in
  [[def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling]] clauses (a)-(c);
- a *parameter entry*: a finite tuple of real numbers in a declared subset of
  $\mathbb R^m$, each component with declared units;
- an *annotation entry*: a finite string recording declared conditions of the
  configuration and, where a datum is taken from a report, the bibliographic
  identification of that report.

A model configuration is a description of a hypothetical model situation. The
tuple asserts nothing about any apparatus and nothing about nature, and no
clause of this definition asserts that a configuration with prescribed entries
exists: existence claims belong to the items that construct the entries.

**(b) Readouts.** Let $D$ be a model configuration. The following **readouts**
are defined whenever $D$ contains the entries named in the clause together with
the stated incidence conditions; each is a real number or a finite tuple of
real numbers determined by the entries of $D$.

1. *Frequency ratio and redshift.* Suppose $D$ contains a ray entry
   $\eta:J\to M$ with tangent $W:=\eta'$, worldline entries $h_E:I_E\to M$ and
   $h_R:I_R\to M$ with four-velocities $U_E,U_R$, and parameter values
   $s_E<s_R$ in $J$, $t_E\in I_E$, $t_R\in I_R$ with $\eta(s_E)=h_E(t_E)$ and
   $\eta(s_R)=h_R(t_R)$. The **observer energies** of the ray at the two events
   relative to the unit observers $U_E/c$ and $U_R/c$ are

   $$E_E:=-c\,g_{\eta(s_E)}\bigl(W(s_E),U_E(t_E)/c\bigr),\qquad E_R:=-c\,g_{\eta(s_R)}\bigl(W(s_R),U_R(t_R)/c\bigr),$$

   the values of clause (a) of
   [[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]] for those observers; both
   are strictly positive by claim 1 of
   [[lem-gr-observer-pairing-with-future-causal-vectors]], because $W$ is
   nonzero future null and $U_E/c$, $U_R/c$ are future unit timelike. The
   **frequency-ratio readout** and the **redshift readout** are

   $$\mathcal F:=\frac{E_R}{E_E}=\frac{g_{\eta(s_R)}\bigl(W(s_R),U_R(t_R)\bigr)}{g_{\eta(s_E)}\bigl(W(s_E),U_E(t_E)\bigr)},\qquad z:=\frac{E_E}{E_R}-1=\frac1{\mathcal F}-1 .$$

2. *Radar round-trip proper time.* Suppose $D$ contains worldline entries
   $h_R:I_R\to M$ (the receiver) and $h_C:I_C\to M$ (the reflector), parameter
   values $t_1<t_2$ in $I_R$ and $s_C\in I_C$, and ray entries $\eta_1,\eta_2$
   whose parameter intervals contain values exhibiting
   $\eta_1(s_1)=h_R(t_1)$, $\eta_1(s_1')=h_C(s_C)$ with $s_1<s_1'$, and
   $\eta_2(s_2)=h_C(s_C)$, $\eta_2(s_2')=h_R(t_2)$ with $s_2<s_2'$. The
   **radar readout** is the receiver proper-time increment
   $\Delta\tau:=t_2-t_1$ between emission and reception. It is independent of
   the affine parametrizations of $\eta_1,\eta_2$, which enter only through the
   incidence statements ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]] clause
   (d), [[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]).

3. *Deflection angle.* Suppose $D$ contains a ray entry $\eta:J\to M$ with
   tangent $W$, parameter values $s_1<s_2$ in $J$, observer entries $n_1,n_2$ at
   $p_1:=\eta(s_1)$ and $p_2:=\eta(s_2)$, and an isometric identification
   $\Phi:T_{p_1}M\to T_{p_2}M$, by which is meant a linear isomorphism with
   $g_{p_2}(\Phi v,\Phi w)=g_{p_1}(v,w)$ for all $v,w\in T_{p_1}M$ and
   $\Phi(n_1)=n_2$. Put $q_i:=h_{n_i}(W(s_i))$, the spatial projection of
   clause (b) of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]], and suppose $q_1,q_2\ne0$.
   Then $|q_i|_{n_i}:=\sqrt{g_{p_i}(q_i,q_i)}>0$, because $g_{p_i}$ is positive
   definite on the rest space ([[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]),
   and $\Phi(q_1)$ lies in $n_2^{\perp}$ with
   $g_{p_2}(\Phi q_1,\Phi q_1)=g_{p_1}(q_1,q_1)$. The **deflection cosine**
   and **deflection readout** are

   $$\kappa:=\frac{g_{p_2}\bigl(\Phi(q_1),q_2\bigr)}{|q_1|_{n_1}\,|q_2|_{n_2}}\in[-1,1],\qquad \Theta:=\arccos\kappa,$$

   where the bound is the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality in the real inner product
   space $(n_2^{\perp},g_{p_2})$
   ([[def-inner-product-space]],
   [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]]) and
   $\arccos$ is the principal inverse cosine of
   [[def-principal-inverse-sine-and-cosine]].

4. *Azimuthal increment and perihelion advance.* Suppose $D$ contains a
   worldline entry $h:I\to M$, a chart entry $(U,x)$ with
   $h([t_1,t_2])\subseteq U$ for $t_1<t_2$ in $I$, and an azimuth entry
   $\varphi:[t_1,t_2]\to\mathbb R$. Put $r(t):=x^1(h(t))$ on $h^{-1}(U)\subseteq I$. Require $t_1,t_2$
   to be strict local minima of $r$ (relative to its domain in $I$), with no
   strict local minimum between them; these are the designated successive
   perihelion passages. For every $t\in[t_1,t_2]$ require a smooth chart
   $(V,y)$ containing $h(t)$, whose dimensionless coordinate $y^2$ is
   designated as a local azimuth, and a relative parameter neighborhood $J_t$
   of $t$ on which $h(J_t)\subseteq V$ and
   $\varphi(u)-y^2(h(u))\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ for every $u\in J_t$.
   Here $2\pi\mathbb Z:=\{2\pi k:k\in\mathbb Z\}$, and the designations
   specify a common angular orientation and period $2\pi$. The supplied
   continuous $\varphi$ is the **unwrapped azimuth** along this traversal;
   local azimuth representatives alone are not sufficient input. The
   **azimuthal-increment readout** and the **perihelion-advance readout** are

   $$\Delta\varphi:=\varphi(t_2)-\varphi(t_1),\qquad A:=\Delta\varphi-2\pi .$$

   This convention subtracts one positive circuit; for a negatively oriented
   traversal it still uses the displayed signed formula. The radial and
   angular designations are part of the declared configuration, not a
   dynamical prediction or a chart-invariance assertion. Adding a constant
   $2\pi k$ to the supplied lift leaves the increment unchanged. A traversal
   with $\varphi(t_2)=\varphi(t_1)+2\pi$ has $A=0$ even when its endpoint
   local azimuth representatives coincide. No lift-existence theorem is
   assumed: the readout is defined only when the required lift is supplied.

5. *Arrival times.* Suppose $D$ contains worldline entries $h_E,h_R$, a finite
   family of ray entries $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_N$ and parameter values such that
   $\eta_k$ joins an event of $h_E$ to $h_R(t_k)$, with $t_1<\cdots<t_N$ in
   $I_R$. The **arrival-time readout** is the tuple $(t_1,\dots,t_N)$ of
   receiver proper-time values.

6. *Strain.* Suppose $D$ contains a detector entry of (a) and a parameter
   value at which the quantity under the square root of clause (c) of
   [[def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling]] is positive. The
   **strain readout** is the value $S_\delta(s)$ of the strain function of that
   clause.

**(c) Operational models.** An **operational model** is a tuple
$M=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ in which $S$ is a nonempty set, the *preparation
index set*; $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is a nonempty *parameter set* whose
coordinates carry declared units; $\theta:S\to\Theta$ is a surjection, the
*parameter map*; $D$ assigns to each $s\in S$ a model configuration $D(s)$ of
(a); and for some integer $d\ge1$ a map $F:\Theta\to\mathbb R^d$ is a
**prediction map** for $D$, subject to the declared interpretation $(*)$: for
every $s\in S$, each component of $F(\theta(s))$ is a value that the
framework's definitions, postulates and proved consequences assign to a
readout of (b) of the configuration $D(s)$, with every intermediate quantity,
event, frame, sign and unit declared. In particular, a component asserted to be
a frequency ratio, redshift, radar, deflection, azimuthal, advance,
arrival-time or strain value must be the corresponding readout of (b) for
entries that the configuration contains, and a component read from a cited
prediction theorem must be a value that theorem assigns to entries of $D(s)$
satisfying its hypotheses. Condition $(*)$ is a declared interpretation that
reviewers check when the model is used; it is not a consequence of the tuple
structure, and no clause of this definition asserts that any apparatus realizes
$M$ or that any component of $F$ is measured.

**(d) Data records.** A **data record** is a tuple $R=(N,z,\varepsilon,a)$ with
an integer $N\ge1$; $z=(z_1,\dots,z_N)$ with $z_k\in\mathbb R^d$;
$\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_N)$ with
$\varepsilon_k\in[0,\infty)^d$; and $a=(a_1,\dots,a_N)$ a finite tuple of
*condition annotations* as in (a). The record declares: for each $k$, the value
of the readout under the condition annotated by $a_k$ lies in the closed box
$\prod_{j=1}^d[z_{k,j}-\varepsilon_{k,j},\,z_{k,j}+\varepsilon_{k,j}]$, in the
declared units. A data record contains no probability space, random variable,
distribution, sampling law, independence assumption, likelihood or coverage
statement; it declares nothing about how the values $z_k$ were produced and
nothing about the correctness of any calibration.

**(e) Calibration declarations.** Let $Z$ be a nonempty set of declared
*instrument-output values*. A **calibration declaration** is a tuple
$C=(Z,c,\delta,h)$ with $c:Z\to\mathbb R^d$, $\delta:Z\to[0,\infty)^d$ and $h$
a condition annotation as in (a); it declares that for every $z\in Z$ obtained
under the condition annotated by $h$, the value of the declared readout lies in
the closed box
$\prod_{j=1}^d[c_j(z)-\delta_j(z),\,c_j(z)+\delta_j(z)]$ in the declared units.
A **calibration record** is a data record of (d) whose declared readout is the
value of the calibration map's output. The declaration asserts no accuracy
beyond the bound $\delta$ and no statistical property of $c$ or $\delta$.

**(f) Uncertainty vocabulary.** For a data record of (d), the **declared
uncertainty** of the $k$-th datum is the vector $\varepsilon_k$; a **source
label** is an element of the finite declared set
$\{\text{calibration},\ \text{systematic},\ \text{sampling-variability},\
\text{rounding},\ \text{other}\}$ attached to a bound; and a **total declared
bound** for a value computed from finitely many recorded values by a declared
finite arithmetic expression is any $B\in[0,\infty)$ for which the declaration
states: whenever each recorded value lies in its declared closed box, the
computed value lies in $[\hat y-B,\hat y+B]$ for the declared number $\hat y$
(for instance, for a sum of recorded scalars the sum of the recorded bounds is
such a bound). Every uncertainty entry is a declared constraint of the form in
(d) and (e); no probability law, coverage probability, confidence level,
p-value or posterior is defined by this vocabulary.

**(g) Comparison claims are separate.** A claim that a data record $R$ and an
operational model $M$ are consistent, or that $R$ supports, refutes or fails to
distinguish $M$, is not part of (a)-(f): it requires its own statement, an
explicitly declared comparison rule, and adequate primary-report and analysis
prerequisites. A declared rule of the form "$t\in\Theta$ is consistent with the
one-point hard-bound record $R$ exactly when $F(t)$ lies in the record's closed
box", together with the resulting consistency set
$C(R,M):=\{t\in\Theta:F(t)\in\prod_{j}[z_{1,j}-\varepsilon_{1,j},\,z_{1,j}+\varepsilon_{1,j}]\}$,
is a comparison rule in this sense; it is conditional on the record's declared
bounds and on the interpretation $(*)$, and it establishes neither the truth of
a postulate nor the correctness of any apparatus. The source design's research
prerequisite labelled M20, the primary-report and analysis layer, is not
supplied by the items of this page: no reported measurement and no experiment
item occurs here. The framework's model-side prediction content for the
readouts of (b) currently consists of the restricted redshift theorems
`pthm-gr-schwarzschild-stationary-redshift` (static observers in the
Schwarzschild exterior model) and `pthm-gr-flrw-cosmological-redshift`
(comoving observers in a homogeneous cosmological model) for readout 1, and of
the ideal-detector definition `def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling`
with the response theorem `pthm-gr-plane-wave-tidal-detector-response` for
readout 6; the propagation-delay, deflection, perihelion-advance and
arrival-time readouts of 2-5 have no in-framework prediction theorem yet and
are recorded as report destinations in
`rem-gr-primary-report-research-queue`. These item names are nonlogical
status pointers; they add no premise to this definition.

**(h) Well-definedness and scope.** All components of (a)-(g) are finite tuples
of sets, maps, curves and real numbers with declared domains and units. The
constructions use no choice principle beyond those already assumed by the cited
suppliers: [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] uses countable choice
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the canonical smooth structures of tangent
bundles, and nothing here uses any further choice. No measurability,
integrability, completeness, differentiability or convergence beyond the cited
items is used; the continuous unwrapped azimuth in (b)4 is supplied explicitly. Clause (c) evaluates a prediction only at parameter values for
which the cited items supply its ingredients, and each readout of (b) is
defined only for configurations carrying the stated entries and incidence
conditions, so this definition asserts no existence of worldlines, rays,
charts, detectors or configurations. The vocabulary asserts no measurement, no
apparatus behaviour, no empirical support or refutation, no value of the
constant $c$ or of any other physical parameter, and no statistical inference.

retained_claims.statement:
Let $a_*>0$ be a real number and define

$$F:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty),\qquad F(a):=\frac{a_*}{a}=a_*\,a^{-1}.$$

1. **Strict decrease.** For reals $0<a_1<a_2$ one has $F(a_1)>F(a_2)$; so $F$ is
   strictly decreasing.
2. **Inverse.** $F$ is a bijection of $(0,\infty)$ onto $(0,\infty)$ with
   inverse $F^{-1}(u)=a_*/u$: that is, $F(F^{-1}(u))=u$ and
   $F^{-1}(F(a))=a$ for all $a,u>0$.
3. **Point preimages.** For every $u>0$, $F^{-1}(\{u\})=\{a_*/u\}$, and
   $F(a)=u$ holds if and only if $a=a_*/u$.
4. **Interval windows.** For reals $0<u_1\le u_2$ the preimage of the closed
   interval is

   $$F^{-1}\bigl([u_1,u_2]\bigr)=\left[\frac{a_*}{u_2},\ \frac{a_*}{u_1}\right],$$

   a nonempty closed interval contained in $(0,\infty)$, of length

   $$\frac{a_*}{u_1}-\frac{a_*}{u_2}=\frac{a_*(u_2-u_1)}{u_1u_2};$$

   the length is $0$ exactly when $u_1=u_2$ and strictly positive exactly when
   $u_1<u_2$.

retained_claims.statement:
Scope-and-queue record for the empirical layer of the classical gravitational
framework, stated in the vocabulary of
[[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]].

(i) **Status of the empirical layer.** The source design of the experimental
interface reserves a definition of the observation and analysis architecture
(delivered by [[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]]) and this
primary-report research queue. No experiment item is authored in this batch and
no measured value is recorded anywhere in it. The research label M20 of the
source design, the primary-report and analysis layer, remains unsupplied:
before any experiment item can be authored on a destination, the actual primary
report must be retrieved and read in full, and the record must carry the
apparatus and preparation, the operational definitions of the measured
quantities, the calibration model, the sampling and error model, the treatment
of systematic effects, the measured values with their reported uncertainties,
and the source's own limitations. Secondary surveys and lecture notes describe
these report families and their analysis structure; they are not substitutes
for the primary reports and no number attributed to any of them is asserted
here.

(ii) **Report families.** The source design names six *primary-report search
destinations*, that is, families of published reports to retrieve and read in
full; no destination is evidence for any postulate. For each family the
in-framework model-side content that a comparison would consume is named by its
item, and the missing predictions are recorded as future obligations rather
than assumed.

1. *Redshift and clock comparisons.* Comparisons of identical frequency
   standards or clocks at rest at different locations in a gravitational field,
   including transported-clock comparisons (Will section 2.1.3; Carroll
   (7.61)-(7.62); Tong section 1.2.5). Model-side content available: the
   frequency-ratio and redshift readouts of
   [[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]] clause (b), realized for
   static observers by `pthm-gr-schwarzschild-stationary-redshift` and for
   comoving observers by `pthm-gr-flrw-cosmological-redshift`. What is still
   missing for a comparison: the apparatus, calibration, line-shape and
   statistical analysis of an actual report, as in (i).

2. *Light-propagation delay.* Measurements of the variation of round-trip
   travel times of signals passing near a massive body, analysed differentially
   against an ephemeris (Will section 4.1.2; Carroll printed p. 181). The
   interface readout is the radar readout of clause (b)2 of
   [[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]]. Model-side content: no
   in-framework prediction theorem for the round-trip delay exists in the
   library; a restricted prediction for a specified ray family and reflector
   worldline would have to be authored before any comparison.

3. *Light deflection.* Measurements of the change in angular separation of
   sources whose lines of sight pass near a massive body, by optical astrometry
   or radio interferometry, with a fitted deflection coefficient (Will section
   4.1.1; Carroll printed p. 181). The interface readout is the deflection
   readout of clause (b)3. Model-side content: no in-framework prediction
   theorem for the deflection angle of a specified ray exists; it is a future
   obligation.

4. *Perihelion advance.* Measurements of the residual precession of an
   almost-elliptical planetary orbit after the perturbations of the other
   bodies and the precession of the equinoxes have been modelled and removed,
   analysed over long astrometric baselines (Will section 4.2; Carroll
   (7.56)-(7.57)). The interface readout is the perihelion-advance readout of
   clause (b)4. Model-side content: the restricted Schwarzschild page supplies
   circular-orbit and photon-sphere predictions only
   (`pthm-gr-schwarzschild-circular-orbit-predictions`); a prediction of the
   advance of an eccentric orbit is a future obligation.

5. *Binary-system timing.* Analyses of pulse arrival-time series of
   relativistic binary pulsars, in which orbital and relativistic parameters
   are fitted to a timing model (Will section 6.1). The interface readout is
   the arrival-time readout of clause (b)5. Model-side content: the framework
   contains no binary dynamics, no gravitational-wave source model and no
   timing-model theorem; these are future obligations in a different module.

6. *Interferometric strain.* Measurements of strain by laser-interferometric
   observatories and proposals for pulsar timing arrays (Will section 7.1;
   Carroll Ch. 6; Tong sections 5.2-5.3). The interface readout is the strain
   readout of clause (b)6. Model-side content: the ideal two-body detector of
   `def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling` clause (c) and the
   response theorem `pthm-gr-plane-wave-tidal-detector-response`. What is still
   missing: a source model producing the waveform, the propagation of light in
   the instrument, readout and noise models, calibration, and a statistical
   analysis; without them no comparison is instantiable.

(iii) **Analysis obligations for every future comparison.** Each comparison
will require a declared comparison rule of clause (g) of
[[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]], an operational model whose
prediction map satisfies condition $(*)$, a data record with declared closed
bounds or separately defined source-reported estimates and scales, a declared
treatment of calibration and of the dominant systematic effects, and, for
reported data, the primary report's own sampling and error model. Agreement of
a prediction with a record tests the combined model, apparatus and analysis
assumptions; it is evidence, not a deductive proof of the model or of any
postulate.

(iv) **Qualifications any future comparison must carry.** The following are
part of the interface contract and must appear in any consuming item: (a) model
predictions are conditional on the adopted postulates and on the explicit
hypotheses of the prediction theorem; (b) observations are reported under the
source's conditions and limitations; (c) finite-sample agreement does not
establish a postulate or a model, and a finite hard-bound record does not by
itself determine a unique parameter; (d) a p-value would not be the probability
that a theory is false and a confidence level would not be a posterior
probability; (e) reported standard uncertainties are not hard bounds and carry
no coverage guarantee; (f) every conclusion inherits the calibration
dependence, systematic limitations and selection assumptions of the source.

(v) **Pointer.** The primary observations, when they are eventually recorded,
belong in experiment items with their own empirical contracts; the comparison
arithmetic belongs in a separate proved item. This remark is a queue and status
pointer only: it supplies no independent empirical conclusion and no certainty.
