items.title: Local well-posedness and finite-speed independence of the extension for symmetric hyperbolic systems on a coordinate neighbourhood
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the class $\mathcal S(K,R)$; for every datum $u_0\in\mathcal S(K,R)$ let $u$ be
the solution produced there on $(-T,T)$ with values in $K'$. Then:

**(a) [local existence]** For every $u_0\in\mathcal S(K,R)$ and every
$x_0\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ the solution $u$ is $C^1$ on a neighborhood of
$(0,x_0)$ in $(-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and solves $(\star)$ pointwise
there.

**(b) [finite speed / independence of the extension]** Let $\lambda_0>0$ be
determined by the coefficient bounds on a compact set containing the values of
the solutions in the following sense: for a truncated cone
$$D:=\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,\ d(x,x_0)\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$$
with $t_0<T$, $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$, lying in a single chart of $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$
in which the coordinate representation of $A^\mu$ satisfies
$\lambda\,A^0+\xi_iA^i\ge0$ for all unit $\xi$ (which holds for $\lambda$ large
enough by clause (a) of [[lem-gr-finite-speed-independence-of-extension]]),
let $u,v$ be solutions of two periodic symmetric hyperbolic systems whose
coefficient functions agree on a neighborhood of $D$ in the independent variables and on one common open state set containing both solution ranges, with
$u(0,\cdot)=v(0,\cdot)$ on the ball $\{d(x,x_0)\le\lambda t_0\}$. Then
$u=v$ on $D$.

**(c) [local uniqueness and stability]** If two classical solutions of the same
system on a common interval have values in $K$, $H^s$ norms at most $R$ and the
same initial value, they coincide; and the continuous-dependence estimate of
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] clause (b) holds
for the solutions of clause (a).

items.title: The barotropic fluid equations in enthalpy form are symmetric hyperbolic with positive principal symbol
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the enthalpy integral. Fix a smooth EOS $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an open interval $J$ satisfying $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$. Fix the integration reference in the enthalpy variable $r$ of [[def-gr-barotropic-enthalpy-variable]], and put $c_s=\sqrt{p'}$. Let $u$ be the future unit fluid velocity, $D=\nabla_u$, $\vartheta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a=\nabla_u u$ and $\Pi^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Then:

**(a)** The full fluid equations are equivalent to
$$Dr+c_s\vartheta=0,\qquad \nabla_u u^b+c_s\Pi^{ba}\partial_ar=0.$$
The fluid stress $T^{ab}=(\epsilon+p)u^au^b+pg^{ab}$ is divergence-free precisely when these fluid equations hold.

**(b)** For variations $\eta=(\delta r,\delta u)$ with $g(u,\delta u)=0$, the smooth symmetric principal bilinear form at a covector $\zeta$ is
$$Q_\zeta(\eta,\eta')=\zeta(u)\left[\delta r\delta r'+g(\delta u,\delta u')\right]+c_s\left[\delta r\zeta(\delta u')+\delta r'\zeta(\delta u)\right].$$
For every timelike covector positively evaluated on future timelike vectors, it is positive definite. In a rest orthonormal basis it has eigenvalues $\zeta(u)$ twice and $\zeta(u)\pm c_s|\zeta_\perp|$, where $\zeta=-\zeta(u)u^\flat+\zeta_\perp$. Smooth velocity coordinates turn this bilinear form into actual smooth symmetric coefficient matrices.

**(c)** Appending the harmonic reduced Einstein metric block gives a smooth coupled first-order symmetric hyperbolic family on a local open admissible state set, with zeroth-order coupling in derivatives of the first-order variables. In an initially orthogonal chart, complete fluid data are $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, or the corresponding bundle velocity $U_0=W_0(N+v_0)$, $W_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}$ in $\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$. Write the initial lapse as $\alpha_0:=\sqrt{-g^0_{00}}>0$, so orthogonality means $g^0_{0i}=0$ and $N=\alpha_0^{-1}\partial_t$. They initialize $r=r(\epsilon_0)$, $u^0=W_0/\alpha_0$ and $u^i=W_0v_0^i$. Normalization is enforced by reconstruction, and a reduced solution recovers the full fluid equations and conserved stress before imposing Einstein's unreduced equations. Every full fluid solution extracts to the same system. No vanishing-sound-speed or dust conclusion is asserted.

items.title: Symmetric hyperbolic reduction of the Einstein-scalar system and on-shell conservation
items.statement:
Fix one scalar model with smooth potential $V$ and fixed stress normalization $K_\phi$ as in [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]. On a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold its equations and stress are
$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad T_{ab}=K_\phi\left[\partial_a\varphi\partial_b\varphi-g_{ab}\left(\tfrac12g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\partial_d\varphi+V(\varphi)\right)\right].$$
Fix a chart and a smooth background $\bar g$ for the reduced Einstein equation of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. On the open state set where $g^{00}<0$ and $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite, the reduced Einstein equation coupled to this scalar equation has a smooth first-order symmetric hyperbolic reduction with variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},\varphi,P=\partial_0\varphi,Q_i=\partial_i\varphi).$$
The time matrix is block diagonal with metric block $\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ and scalar block $\operatorname{diag}(1,-g^{00},g^{ij})$. Matter and metric cross-coupling is zeroth order in derivatives of $z$. The partial-derivative metric variables and the background-covariant ones are related by an invertible smooth zeroth-order change of variables; either gives the reduction.

For complete initial scalar data $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ in an initially orthogonal chart with $\partial_0=n$, prescribe $(\varphi,P,Q_i)=(\varphi_0,\pi_0,\partial_i\varphi_0)$. The auxiliary constraints propagate, the reconstructed scalar solves its full equation on the reduced metric, and its stress is conserved there before imposing the unreduced Einstein equation. Conversely every smooth physical scalar solution extracts to the same system. No potential positivity or mass sign is required; local arguments do not require a global orientation.

items.title: Propagation of the harmonic gauge and of the Einstein constraints: a constrained reduced solution is an Einstein solution
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), carrying the hypotheses of the analytic suppliers used below.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike hypersurface
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]) with future unit normal
field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential frame $(e_i)$
([[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$U$ be an open neighborhood of $\Sigma$ carrying a smooth background metric
$\bar g$ and a smooth symmetric tensor $T$ with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$. Let
$H$ and $E$ be the gauge vector and Einstein residual of
[[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Suppose:

1. $(g,T)$ solves the reduced Einstein equation on $U$;
2. $H=0$ on $\Sigma$;
3. the constraint residuals vanish on $\Sigma$: $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)=0$
   and $E(\mathfrak n,e_i)=0$ for all $i$.

Then there is an open neighborhood $W\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma$ on which $H=0$ and
$E=0$; consequently $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ on $W$, so $g$ solves
the Einstein equation with the prescribed matter tensor there.

items.title: Local existence for the reduced Einstein equation from Cauchy data on a spacelike slice
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), carrying the hypotheses of the analytic suppliers used below.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold carrying a chart $(x^0=t,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ whose
domain $U$ contains the slice $\Sigma:=\{t=0\}$, let $\bar g$ be a smooth
background metric on $U$ with its Levi--Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $U$ together with the
background-covariant derivatives needed below (the matter field data). Suppose
smooth functions $g^0_{ab},g^1_{ab}$ on $\Sigma\cap U$ are given such that:

1. $g^0$ is a smooth field of Lorentzian bilinear forms on the restricted
   spacetime tangent bundle $TM|_{\Sigma\cap U}$, whose restriction to
   $T\Sigma$ is positive definite. Write $g^0_{ab}$ for its components in the
   given spacetime chart; its inverse components satisfy $g^{00}_0<0$ and the
   spatial block $(g_0^{ij})$ is positive definite;
2. $g^1_{ab}$ is symmetric and agrees on $\Sigma$ with the components of
   $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$ for some smooth extension $g$ of $g^0$ to $U$;
3. the harmonic-gauge condition $H^a=0$ holds on $\Sigma\cap U$ for the pair
   $(g,\bar g)$ ([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]).

Then there is an open neighborhood $V\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma\cap U$ and a smooth
metric $g$ on $V$ with $g|_{\Sigma\cap U}=g^0$ and
$\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}|_{\Sigma\cap U}=g^1_{ab}$, solving the **reduced Einstein
equation** with the given background $\bar g$ and matter tensor $T$
([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]) on $V$.

Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 5.1 (Local Existence Theorems for the Einstein Equations): harmonic-map gauge, the reduced initial data constructed from (h,chi), the propagation of the gauge by the homogeneous wave system for the gauge residual Delta^alpha, and the local existence theorem

H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 3.1 (Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems): the definition of a quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system, the finite-dimensional mollifier approximation (3.1) solved by ODE theory, the energy and Moser product/composition estimates, the higher-order energy inequality, uniqueness, the Rellich/Ascoli compactness step and the passage to a classical solution, with Remarks 1-6 on smooth persistence, the continuation criterion, Cauchy stability and the non-identity time matrix

items.title: Local geometric uniqueness for a fixed covariant Einstein-matter model with complete data
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth tensor fields $\Psi$, specified equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$, and a specified stress expression $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Covariance means pullback by a local diffeomorphism commutes with these equations and stress expression. Fix complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$ for this model, a smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric tensor $K$ on a smooth three-manifold $\Sigma$, with $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal.

The following explicit harmonic-reduction hypothesis is required. On each relatively compact initial coordinate ball, with flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, specify finite first-order variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w),$$
fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules for $w,\Psi$, and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$, shared by both solutions, such that:

**(R1)** Every smooth solution of this same model written in harmonic coordinates has extracted variables satisfying
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_iA^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
where all $A^\mu$ are symmetric and $A^0$ is positive definite. Reconstruction recovers all matter fields and $T$ from $z$. Any internal matter gauge has already been fixed with its specified data and equations; otherwise the conclusion must include the appropriate internal gauge equivalence.
**(R2)** The initial value of $w$ is a specified smooth expression $\mathcal I(h,K,d)$ in the full data in this coordinate gauge. Thus $d$ determines every initial first-order variable, not merely initial stress tensor jets.
**(R3)** After shrinking a closed cylinder, both state ranges lie in one compact convex subset of $O$, coefficient first derivatives are bounded and $A^0\ge aI$ for some $a>0$.

These are PDE and extraction hypotheses, not an assumption of geometric uniqueness. Let $(M,g,\Psi,j)$ and $(M',g',\Psi',j')$ be two smooth time-oriented developments of this same model, solving the same Einstein equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$ and the same matter equations, whose spacelike embeddings induce $(h,K,d)$. Then near each initial point there is a smooth time-orientation-preserving isometry $\Phi$ with $\Phi\circ j=j'$ on the initial patch, $\Phi^*\Psi'=\Psi$ and consequently $\Phi^*T'=T$. Its germ along the initial patch is unique. These germs glue to one such isometry between open neighborhoods of the entire embedded initial surfaces. No uniform collar width or global-in-time assertion is made.

references.title: Friedrich and Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, sections 3.1-3.2, 5.1-5.2 and 5.4

items.title: Local geometric development for a fixed covariant Einstein-matter model with complete constrained data
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth fields $\Psi$, equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ and stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Pullback by local diffeomorphisms commutes with these equations and stress expression. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$. The sign convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Initial matter tensors involving normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, rather than on a pre-existing spacetime.

Require the following explicit reduction hypotheses on each sufficiently small relatively compact initial coordinate ball with labels $x^i$, flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, and finite variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w).$$

1. There are fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$ giving a system
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_i A^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
with symmetric $A^\mu$ and positive definite $A^0$. Its metric equations are exactly the first-order reduction of the reduced Einstein equations of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], with stress $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Every smooth physical solution of this fixed model in harmonic coordinates extracts to this same system. Any internal matter gauge is already fixed with its specified equations and complete data; otherwise state the corresponding internal gauge equivalence in the conclusion.
2. Complete data determine a smooth initial value $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$, including all auxiliary variables and their compatibility constraints. The initial metric jet displayed in step 1.1 and this value lie in $O$. The reduction propagates its auxiliary compatibility constraints, so the reconstructed fields solve $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ on the reduced solution, before imposing $H=0$ or the unreduced Einstein equations. The initial reconstruction induces exactly $d$ and the specified initial stress.
3. Whenever the reconstructed metric and fields satisfy those matter equations, their stress obeys $\nabla^a\mathcal T(g,\Psi)_{ab}=0$, independently of the unreduced Einstein equations. In particular this applies to the reduced solution furnished by clause 2. This is stronger than conservation asserted only after the full coupled equations have been proved.

These are concrete PDE, initialization and reconstruction hypotheses; they do not assume existence or geometric uniqueness. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the stress determined by $(h,K,d)$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(N,N),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(N,\cdot).$$

Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local development $(g,\Psi)$ on an open variable-width neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in the literal manifold $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$, with induced data $(h,K,d)$, solving
$$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi),\qquad\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0.$$
After restriction to a smaller collar, $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence. The interior of that domain is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and these complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching all matter fields. There is no uniform noncompact time width or global-in-time conclusion.

references.title: Friedrich and Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, sections 3.1-3.2, 5.1-5.2 and 5.4

items.title: Local evolution for a strict barotropic perfect fluid: smooth constrained data admit a development, unique up to a data-fixing isometry
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and one smooth EOS $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an open interval $J$ with $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth metric $h$, symmetric tensor $K_2$, density $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and tangent field $v_0$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$. These specify the future unit initial velocity
$$U_0=W_0(N+v_0),\qquad W_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}$$
in $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for
$$T_0=(\epsilon_0+p(\epsilon_0))U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}+p(\epsilon_0)g_0.$$
Then a smooth time-oriented local development has metric $g$, density $\epsilon$ and future unit fluid velocity $u$ satisfying
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\left[(\epsilon+p)u_au_b+pg_{ab}\right],\qquad D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\epsilon+p)a^b+\Pi^{ba}\partial_ap=0.$$
Here $D=\nabla_u$, $\vartheta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a=\nabla_u u$ and $\Pi^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$. Initial geometric data are $(h,K_2)$ and initial matter data are $(\epsilon_0,U_0)$ under $N\mapsto n$, $X\mapsto i_*X$. Arbitrary smooth subluminal tilt is allowed. The initial surface lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence; its interior Cauchy neighborhood is globally hyperbolic. Any two developments of this same EOS and complete data agree near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing future isometry matching density and velocity. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; shocks, vacuum boundaries and vanishing sound speed are outside this strict interior-fluid statement ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]).

Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 4.2 (The Einstein-Euler System): the hyperbolic reduction of the Einstein-Euler system, the positivity conditions on specific enthalpy and speed of sound (4.38), the frame variables and their reduced equations, and the pressure-free (dust) subsidiary system of Sections 4.2.4-4.2.5, equations (4.26)-(4.48) and (4.56)-(4.63)

Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 5.1 (Local Existence Theorems for the Einstein Equations): harmonic-map gauge, the reduced initial data constructed from (h,chi), the propagation of the gauge by the homogeneous wave system for the gauge residual Delta^alpha, and the local existence theorem

items.title: Local Einstein-dust evolution: smooth constrained data with prescribed velocity admit a smooth local development, unique up to a data-fixing isometry
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix constants $c>0$, $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and a smooth mass-normalized density $\rho_0\ge0$. Specify initial velocity as a smooth section $U_0$ of $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with the bundle metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, satisfying $g_0(U_0,U_0)=-1$ and positive $N$ coefficient. Thus the velocity need not be normal and does not presuppose a spacetime development. Put $\varepsilon_0=\rho_0c^2$ and require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for $T_0=\varepsilon_0U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}$. On $\{\rho_0>0\}$ this is exactly the dust supplier with density parameter $\varepsilon_0$, rather than $\rho_0$ ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); zero regions have independently prescribed velocity.

Then there is a smooth local development: a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian metric $g$, density $\rho\ge0$ and future unit timelike field $u$ near an embedded copy of $\Sigma$, solving
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\rho c^2u_au_b,\qquad \nabla_uu=0,\qquad u(\rho)+\rho\nabla\!\cdot u=0.$$
The induced geometric and matter data are $(h,K,\rho_0,U_0)$, with $\mathcal V$ identified by $aN+X\mapsto an+i_*X$ using the future unit normal $n$. The initial surface lies in the interior of its domain of dependence; restriction to its Cauchy neighborhood gives a local Cauchy development. Every two such developments agree near $\Sigma$ by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching $\rho,u$. No division by density is used, so smooth empty regions are admitted. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; no uniform noncompact slab or continuation past flow crossings is asserted.

Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 4.2 (The Einstein-Euler System): the hyperbolic reduction of the Einstein-Euler system, the positivity conditions on specific enthalpy and speed of sound (4.38), the frame variables and their reduced equations, and the pressure-free (dust) subsidiary system of Sections 4.2.4-4.2.5, equations (4.26)-(4.48) and (4.56)-(4.63)

H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 5.1 (Local Existence Theorems for the Einstein Equations): harmonic-map gauge, the reduced initial data constructed from (h,chi), the propagation of the gauge by the homogeneous wave system for the gauge residual Delta^alpha, and the local existence theorem

items.title: Local Einstein-scalar evolution: smooth constrained data admit a local development, unique up to a data-fixing isometry
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and one scalar model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ of [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]], with its fixed smooth potential and normalization. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric tensor $K_2$ and complete scalar data $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$. Suppose the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] hold for the scalar stress computed from these data, with $\pi_0$ the prescribed future-normal derivative. Then there is a smooth local Einstein-scalar development
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab},\qquad \Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,$$
with induced geometric data $(h,K_2)$, $\varphi|_\Sigma=\varphi_0$ and $n(\varphi)|_\Sigma=\pi_0$. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width. The initial surface is interior to its intrinsic domain of dependence; restricting to the interior Cauchy neighborhood gives a globally hyperbolic development. Every two developments of this same fixed model and complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching $\varphi$. No potential positivity, mass sign, global existence or uniform noncompact slab is asserted ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]).

Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 5.4 (Matter Models): the conditions defining a matter model and the treatment of scalar-field matter coupled to the Einstein equations

items.title: High-regularity local developments for the selected matter sectors: vacuum with Lambda, scalar, strict barotropic fluid and geodesic dust
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]).

Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and $c>0$ be constants, let $\Sigma$ be a smooth
three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and symmetric $2$-tensor $K$,
and suppose smooth matter initial data and a matter sector are given in one of
the following four branches, with the constraint equations of
[[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] satisfied:

1. **vacuum with cosmological constant:** no matter fields; the constraints
   read $S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda$ and
   $\operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=0$;
2. **scalar field:** a model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ as in
   [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] with smooth potential and initial data
   $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$;
3. **strict barotropic perfect fluid:** a model with smooth $p=p(\epsilon)$ and
   $\epsilon+p>0$, $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$, with initial data
   $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, equivalently the abstract bundle velocity $U_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}(N+v_0)$, as specified in [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]];
4. **geodesic dust:** an energy-coefficient density $\varepsilon_0\ge0$
   with prescribed smooth future unit velocity $U_0$, as a section of
   $\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$ with metric $-ab+h(X,Y)$.
   On positive-density regions this is the model $(\varepsilon,u)$ of
   [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]; through zero-density regions its smooth
   unit velocity is separately prescribed and required to remain geodesic.
   Its source is $T=\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat$.

Then in each branch there is a smooth local development with the properties
established in the corresponding item, [[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]]
(branch 2), [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]] (branch 3),
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] (branch 4) and, for branch 1, the vacuum
instance of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a smooth Lorentzian metric
$g$ with $\Sigma$ spacelike of induced data $(h,K)$, solving
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ with the branch's stress tensor and matter
equations, with $\Sigma$ in the interior of its domain of dependence, and with
uniqueness near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry.

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 4.2 (The Einstein-Euler System): the hyperbolic reduction of the Einstein-Euler system, the positivity conditions on specific enthalpy and speed of sound (4.38), the frame variables and their reduced equations, and the pressure-free (dust) subsidiary system of Sections 4.2.4-4.2.5, equations (4.26)-(4.48) and (4.56)-(4.63)

H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 5.1 (Local Existence Theorems for the Einstein Equations): harmonic-map gauge, the reduced initial data constructed from (h,chi), the propagation of the gauge by the homogeneous wave system for the gauge residual Delta^alpha, and the local existence theorem

items.title: Local Cauchy development of the adopted Einstein field law for smooth constrained data in the selected matter sectors
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]).

Adopt the direct-equation presentation of the classical gravitational framework
for a model satisfying the spacetime and classical-domain postulate
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and the field-and-matter postulate
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], with the field law
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]]: on the matter domain of the model,
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab},\qquad \kappa=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4},$$
with $T$ the stress-energy tensor of the model's selected matter sector. Let the
sector be one of:

1. vacuum with cosmological constant ($T=0$);
2. the scalar-field model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ of [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]
   with a chosen smooth potential whose scalar equation and stress tensor are
   those defined there, writing $K_\phi$ for that definition's scalar normalization constant;
3. the perfect-fluid model of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]] with a
   smooth barotropic equation of state satisfying $\epsilon+p>0$ and
   $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ on the range of the data;
4. an energy-coefficient dust density $\varepsilon\ge0$ and prescribed
   smooth future unit velocity, with $T=\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat$.
   On positive-density regions this is [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]];
   on zero-density regions the velocity is separately prescribed and the
   geodesic equation remains imposed. Equivalently the mass-normalized
   density is $\rho=\varepsilon/c^2$.

Use the SI and coordinate conventions of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]: in a length-coordinate chart
$x^0=ct$, the metric is dimensionless, $[c]=\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, $[\Lambda]=\mathrm m^{-2}$,
$[G_N]=\mathrm m^3\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^{-2}$, and
$[\kappa]=\mathrm m^{-1}\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^2$, so $\kappa T$
has curvature units. Every velocity denoted $u$ in this theorem is normalized
by $g(u,u)=-1$. Its SI proper-time four-velocity is $U_{\rm SI}=cu$, with
$g(U_{\rm SI},U_{\rm SI})=-c^2$; the initial $U_0$ in the mathematical bundle
formulation is normalized, and its SI counterpart is $cU_0$. The mass-normalized density is $\rho=\rho_{\rm mass}:=\varepsilon/c^2$ with
units $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. The dust source uses
$\varepsilon=\rho_{\rm mass}c^2$ and
$\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat=\rho_{\rm mass}U_{\rm SI}^\flat\otimes
U_{\rm SI}^\flat$; fluid $\epsilon$ and $p$ have units
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $p'$ is dimensionless. For the scalar branch
choose an arbitrary field unit $\Phi$ and use $[\varphi]=\Phi$,
$[V]=\Phi^2\,\mathrm m^{-2}$, and $[K_\phi]=\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-1}\,\Phi^{-2}$;
then $\Box_g\varphi$ and $V'(\varphi)$ have units $\Phi\,\mathrm m^{-2}$ and
$T_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$.

Let $(\Sigma,h,K)$ with the sector's smooth initial data (respectively nothing,
$(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$, $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$, $(\varepsilon_0,U_0)$) satisfy the constraint
equations [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the sector's
stress tensor. Here fluid $v_0\in\Gamma(T\Sigma)$ obeys $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, with full initial unit velocity $U_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}(N+v_0)$ in $\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, exactly as in [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]]. Then the model admits a **local Cauchy development**: there are
a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of the framework and
a spacelike embedded image of $\Sigma$ inducing $(h,K)$ and the stated matter
data, solving the field law $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ and the
sector's matter equations on a neighborhood of $\Sigma$; $\Sigma$ lies in the
interior of its domain of dependence; and any two such developments of the same
data agree near $\Sigma$ up to an isometry fixing the data and the time
orientation. The development is local in time and no uniform-in-the-data
existence time or global statement is asserted.
items.physical_scope: Classical general relativity in the smooth high-regularity branch: four-dimensional smooth Lorentzian geometry of signature (-+++), cosmological constant Lambda, and one of the classical matter sectors — vacuum, a scalar field with smooth potential, a strict barotropic perfect fluid with 0<p'<1, or geodesic dust — with smooth constrained initial data; the conclusion is a local-in-time development before any flow crossing. It makes no statement about nature, global or all-time existence, nonsmooth or distributional sources, shocks, free-boundary or junction behavior, asymptotic regimes, or an optimal Sobolev threshold. Smooth zero sets and empty regions are included in the dust branch with its separately prescribed smooth geodesic velocity.

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 5.1 (Local Existence Theorems for the Einstein Equations): harmonic-map gauge, the reduced initial data constructed from (h,chi), the propagation of the gauge by the homogeneous wave system for the gauge residual Delta^alpha, and the local existence theorem

H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 5.2 (Uniqueness): geometric uniqueness up to diffeomorphism, proved by putting two developments into the same harmonic-map gauge and invoking the uniqueness theorem for the reduced symmetric hyperbolic system

items.title: Scope and status of the Gr14 high-regularity symmetric hyperbolic material
items.statement:
This page contains the Gr14 high-regularity symmetric hyperbolic proof material:
the periodic first-order theory (E0), the harmonic-gauge reduced Einstein
equation and its subsidiary system (E1), the geometric data and local
development theorems (E2), and the selected matter reductions with the complete
geodesic-dust residual chain (E3, E3d--E3d.2). Its content assumes Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for local analytic extraction and manifold patching, and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]) for the causal-curve calculus in the Cauchy-neighborhood argument. Its physical content is conditional:
the physical reading is the model deduction of
[[pthm-gr-high-regularity-local-development]] from the adopted postulates
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] and the matter definitions
[[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]], [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]],
[[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]; the mathematical carriers are
[[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]] and its prerequisites.

**What is established.** Local-in-time smooth developments of the adopted field
law with the selected matter sectors, from smooth constrained data, with
uniqueness near the initial surface up to a data-fixing time-orientation-
preserving isometry, and with the initial surface lying in the interior of its
domain of dependence.

**What is not established or assumed away.** No global or all-time existence,
no uniform existence time on noncompact data, and no maximality or boundary
behaviour of the spacetime development (that is the scope of the successor
page). The matter results do not treat shocks, nonsmooth free boundaries,
nonsmooth vacuum interfaces, junction conditions, distributional or
low-regularity sources, or boundary layers; the theorem works in the
smooth/high-regularity branch with $s\ge5$ and makes no optimal Sobolev
threshold claim. These exclusions are distinct from smooth zeros of the dust
density. For dust, the construction occurs before flow crossings and a smooth
future unit velocity is prescribed and remains geodesic even where the smooth
nonnegative energy coefficient $\varepsilon$ vanishes. Thus smooth zero sets
and open empty regions are included, with no division by density. The source
density parameter is $\varepsilon$, with mass-normalized
$\rho_{\rm mass}=\varepsilon/c^2$ for every $c>0$; in the reduction notation
$r=\varepsilon$ solves $\partial_sr=-r\chi$ with the explicit exponential
solution of [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]]. For the fluid branch the strict
hypotheses $\epsilon+p>0$, $0<p'<1$ are essential; the failure at negative
$p'$ is the companion counterexample on the examples page. No statement is
made that any model here describes nature, and no empirical premise enters.

**Conventions and sources.** The reduction uses $\gamma=-g$ and the explicit Schouten normalization and curvature decomposition of its definition. Vacuum reduction signs therefore differ from the original metric signs by that constant flip. The physical unit convention, including the distinction between the normalized velocity $u$ with $g(u,u)=-1$ and the SI proper-time four-velocity $U_{\rm SI}=cu$ with $g(U_{\rm SI},U_{\rm SI})=-c^2$, and the selected scalar, fluid and dust units are stated in [[pthm-gr-high-regularity-local-development]]. The local dust proof derives the electric/magnetic projections and the Cartan subsidiary system in those conventions; its magnetic double-epsilon term has the sign required by trace preservation. Friedrich and Rendall supplies derivation provenance; the displayed local arguments carry the deductions.
items.physical_scope: Classical general relativity in the smooth high-regularity branch with the selected matter sectors (vacuum with Lambda, scalar field, strict barotropic perfect fluid, geodesic dust) and smooth constrained initial data; purely conditional local-in-time model statements with no empirical content.

Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 5.1 (Local Existence Theorems for the Einstein Equations): harmonic-map gauge, the reduced initial data constructed from (h,chi), the propagation of the gauge by the homogeneous wave system for the gauge residual Delta^alpha, and the local existence theorem

H. Friedrich and A. D. retained_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the quotient, product-measure and integration
clauses below, as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]].

**(a) The 2 pi-periodic torus.** Let $\mathbb T_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$
carry the quotient topology, and let
$$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$$
with the product topology; write $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ for the
quotient map and $[x]:=(x^1+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^2+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^3+2\pi\mathbb Z)$.
The map $[0,2\pi)^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $x\mapsto[x]$, is a bijection. The
normalized product measure $\mu$ is $\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}$,
where $\mu_{\mathbb T}$ is the normalized measure of
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]] transported by
$t\mapsto2\pi t$; it is a probability measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and $\int f\,d\mu=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}f\circ q\,d\lambda_3$
for bounded measurable $f$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

**(b) Test functions and continuous classes.** For $N\ge1$ let
$C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of maps
$u:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^N$ whose pullbacks
$\widetilde u:=u\circ q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$ are smooth;
these are the **smooth test functions** (real-valued when $N=1$).
Equivalently every smooth map $\widetilde u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$
that is $2\pi$-periodic in each coordinate descends to the unique map
$u([x])=\widetilde u(x)$, since periodicity makes this value independent of
$x$ in its equivalence class. For an integer $m\ge0$, define
$C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ similarly by requiring
$\widetilde u\in C^m(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^N)$
([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]), and define
$D^\alpha u([x]):=D^\alpha\widetilde u(x)$ for $|\alpha|\le m$.
Derivatives of a periodic $C^m$ map are periodic, so these values are
well-defined, with
$$\|u\|_{C^m}:=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\ \sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}|(D^\alpha u)(x)|,$$
where the multi-index derivative is that of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]].

**(c) The Hilbert space $L^2$.** For $N\ge1$ let
$L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the quotient of the set of measurable
$u$ with $\int|u|^2\,d\mu<\infty$ by the $\mu$-a.e. zero functions
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]),
with inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int u\cdot v\,d\mu$ and norm
$\|u\|_2=\langle u,u\rangle_2^{1/2}$; it is a real Hilbert space
([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when their representatives $F(t,q(x),u)=G(t,x,u)$ have
$G\in C^\infty$. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), carrying the hypotheses of the analytic suppliers used below.

Let $T>0$, let $A^\mu:(-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
($\mu=0,1,2,3$) be smooth with $A^0(t,x)\ge aI$ for some constant $a>0$ and all
$(t,x)$, and let $\|A^i(t,x)\|\le b$ for the operator norm and all $i,t,x$. Let
$C:(-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3\to M_m(\mathbb R)$ be smooth and bounded by $K$.

**(a)** Put $\lambda:=\sqrt3\,b/a+1$; then $\lambda A^0(t,x)+\xi_iA^i(t,x)\ge0$ as a
quadratic form for every $(t,x)$ and every $\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ with
$|\xi|\le1$.

**(b)** Let $w\in C^1((-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ solve
$$A^0\partial_tw+A^i\partial_iw+Cw=0 ,$$
and let $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, $0<t_0<T$, and suppose $w(0,x)=0$ for every
$|x-x_0|\le\lambda t_0$. Then $w(t,x)=0$ for every
$(t,x)\in\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,\ |x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$.

**(c)** [independence of the extension] If $w_1,w_2$ are two solutions of two
such systems whose complete coefficient families, including $C$, agree on an open set containing the
truncated cone $D=\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,|x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$, and if
$w_1(0,x)=w_2(0,x)$ for $|x-x_0|\le\lambda t_0$, then $w_1=w_2$ on $D$.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero
$z\in\mathbb R^m$ with the standard coordinate inner product.

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in
particular $\|B^{-1}z\|\le a^{-1}\|z\|$.

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let
$B:\Lambda\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be continuous with $B(\lambda)$
positive definite for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then there are constants
$0<a\le b$ with $aI\le B(\lambda)\le bI$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$.

**(d)** Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ be open and let $B:D\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
be smooth with $B(x)\ge aI$ for a constant $a>0$ and all $x\in D$. Then
$x\mapsto B(x)^{-1}$ is smooth on $D$ and $B(x)^{-1}\le a^{-1}I$ there.
retained_claims.authority: unchanged canonical row and existing published carrier

retained_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $X_0$ be a complete normed space over
$\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ ([[def-banach-space]],
[[def-complete-metric-space]]) and let $X_1\subseteq X_0$ be a linear subspace
carrying a norm $\|\cdot\|_1$ such that ([[def-normed-subspace]]):

**(i)** there is $\kappa\ge0$ with $\|x\|_0\le\kappa\|x\|_1$ for every
$x\in X_1$; and

**(ii)** every sequence in $X_1$ bounded in $\|\cdot\|_1$ has a subsequence
converging in $X_0$ ([[def-metric-convergence]]).

Let $T>0$, $R\ge0$, $C\ge0$, and for $j\in\mathbb N$ let
$f_j:(-T,T)\to X_1$ satisfy
$$\|f_j(t)\|_1\le R,\qquad \|f_j(t)-f_j(t')\|_0\le C\,|t-t'|\qquad(t,t'\in(-T,T),\ j\in\mathbb N).$$

Then there are a strictly increasing sequence $j_1<j_2<\cdots$ in $\mathbb N$
and a continuous map $f:(-T,T)\to X_0$ ([[def-continuous-map-top]]) such that
$f_{j_n}\to f$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$; moreover
$\|f(t)-f(t')\|_0\le C\,|t-t'|$ for all $t,t'\in(-T,T)$.
